h1: Free Roofing Invoice Template & Example
subtitle: How to invoice roof replacements and repairs in squares, with tear-off, materials, flashing and disposal on separate lines, so homeowners and insurance adjusters can follow every number.
intro_paragraph: A roof is one of the largest bills a homeowner ever pays, and often an insurance company reads the invoice too. That makes clarity your best sales tool. A roofing invoice that speaks in squares, names every material and separates tear-off from installation gets approved and paid; a lump sum gets questioned.
what_to_include_intro: Roofing invoices are read by homeowners, adjusters and sometimes mortgage lenders. These fields make yours easy for all three.
req_1_text: Bill roofing by the square (100 square feet) and state how many squares the roof measured, plus the waste factor on materials. It's the unit adjusters use, so their estimate and your invoice can be compared line by line.
req_2_text: Removing the old roof is its own job with its own price, especially with more than one layer. Separate lines for tear-off and installation also make it obvious if an extra layer was found once the work started.
req_3_text: Shingle type and brand, underlayment, ice and water shield, drip edge, flashing, vents and ridge cap. Named materials prove you used what you quoted, and they're needed for the manufacturer's warranty registration.
req_4_text: Rotten decking is only visible after tear-off. Agree a price per sheet in the contract and invoice the number of sheets replaced as a separate line, with photos, so the extra cost is documented, not argued.
req_5_text: Dumpster, haul-away and landfill fees, plus the permit if your area needs one. These are real costs that homeowners forget, so name them instead of spreading them over other lines.
req_6_text: State your workmanship warranty (years and what it covers) and that the manufacturer's material warranty applies separately. Homeowners selling the house later will look for exactly this line.
what_to_include_outro: An invoice built like this is also your best defense if a claim or a complaint ever comes back: it records what was found, what was replaced and what was promised.
sample_breakdown_intro: A full replacement of a 24-square asphalt roof (26 squares of shingles with waste). The homeowner paid a $3,000 deposit when signing. Material prices include sales tax in this example.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Ice and water shield, eaves and valleys
Drip edge, step flashing and ridge vent

sample_breakdown_notes: No decking replacement needed. 10-year workmanship warranty; manufacturer's shingle warranty registered separately. Permit #R-2026-118. Balance due on completion. License #RC-XXXXX, insured.

industry_notes.title: Insurance claims
industry_notes.text: On storm jobs the insurer pays based on its own estimate, often in two parts (the actual cash value first, the rest after the work is done). Use the adjuster's line descriptions where you can, keep the claim number in the notes and invoice the homeowner for their deductible separately.

industry_notes.title: Deposits and material orders
industry_notes.text: Most roofers take a deposit to order materials. Show it as received on the final invoice. Some states limit deposits on home improvement contracts, so check your local rule.

industry_notes.title: Repairs versus replacements
industry_notes.text: For small repairs a flat price ('Replace 12 shingles and reseal pipe boot') is clearer than squares. Add a photo of the damaged area to the message you send with the invoice.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes roofers make on invoices

mistakes.title: Lump-sum pricing
mistakes.text: 'Roof replacement: $10,617' gives an adjuster nothing to approve and a homeowner nothing to check. Squares and named materials do.

mistakes.title: Undocumented extras
mistakes.text: Extra decking or a second layer without photos and a per-unit price from the contract becomes a negotiation. With both, it's just another line.

mistakes.title: No warranty line
mistakes.text: Homeowners keep roofing invoices for years. If the warranty isn't on it, you'll be explaining it again when they sell the house.

pro_tip: Measure and photograph the roof before tear-off and attach the photos to the message you send with the final invoice. It turns 'why did it cost more?' into 'thanks for showing me'.

faqs.question: What is a square in roofing?
faqs.answer: A square is 100 square feet of roof surface. Roofers price tear-off, materials and labor per square, and add a waste factor (often 5–15%, depending on the roof's shape) to the materials.

faqs.question: How do I invoice a roof replacement covered by insurance?
faqs.answer: Invoice the work with the same line items the adjuster used, put the claim number in the notes, and bill the homeowner for their deductible. The insurer usually pays in parts, so record each payment as it arrives.

faqs.question: Should rotten decking be on a separate line?
faqs.answer: Yes. Agree a price per sheet in the contract, then invoice the number of sheets replaced with photos. It's the most common surprise on a roof, and a separate, documented line keeps it from becoming a dispute.

faqs.question: Do roofers charge sales tax?
faqs.answer: It depends on the state: in some, roofers pay tax on materials when they buy them and don't charge it to the homeowner; in others the job is taxable. Check your state's rule and keep it the same on every invoice.

h1: Free Painting Invoice Template & Example
subtitle: For house painters and decorators: how to invoice prep work, walls by the square foot, ceilings, trim and paint, so the customer sees the care behind the finish they're looking at.
intro_paragraph: Good painting is mostly preparation the customer never sees: patching, sanding, caulking, masking. If the invoice only shows 'Paint living room', the price looks high for what seems like a weekend job. A painting invoice that separates prep, coats, surfaces and materials explains the price and makes the customer proud of what they paid for.
what_to_include_intro: Painting invoices work best when they follow the rooms and surfaces the customer walked through with you. Include these parts.
req_1_title: Prep work as its own line
req_1_text: Patching, sanding, caulking, masking and moving furniture take hours. Bill them separately (by the hour or as a flat prep fee), so the customer sees the work that makes the finish last.
req_2_text: Walls and ceilings by the square foot (or by room), trim by the linear foot, doors and windows by the piece. Name the rooms. It matches how you quoted and makes the invoice easy to check.
req_3_text: 'Two coats' is part of the product. Write it on each surface line, especially when a color change or fresh drywall needed a primer coat.
req_4_text: Name the paint line and sheen, and the quantity. Customers like to know what's on their walls, and the next time they need a touch-up they'll know exactly what to buy (or whom to call).
req_5_text: Most painters take a deposit to buy paint and secure the dates. Show it as received on the final invoice so the balance is clear.
req_6_text: List the color names and codes per room in the notes, and how long to wait before washing the walls. It's the most useful thing on the invoice a year later.
what_to_include_outro: A painting invoice like this reads like a finished job sheet: every room, every surface and every color, ready for the customer's records.
sample_breakdown_intro: Interior repaint of a living and dining room with ceilings, trim and six doors. The customer paid a 30% deposit when booking.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Prep: patch, sand, caulk and mask
Walls, 2 coats: living and dining room

sample_breakdown_notes: Colors: walls 'Agreeable Gray' (eggshell), ceilings flat white, doors 'Pure White' semi-gloss. Leftover paint labeled in the garage. Wait 2 weeks before washing walls. 2-year warranty on peeling. Balance due on completion.

industry_notes.title: Pricing by area, room or hour
industry_notes.text: Per square foot is easiest to compare, per room is easiest to sell, per hour is safest for repairs and touch-ups. Use one per job and keep the invoice in the same unit as the quote.

industry_notes.title: Exterior jobs and weather days
industry_notes.text: On exteriors, agree in the quote that weather delays don't change the price. If power washing, scraping or wood repair turn out larger than expected, add them as separate lines with photos.

industry_notes.title: Who buys the paint
industry_notes.text: If the customer supplies the paint, say so in the notes and leave the materials line out; your warranty may not cover a product you didn't choose.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes painters make on invoices

mistakes.title: Hiding the prep
mistakes.text: If prep is folded into 'walls', customers compare your price with a cheaper quote that skipped it. Showing it separately makes your quality visible.

mistakes.title: No color record
mistakes.text: Without color names on the invoice, the customer can't touch up a scuff or order the same shade, and they won't think of you when they need more.

mistakes.title: Waiting to invoice
mistakes.text: Do the final walk-through, fix the little things on the spot and send the invoice before you pack the drop cloths. That's when the customer is happiest with the room.

pro_tip: Leave a labeled can of each color with the room name written on the lid, and mention it in the invoice notes. Customers remember the painter who did that, and they call the same one for the next room.

faqs.question: How do painters calculate an invoice?
faqs.answer: Most measure the wall and ceiling area in square feet, count doors and windows, and add prep time and materials. Others price per room or per hour. Whichever unit you quote in, use the same unit on the invoice.

faqs.question: Should a painting invoice list the paint brand?
faqs.answer: Yes. Name the paint line, sheen and color per room. It shows the quality you used and lets the customer buy the right paint for touch-ups.

faqs.question: How much deposit do painters take?
faqs.answer: Commonly 20–50%, enough to buy materials and book the dates. Show it as received on the final invoice. Some states limit deposits on home improvement work, so check your local rule.

faqs.question: How do I invoice extra prep work I didn't quote?
faqs.answer: Stop and agree it with the customer before you do it (a text is fine), then add it as a separate line on the invoice with the hours or the agreed price. Undocumented extras are the most common painting dispute.

faqs.question: Can I fill in this painting invoice online?
faqs.answer: Yes. Open the example in the free generator, change the rooms, areas and prices, and download a PDF. The Invoicor iPhone app saves your usual line items and customers if you invoice every week.

h1: Free Web Development Invoice Template & Example
subtitle: For freelance web developers and small studios: how to invoice milestones, extra hours, hosting and licenses so clients approve the payment quickly and scope creep is visible, not silent.
intro_paragraph: Web projects drift. A five-page site becomes six, a contact form needs a CRM connection, and 'small tweaks' add up to a day. A web development invoice is where scope gets written down: what was delivered in this milestone, what was extra and what the client is paying for every month after launch.
what_to_include_intro: Clients approve developer invoices faster when every line maps to something they can open in a browser. These fields do that.
req_1_text: Bill by milestone ('Design system and 5 page templates, approved'), each with a short description that matches the proposal. Milestones are easier to approve than hours because the client can see the result.
req_2_text: Anything not in the proposal goes on its own line with hours and rate, plus a reference to the email or ticket where the client asked for it. This keeps the relationship friendly and the scope honest.
req_3_text: Domains, hosting, premium plugins, fonts and stock images you bought for the client are separate, reimbursable lines. State the period for subscriptions ('12 months').
req_4_text: Most developers ask 25–50% up front. Subtract it on later invoices and show the remaining balance, so the client always knows what's left.
req_5_text: State when the code and content transfer to the client, usually on full payment. It protects your work and gives the client a clear reason to pay the final invoice.
req_6_text: If you maintain the site after launch, bill it as a clearly named monthly line ('Maintenance: updates, backups, 2 hrs support') with what's included, so it never looks like a surprise fee.
what_to_include_outro: With these parts, each invoice is also a short project report the client can forward to their boss without explaining anything.
sample_breakdown_intro: The second invoice for a small business website. The client paid a $2,700 deposit at the start; this invoice covers the delivered milestones, one extra request and a year of hosting.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Out of scope: contact form to CRM (ticket #14)

sample_breakdown_notes: Staging: staging.example.com. Code repository and admin access transfer on full payment. 30 days of bug fixes included after launch. Payment due within 14 days.

industry_notes.title: Fixed price or hourly
industry_notes.text: Fixed price per milestone works when the scope is clear; hourly (or a weekly rate) works for open-ended product work. Many developers combine them: fixed milestones plus an hourly rate for anything outside the proposal.

industry_notes.title: Retainers
industry_notes.text: For ongoing work, a monthly retainer with a fixed number of hours gives you predictable income. Bill it at the start of the month and list hours used in the notes, so unused or extra hours are visible.

industry_notes.title: International clients
industry_notes.text: Invoice in the client's currency when you can, put your bank details (IBAN and SWIFT) on the invoice, and check whether VAT rules require the client's VAT ID or a reverse-charge note for business clients in other countries.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes developers make on invoices

mistakes.title: Silent scope creep
mistakes.text: Doing the extra request for free 'just this once' trains the client to ask again. Bill it, even at a friendly rate, and it stays a conversation instead of an expectation.

mistakes.title: Handing over before payment
mistakes.text: Once the client has the admin login and the repository, the final invoice loses its urgency. Make handover the last step after payment.

mistakes.title: Vague line names
mistakes.text: 'Development work: $4,500' gets forwarded to finance with questions. 'Front-end build, 5 pages, responsive' gets approved.

pro_tip: Send the invoice with a link to the staging site or a short screen recording of what was delivered. Clients approve faster when they can see the milestone, and the recording doubles as a record if questions come up later.

faqs.question: How do I write an invoice for web development?
faqs.answer: Put your business and the client's details at the top, then the delivered milestones with short descriptions that match the proposal, any out-of-scope hours with their rate, reimbursable costs like hosting or licenses, the deposit already paid and the balance due. Add handover terms and the due date in the notes.

faqs.question: Should freelance developers charge hourly or per project?
faqs.answer: Per project (by milestone) when the scope is clear, hourly when it isn't. Many developers quote a fixed price for the defined work and add an hourly rate for anything outside it.

faqs.question: How much deposit should a web developer ask for?
faqs.answer: Commonly 25–50% before starting, or the first milestone up front. It covers your time on discovery and filters out clients who aren't committed.

faqs.question: How do I invoice hosting and domains?
faqs.answer: As separate reimbursable lines with the period ('Hosting, 12 months'). If you resell hosting with a markup or a maintenance package, name it clearly as your service.

faqs.question: Can I invoice international clients in their currency?
faqs.answer: Yes. Invoicor supports 38 currencies and 11 invoice languages, in the app and in the free online generator. Add your bank details so the client can pay by transfer.

h1: Free Personal Training Invoice Template & Example
subtitle: For personal trainers and online coaches: how to invoice session packages, consultations and products so clients commit up front and your cancellation policy is written down every time.
intro_paragraph: Personal training lives on commitment. A client who prepays twelve sessions shows up; a client who pays per session cancels when it rains. A clear personal training invoice sells the package, records what's included and puts your cancellation policy in writing, without an awkward conversation on the gym floor.
what_to_include_intro: A trainer's invoice is short, but a few details make the difference between a payment and a dispute.
req_1_text: '12-session package, 60 minutes, valid 8 weeks from 3 March'. The number of sessions, the length and the expiry date belong in the line itself, so there's never a question about what was bought.
req_2_text: Assessments, nutrition consultations and programs for training alone are separate services with their own price. Listing them shows the full value of what you offer.
req_3_text: Bands, supplements or apparel are goods and may be taxed differently from training. Put them on their own lines (or their own invoice) so the tax is easy to get right.
req_4_text: Write your rules in the notes: how much notice a cancellation needs, what happens to a missed session and whether packages are refundable. Having it on every invoice ends most arguments before they start.
req_5_text: Gym, park, the client's home or online. It matters for travel fees and, in some places, for tax. A word in the line description is enough.
req_6_text: A payment link or business bank details, not a personal payment app. It looks professional and keeps your business income separate for tax time.
what_to_include_outro: Short, clear and the same every time: that's what makes clients see you as a business and pay like one.
sample_breakdown_intro: A new client starting with a 12-session package, a nutrition consultation, a body composition assessment and a set of resistance bands for training at home.
sample_breakdown_notes: Sessions at Northside Gym. Cancellations need 24 hours' notice; later cancellations count as a used session. Packages are non-refundable but can be paused once for illness. Payment due before the first session.

industry_notes.title: Packages beat single sessions
industry_notes.text: Prepaid packages improve attendance and smooth your income. A small discount per session for larger packages rewards commitment without cutting your hourly rate much.

industry_notes.title: Online coaching
industry_notes.text: For monthly programming and check-ins, send one invoice at the start of each month. Duplicate last month's invoice and change the date; it's quicker than writing a new one.

industry_notes.title: Gym rent and fees
industry_notes.text: If you pay a gym a floor fee or a percentage, that's your cost, not a line for the client. Keep it in your own records for taxes.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes trainers make on invoices

mistakes.title: Taking payment by personal app
mistakes.text: Personal payment apps don't produce proper records, and using them for business can break their terms. An invoice with a business payment link solves both.

mistakes.title: No expiry date on packages
mistakes.text: Without an end date, a 10-session package can stretch over a year. Put the validity in the line description.

mistakes.title: Policy only on the website
mistakes.text: Clients don't reread your website before cancelling. They do read the invoice they paid.

pro_tip: Send the package invoice right after the free consultation, while the client is still in the gym and motivated. Paying on the spot turns 'I'll think about it' into a booked first session.

faqs.question: What should a personal training invoice include?
faqs.answer: Your business name and contact details, the client's name, the date and invoice number, the package or sessions (number, length and expiry), any extra services or products, tax where it applies, the total, how to pay and your cancellation policy.

faqs.question: Should personal trainers charge sales tax?
faqs.answer: Training services are often not taxed, but products like supplements or equipment usually are, and some places tax digital programs. Rules differ by state and country, so check yours and keep products on separate lines.

faqs.question: How do I invoice a session package?
faqs.answer: One line for the package with the number of sessions, their length and how long the package is valid, paid before the first session. Track used sessions in your calendar or training app.

faqs.question: How do I bill online coaching clients every month?
faqs.answer: Send an invoice at the start of each month. In the Invoicor app you duplicate last month's invoice in one tap and update the date; Invoicor doesn't send invoices automatically, so you stay in control.

faqs.question: Is this personal trainer invoice template free?

intro_paragraph: Tutoring is usually paid by parents who weren't in the room. Your invoice is how they see what their money bought: how many sessions, which subject, what was covered. A clear tutoring invoice builds the trust that keeps a student with you for years, and it settles questions about missed lessons before they turn awkward.
what_to_include_intro: Parents scan a tutoring invoice in seconds. Make these parts easy to find.
req_1_text: Bill the parent, but name the student and the subject on every line ('Emma, algebra'). Families with more than one child, or with grandparents paying, will thank you.
req_2_text: List the number of sessions and their dates (in the line or the notes). It's the first thing a parent checks against the family calendar.
req_3_text: Practice tests, essay reviews and progress reports take extra time. Bill them as separate services so parents see the full picture.
req_4_text: Books, printed materials or platform subscriptions you bought for the student go on their own lines.
req_5_text: State the notice you need to cancel (24 hours is common) and what happens to a late cancellation. When it applies, add it as a line on the invoice, so it's transparent rather than a surprise.
req_6_text: One or two sentences on what was covered and what's next. It's not required, but it's the part parents read most, and the best reason they keep booking.
what_to_include_outro: An invoice like this tells parents what happened this month and why it was worth it, which is what turns one term into a school year.
sample_breakdown_intro: A monthly invoice for one student: weekly math sessions, a practice test with review, a workbook, and one lesson cancelled without notice.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: SAT practice test and review session

sample_breakdown_notes: Student: Emma R. This month: linear equations, systems of equations, first full SAT practice test (math 640). Next: functions and word problems. Payment due by April 5.

industry_notes.title: Monthly in arrears or in advance
industry_notes.text: Billing at the end of the month for sessions held is simplest. Billing at the start for the month ahead improves attendance and cash flow. Pick one, tell families, and keep it the same.

industry_notes.title: Packages and discounts
industry_notes.text: A small discount for a prepaid block of sessions rewards commitment. Show it as a discount on the invoice, so the full value stays visible.

industry_notes.title: Online sessions
industry_notes.text: For online tutoring, mention the platform in the notes. If students are in other countries, you can invoice in their currency and language.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes tutors make on invoices

mistakes.title: No dates

mistakes.title: Waiving every missed session
mistakes.text: Being kind once is fine; never charging makes your policy meaningless. Apply it consistently and say so on the invoice.

mistakes.title: Invoicing irregularly
mistakes.text: Families budget monthly. An invoice that arrives on the same day every month gets paid like a bill; one that arrives whenever gets forgotten.

pro_tip: End every invoice with one specific win ('Emma solved her first full SAT section under time'). Parents forward those to the other parent, and that's how tutors get referrals.

faqs.question: How do tutors invoice parents?
faqs.answer: Most send one invoice per month per family, listing each student, subject and session date, any test prep or materials, and the total. Add your missed-session policy and how to pay in the notes.

faqs.question: Should I charge for missed tutoring sessions?
faqs.answer: A common, fair policy is to charge for sessions cancelled with less than 24 hours' notice and reschedule anything earlier. Write it on every invoice and apply it consistently.

faqs.question: Do tutors need to charge sales tax?
faqs.answer: In many places tutoring is a service without sales tax, but rules differ, and VAT may apply in other countries above a turnover threshold. Check your local rule; materials you sell can be taxed differently.

faqs.question: Can I invoice in another currency for online students?

h1: Free Catering Invoice Template & Example
subtitle: For caterers and private chefs: how to invoice per-guest menus, staff hours, rentals, service charges and deposits, so the final bill matches the event the client planned.
intro_paragraph: Catering invoices carry a lot: a menu priced per guest, staff by the hour, rentals, a service charge, a deposit paid months ago and tax on top. Clients planning a wedding or a company event are already juggling budgets, so an invoice that lays every part out clearly is part of the service, and it's what gets the final balance paid on time.
what_to_include_intro: Event clients compare the invoice with the proposal they signed. These parts keep the two aligned.
req_1_text: Event name, date, venue and the final guest count. Most disputes are about the guest count, so state the number the client confirmed and when.
req_2_text: Menu items or packages per guest ('Plated dinner, 3 courses × 120 guests'). It's how you quoted, and it lets the client see the effect of a changed headcount immediately.
req_3_text: Servers, bartenders and chefs on site, with the number of staff and hours. Overtime past the agreed end time goes on its own line.
req_4_text: Linens, china, glassware, equipment and fees like cake cutting or corkage, each named. Clients often don't realize how much of an event is rentals until they see it listed.
req_5_text: If you add a service charge, state the percentage and what it's based on, and be clear that it isn't a tip if it isn't. Unexplained service charges are a common source of complaints.
req_6_text: Subtract the deposit, add tax as your state requires (often including the service charge), and make the balance and its due date unmistakable.
what_to_include_outro: When the invoice mirrors the proposal line for line, the client signs off without a meeting, which is exactly what they want the week after their event.
sample_breakdown_intro: A wedding dinner for 120 guests with passed appetizers, six staff for six hours, rentals, a 20% service charge on food, and a $3,000 deposit paid at booking. Tax rules for catering vary; this example taxes everything at 8%.
sample_breakdown_notes: Event: Lee & Patel wedding, June 14, Riverside Barn. Final guest count of 120 confirmed May 31. The service charge covers event staffing costs and is not a gratuity. Balance due within 7 days of the event.

industry_notes.title: Final guest count deadline
industry_notes.text: Set a date (often 7–14 days before the event) after which the guest count can go up but not down. Put it in the contract and repeat it on the invoice.

industry_notes.title: Deposits
industry_notes.text: Deposits of 25–50% at booking are common for events, sometimes non-refundable to cover dates you turned down. Show each payment as received.

industry_notes.title: Tax on catering
industry_notes.text: Many US states tax catering, and often the service charge too, while a voluntary tip isn't taxed. Rules differ widely, so check yours. Invoicor applies one tax rate per invoice, which fits most catering jobs.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes caterers make on invoices

mistakes.title: Lump-sum event pricing
mistakes.text: 'Wedding catering: $11,327' makes the client wonder what changed since the proposal. Per-guest lines show it.

mistakes.title: Unexplained service charges
mistakes.text: Guests and clients often read a service charge as a tip. Say what it is in one sentence.

mistakes.title: Forgetting overtime
mistakes.text: When the party runs an hour late, add the extra staff hours to the invoice with the agreed rate, instead of absorbing them.

pro_tip: Send the final invoice within two days of the event with one photo of the table setup. Clients pay faster while the memory is fresh, and the photo often ends up on social media with your name.

faqs.question: What should a catering invoice include?
faqs.answer: The event name, date, venue and final guest count; food per guest; staff and hours; rentals and extra fees; any service charge with its percentage; the deposit received; tax; the balance due and its due date.

faqs.question: Is a catering service charge the same as a tip?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. A service charge is a fee you set (often 18–22%) that may cover staffing costs; a tip is voluntary. Say on the invoice which one it is, because tax and how it's shared with staff can differ.

faqs.question: How do I invoice a catering deposit?
faqs.answer: Send a deposit invoice at booking for the agreed share of the estimated total, then subtract it on the final invoice after the event, once the guest count and extras are final.

faqs.question: Do caterers charge sales tax?
faqs.answer: In many US states yes, on food and often on the service charge and rentals. Rules vary by state and venue, so check yours and treat every event the same way.

what_to_include_intro: Movers are paid on trust. These parts make the invoice something the customer can check in a minute.
req_1_text: State the number of movers, the truck and the hourly rate, plus the start and finish times. Hourly moves are where disputes happen, so write the times down when you start and when you finish.
req_2_text: If you charge for driving to the first address and back from the last, say how: a flat fee or travel time. Customers accept it when it's named and was on the quote.
req_3_text: Boxes, tape, wrap, wardrobe boxes and mattress bags, itemized or as one materials line. It's a real cost, and itemizing it shows you didn't pad the hours.
req_4_text: Pianos, safes, stairs, long carries and elevator waits are extra work. List them as separate lines with the agreed price.
req_5_title: Deposit and how it was paid
req_5_text: Subtract the booking deposit and state how the customer can pay the balance today.
req_6_text: State the liability coverage the customer chose and how to report damage (and by when). In the US, interstate movers have specific federal rules on this; local moves follow state rules.
what_to_include_outro: The best moving invoices take less than a minute to read, which is about how long a tired customer will give them.

industry_notes.title: Hourly versus flat-rate moves

industry_notes.title: Minimum hours

industry_notes.title: Long-distance moves

mistakes_title: Three mistakes movers make on invoices

mistakes.title: No start and finish times
mistakes.text: Without times, every hourly invoice becomes 'you were only here four hours'. Write them on the invoice.

mistakes.title: Surprise extras
mistakes.text: A piano or a fourth-floor walk-up discovered on moving day should be priced before you lift it, then listed on the invoice.

mistakes.title: Collecting payment later
mistakes.text: Ask for the balance on delivery, as agreed at booking. Chasing a payment after the truck has left is slow and uncertain.

pro_tip: Walk through the new home with the customer before you hand over the invoice, and ask if everything is where they want it. Two minutes of moving a sofa again earns more goodwill (and reviews) than any discount.

faqs.question: What should a moving company invoice include?
faqs.answer: Your business and license details, the customer, both addresses and the date, the crew size, truck and hourly rate with start and finish times, travel fees, packing materials, special items, the deposit paid, the balance and how damage claims work.

faqs.question: How do movers charge for travel time?
faqs.answer: Either a flat travel fee or the time to drive to the first address and back from the last, billed at the hourly rate. Put the method on the quote and use the same one on the invoice.

faqs.question: Should packing materials be on a separate line?
faqs.answer: Yes. Boxes, tape and wrap are a real cost; listing them separately shows the hourly charge is only for labor.

faqs.question: When should a customer pay the movers?
faqs.answer: Most local movers take a small deposit at booking and the balance on delivery. Say so on the quote and the invoice, and accept a payment method that works on the doorstep, like your own payment link.

what_to_include_intro: A good pest control invoice is part bill, part service report. Include these parts.

faqs.question: Do pest control companies have to list the chemicals used?

faqs.question: Is pest control taxable?

intro_paragraph: A virtual assistant's work is mostly invisible. Your client sees a cleaner inbox and a calendar that works, but not the eighteen small tasks behind it. A clear VA invoice groups hours by task, shows the billing period, names any retainer the hours come out of and lists software or subscriptions you paid on the client's behalf. what_to_include_outro: An invoice built this way doubles as a work log. Clients who can see the value of each hour tend to keep you on and add tasks rather than trim your hours.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes virtual assistants make on invoices

mistakes.title: One vague line for all the hours
mistakes.text: 'Admin support, 28 hours' invites the client to wonder what they paid for. Break hours into tasks so the value is obvious.

mistakes.title: Retainer hours left unexplained
mistakes.text: If the invoice doesn't say how many hours were used and what happens to the rest, the client assumes they roll over forever. Write your rule on each invoice.

mistakes.title: Absorbing client costs
mistakes.text: Paying for a client's tool or printing with your own card and forgetting to bill it eats into your rate. Add pass-through costs as their own line the month you pay them.

pro_tip: Send the invoice on the same day every month, ideally the first working day, with your time log as a separate attachment in the email. Clients start to expect it, approve it faster, and you never have to chase a month you forgot to bill.
format_pdf_desc: A PDF keeps your task breakdown and rates exactly as you wrote them, whether the client opens it on a phone between showings or forwards it to their bookkeeper. Most small business clients file VA invoices as PDFs with their monthly expenses.

faqs.question: What should a virtual assistant invoice include?
faqs.answer: Your name or business name, the client's name, an invoice number and date, the billing period, hours or items grouped by task with the rate for each, any retainer used and what happens to unused hours, pass-through costs, the total, the due date and how to pay.

faqs.question: How do I invoice a monthly VA retainer?
faqs.answer: Many VAs invoice the retainer at the start of the month and bill any overage hours at the end. Each month in the Invoicor app you duplicate the last invoice and change the date and hours; the app doesn't send invoices automatically, so you send each one yourself.

faqs.question: Should a virtual assistant charge sales tax?
faqs.answer: Usually not for remote administrative services, but a few states tax some services, and digital products or design work can be treated differently. Check your state's rule, and the client's state if you work for out-of-state businesses.

faqs.question: How often should a virtual assistant send invoices?
faqs.answer: Weekly or every two weeks suits new clients and hourly work, because it keeps the amounts small and shows how much time tasks take. Monthly suits steady retainer clients. Pick one rhythm per client and write it in your contract.

faqs.question: Can I use this virtual assistant invoice template for free?
faqs.answer: Yes. Open the example in the free online generator, change the tasks and hours to your month and download the PDF. The Invoicor iPhone app saves your clients and standard tasks, so next month's invoice starts from a duplicate.

h1: Free Pet Sitting Invoice Template & Example
subtitle: For pet sitters and dog walkers: how to bill drop-ins, overnight stays, walks, medication and holiday rates so owners know exactly what each visit cost while they were away.
intro_paragraph: Pet owners hand you their keys, their alarm code and an animal they love, then leave town. When they come home, the invoice is part of how they judge the trip went well. A good pet sitting invoice lists every visit by date and type, shows the extras like a second walk or giving insulin, and explains any holiday or last-minute rate before the owner has to ask. It also gives you a clean record of who you sat for and when, which helps with your own scheduling and taxes.
what_to_include_intro: Owners read a pet sitting invoice against their memory of the trip. Include these parts so it lines up.
req_1_text: Name the pets ('Biscuit, golden retriever; Miso, cat') and the home address. If you sit for the same family at more than one home, or watch pets at your place, say where the care happened.
req_2_text: List drop-in visits, walks and overnight stays separately, with their length (30-minute drop-in, 60-minute walk) and the dates. A short line per visit type with a quantity keeps a ten-day trip readable.
req_3_text: Medication, injections, extra feeding visits, litter changes beyond normal, plant watering or bringing in the mail. Extras you agreed to should appear as their own lines, even at a small price, so the owner sees the care given.
req_4_text: If you charge more on Thanksgiving, Christmas or bookings made within 48 hours, show the surcharge per visit on its own line rather than raising the visit price silently.
req_5_text: Some sitters charge a one-time meet-and-greet or a key pickup and return fee for new clients. If yours is free, saying so on the first invoice still shows the owner what's included.
req_6_text: Give the due date, your PayPal, Venmo business or Stripe link, and your cancellation rule for booked holiday dates, so the policy is on paper before the next busy season.
what_to_include_outro: Laid out like this, the invoice works as a care summary. Owners who can see each visit trust you with longer trips and pass your name to their neighbors.
sample_breakdown_intro: A Thanksgiving week booking for one dog and one cat: twice-daily drop-ins, three overnight stays, midday walks, a daily insulin shot for the cat and a holiday surcharge. Tax rules vary; a few states tax pet sitting or boarding, so this example adds 4% sales tax. Check your state's rule.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Drop-in visit, 30 min (feeding, litter, play), Nov 22 to 26
Overnight stay, 8 p.m. to 7 a.m., Nov 26 to 28
Insulin injection for Miso (cat), per dose

sample_breakdown_notes: Pets: Biscuit (golden retriever) and Miso (cat). All visits completed; Biscuit ate well, Miso's insulin given at 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. as instructed. House key returned to lockbox. Payment due within 7 days via the link on this invoice.

industry_notes.title: Regular walkers
industry_notes.text: Weekday dog walking clients are often billed weekly or every two weeks rather than per walk. Count the walks in the period, list missed or extra walks, and keep the same invoice day so owners can plan for it.

industry_notes.title: Additional pets
industry_notes.text: A second dog or cat usually adds a few dollars per visit, not a full second visit. Show it as a separate 'additional pet' line so owners with one pet and owners with three see why their totals differ.

industry_notes.title: Taxes and licenses
industry_notes.text: Most states don't tax pet sitting in a client's home, but some tax pet care services, boarding or grooming, and a few cities require a business license for dog walkers. Check your state and city once and apply the same rule to every invoice.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes pet sitters make on invoices

mistakes.title: One total for the whole trip
mistakes.text: 'Pet sitting, Nov 22 to 28: $717' hides what was done. List visit types and counts so the owner can match them to their trip.

mistakes.title: Silent holiday pricing
mistakes.text: Raising the visit price on holidays without a separate line feels like a surprise. Put the surcharge on its own line and mention it when you take the booking.

mistakes.title: Forgetting extras like medication
mistakes.text: Giving pills or injections takes time and care. If it isn't on the invoice, the owner doesn't know it was done, and you aren't paid for it.

pro_tip: Text the owner one photo per visit while they're away, then send the invoice within a day of their return while the trip is fresh. A calm, itemized invoice right after a smooth trip is the moment owners book their next holiday with you.
format_pdf_desc: A PDF invoice looks the same on the owner's phone at the airport as it does printed on the fridge. It also gives you a fixed record of each booking's dates and visits, which helps when a regular client asks what last summer's trip cost.

faqs.question: What should a pet sitting invoice include?
faqs.answer: Your business name, the owner's name, the pets and service address, an invoice number and date, each visit type with its dates and count, extras such as medication or extra walks, any holiday surcharge, tax where it applies, the total, the due date and how to pay.

faqs.question: How do I invoice weekly dog walking clients?
faqs.answer: Send one invoice per week or every two weeks listing the walks in that period. In the Invoicor app you duplicate the last invoice, change the date and the number of walks, and send it; the app doesn't send invoices automatically.

faqs.question: Should I take a deposit for holiday pet sitting?
faqs.answer: Many sitters ask for a deposit to hold holiday dates. Send a separate invoice for the deposit when the client books, then a final invoice after the trip with the deposit shown as a line with a negative amount or in the notes.

faqs.question: Is pet sitting taxable?
faqs.answer: It depends on the state. Most don't tax in-home pet sitting, but some tax pet care, boarding or grooming services. Check your state's rule and keep it consistent on every invoice.

faqs.question: Can I use this pet sitting invoice template for free?
faqs.answer: Yes. Open the example in the free online generator, change the pets, visits and dates, and download the PDF. The Invoicor iPhone app saves your regular clients and visit types, so repeat bookings take a minute to invoice.

title: Makeup Artist Invoice Template & Example (Free) | Invoicor

h1: Free Makeup Artist Invoice Template & Example
subtitle: For freelance makeup artists and hair and makeup teams: how to invoice brides, bridal parties, photo shoots and events, with retainers, travel and early call times spelled out.
intro_paragraph: A wedding morning is not the time to talk about money. Makeup artists who get paid smoothly settle the numbers on paper long before the day: a retainer to hold the date, then a final invoice that lists every face, every set of lashes and every fee the bride agreed to. The same goes for photo shoots and events, where the client is often a photographer, a brand or a production company that needs a clean invoice for its own books. A clear makeup artist invoice makes you look as polished as your work.
what_to_include_intro: A bride, a mother of the bride and a production coordinator all read the invoice differently. Include these parts so each one can follow it.
req_1_title: Event date, location and call time
req_1_text: Write the wedding or shoot date, the address where you worked and your start time. Early call times and on-location work explain several of the fees that follow.
req_2_text: List the bride, each bridesmaid, the mothers and any flower girls by service type: full glam, natural makeup, touch-up only. A per-person count is what the bride uses to split costs with her party.
req_3_text: If the trial was paid separately, reference it. If it's billed on this invoice, give it its own line with its date, so it isn't confused with the wedding day services.
req_4_text: Strip or individual lashes, airbrush upgrade, touch-up kits to take home, or staying on site for touch-ups through photos. Show each add-on with its quantity.
req_5_title: Travel, early start and waiting fees
req_5_text: Travel beyond your included radius, a fee for starts before 7 a.m., parking, and hourly on-site time if you stay for the reception. Agreed fees belong on their own lines.
req_6_text: Show the retainer you already received as a negative line, with its date or invoice number, then the balance and when it's due, often on or before the wedding day.
what_to_include_outro: When every face and fee is on the invoice, the bride can share it with her party, the balance gets paid on time and nobody remembers the money part of the day.
sample_breakdown_intro: A wedding morning at a hotel suite: bridal makeup, four bridesmaids, the mother of the bride, strip lashes for six, travel and a 6 a.m. start, with the retainer already paid deducted. Tax rules vary; most states don't tax makeup services, but some tax cosmetic products sold, so check your state. This example charges no sales tax.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Bridal makeup, wedding day (trial billed on #1038)
Travel fee, 30 miles beyond included radius
Early start fee, 6:00 a.m. call time

sample_breakdown_notes: Wedding of Ana and Luis, June 14, Riverside Hotel, Suite 1204. Services start 6:00 a.m.; ready by 10:30 a.m. for photos. Balance due by June 14 via the link on this invoice. Retainer is non-refundable as agreed in the booking contract.

industry_notes.title: Retainers hold the date
industry_notes.text: Bridal artists usually take a non-refundable retainer, often 25 to 50% of the booked total, when the contract is signed. Invoice it separately, then deduct it on the final invoice so the bride sees what she still owes.

industry_notes.title: Commercial and editorial work
industry_notes.text: Photo shoots, music videos and brand campaigns are often billed by half day or full day, plus kit fee and overtime. The client may need a purchase order number or a job name on the invoice, so ask before the shoot.

industry_notes.title: Who pays
industry_notes.text: Bridesmaids sometimes pay for their own makeup. Decide up front whether the bride gets one invoice for everyone or each person is billed separately, and write it in the contract so nobody is chased on the day.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes makeup artists make on invoices

mistakes.title: Retainer not shown
mistakes.text: A final invoice for the full amount, without the retainer deducted, makes the bride think she's being charged twice. Always show it as a negative line.

mistakes.title: Fees mentioned only in messages
mistakes.text: Travel or early start fees agreed in a DM months ago get forgotten. Put them in the contract and on the invoice as separate lines.

mistakes.title: Headcount changes left out
mistakes.text: A bridesmaid added the week before, or a flower girl who skipped makeup, changes the total. Update the invoice to the faces you actually did.

pro_tip: Send the final invoice two weeks before the wedding with a confirmed headcount and call time, and ask for the balance before the day. The bride arrives at her wedding morning with nothing to pay, and you can focus on the work.
format_pdf_desc: A PDF looks polished on a bride's phone and can be forwarded to the parent or planner paying the bill without anyone editing the numbers. Production companies also expect a PDF they can file with the shoot's expenses.

faqs.question: What should a makeup artist invoice include?
faqs.answer: Your business name, the client's name, the event date, location and call time, each service by person, add-ons like lashes, travel and early start fees, any retainer already paid, tax where it applies, the balance due, the due date and how to pay.

faqs.question: How do I invoice a bridal retainer?
faqs.answer: Send a separate invoice for the retainer when the bride books. On the final invoice, show the retainer as a line with a negative amount, with its date or invoice number, so the balance is clear.

faqs.question: Do makeup artists charge sales tax?
faqs.answer: Most states don't tax makeup application as a service, but some tax cosmetic products you sell, like a take-home lipstick, and a few tax personal care services. Check your state's rule and apply it the same way each time.

faqs.question: When should the balance for wedding makeup be paid?
faqs.answer: Many artists ask for the balance a week or two before the wedding, others on the morning itself. Write the due date on the invoice and in your contract; collecting before the day avoids handling money during the event.

faqs.question: Can I use this makeup artist invoice template for free?
faqs.answer: Yes. Open the example in the free online generator, change the faces, fees and date, and download the PDF. The Invoicor iPhone app saves your services and clients, and you can add your PayPal or Stripe link so the bride pays online.

h1: Free Carpentry Invoice Template & Example
subtitle: For finish carpenters, cabinet makers and framing crews: how to bill labor, lumber and sheet goods, trim by the linear foot and hardware so homeowners and contractors can check every line.
intro_paragraph: Carpentry jobs mix two things clients find hard to judge: skilled hours and a pile of materials. A homeowner looking at a new built-in bookcase doesn't know it took six sheets of birch plywood and sixteen hours of cutting, gluing and fitting. A carpentry invoice that separates labor from lumber, prices trim by the linear foot and lists hardware and finish shows the work behind the result. It also protects you when a client asks why the price moved after they upgraded from paint-grade pine to hardwood.
what_to_include_intro: Whether you bill a homeowner directly or a general contractor, a carpentry invoice should answer these questions.
req_1_text: Describe the work in plain words ('built-in bookcase, living room west wall, 9 ft wide') and the job address. For multi-room jobs, name each room or area so the client can walk the house with the invoice.
req_2_title: Labor by hours or by unit
req_2_text: Show labor as hours at your rate, or by unit where that's your habit: trim and crown by the linear foot, doors per door hung, stair treads per tread. Keep the unit visible in the quantity column.
req_3_text: List plywood and MDF by the sheet with thickness and species, and hardwood or trim stock by the board foot, linear foot or as a lot. Clients who chose an upgraded species see exactly what it added.
req_4_text: Hinges, drawer slides, pulls, brackets, fasteners, glue, primer, paint or stain. Group small consumables into one line, but list visible hardware the client picked separately.
req_5_text: If the client added shelves, changed the finish or asked for extra trim during the job, show each change as its own line with a short description, so the final total matches what was agreed along the way.
req_6_text: Note any deposit already paid for materials, the balance due and your terms. Residential clients often pay on completion; contractors may pay Net 15 or Net 30.
what_to_include_outro: An invoice laid out like this reads like the job itself, room by room and board by board, and it leaves little room for a dispute over the final number.
sample_breakdown_intro: A built-in bookcase with cabinet doors below, plus crown molding in the same room: shop and install labor, birch plywood, poplar face frames and trim, and hardware and finish. Tax rules vary; in some states the whole job is taxable, in others only materials, and many treat it differently again. This example taxes the full invoice at 7%.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Built-in bookcase with lower cabinets: build, install, fit (labor)
Poplar face frame stock and crown molding
Hardware and finish: soft-close hinges, primer, paint

sample_breakdown_notes: Living room, west wall: bookcase 9 ft wide by 8 ft tall, four doors, adjustable shelves. Crown installed on all four walls. Paint color: Benjamin Moore White Dove, satin. Offcuts and leftover paint left with homeowner. 1-year workmanship guarantee on joinery and installation.

industry_notes.title: Materials up front
industry_notes.text: Custom work often needs expensive sheet goods or hardwood bought before you start. Many carpenters take a materials deposit, invoiced separately, then deduct it on the final invoice. Keep supplier receipts with the job in case the client asks.

industry_notes.title: Working as a subcontractor
industry_notes.text: When you work for a general contractor, use their job name or number and the property address on every invoice. They may also ask for your insurance certificate and a lien waiver with payment, depending on the state.

industry_notes.title: Taxes on labor and materials
industry_notes.text: States split on carpentry: some tax the whole job, some tax only materials, and some treat permanent improvements to real property differently from repairs or furniture. Check your state's rule for each type of job you do.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes carpenters make on invoices

mistakes.title: Labor and materials in one lump
mistakes.text: 'Bookcase: $2,405' tells the client nothing. When they compare prices, they can't see that half was skilled labor and half was good plywood.

mistakes.title: Changes billed from memory
mistakes.text: An extra shelf, a switch to stain-grade wood or two more doors agreed on site get forgotten by invoice day. Note each change as it happens and give it its own line.

mistakes.title: Missing units
mistakes.text: A quantity of '48' could mean feet, pieces or hours. Write the unit next to every number so the math can be checked.

pro_tip: Save your common items, like your hourly rate, crown per foot, door hanging and your usual plywood, as products in the app with their units. Building the invoice then takes a few taps per line, and your pricing stays the same from job to job.
format_pdf_desc: A PDF holds the line items, units and job notes exactly as you wrote them, so the homeowner, their spouse and the general contractor all see the same numbers. It's also the version you want on file if a lien or payment question ever comes up.

faqs.question: What should a carpentry invoice include?
faqs.answer: Your business name and license number where your state requires one, the client and job address, an invoice number and date, the scope by room, labor in hours or units, lumber and sheet goods, hardware and finish, any changes, tax where it applies, deposits paid, the balance and your terms.

faqs.question: How do I bill a materials deposit for custom carpentry?
faqs.answer: Send a separate invoice for the deposit before you buy materials. On the final invoice, show the deposit as a line with a negative amount, or mention it in the notes with the date it was paid, so the balance is clear.

faqs.question: Should carpenters charge by the hour or by the job?
faqs.answer: Both are common. Fixed prices work for repeatable items like hanging doors or running trim by the foot; hourly suits custom built-ins and repairs where surprises are likely. Whichever you choose, list the hours or units on the invoice.

faqs.question: Is carpentry work taxable?
faqs.answer: It depends on your state and the type of job. Some states tax labor and materials, others only materials, and many treat permanent improvements to a home differently. Check your state's rule before you set up your invoices.

faqs.answer: Yes. Open the example in the free online generator, change the labor, lumber and hardware to your job, and download the PDF. The Invoicor iPhone app saves your clients and standard rates for the next job.

h1: Free Flooring Invoice Template & Example
subtitle: For flooring installers and flooring stores: how to invoice removal, subfloor prep, installation by the square foot, material with waste, and transitions and trim, so the homeowner's math works.
intro_paragraph: Flooring is priced by the square foot, and homeowners know it. They have measured the room, compared prices at the big box store and read that installation costs a few dollars a foot. A flooring invoice has to show why their total is higher than square footage times a number they saw online: tear-out, haul-away, leveling, the 10% extra material for cuts, quarter round around every wall and transitions at each doorway. When each of those has its own line and unit, the invoice explains itself.
what_to_include_intro: Homeowners will check a flooring invoice with a calculator. Include these parts so the numbers hold up.
req_1_text: List the rooms and the measured square footage ('kitchen, dining and hall: 450 sq ft'). Staircases are usually priced per step, so give them their own line with the number of treads and risers.
req_2_text: Tear-out of old carpet and pad, tile, vinyl or glued-down wood, priced per square foot, plus haul-away or a dumpster fee. Glued or tiled floors take far longer, so name the old floor type.
req_3_text: Leveling compound by the bag, plywood patches by the sheet, moisture barrier or underlayment by the square foot. Prep is where surprises happen; record what you found and what you did about it.
req_4_text: Price installation separately from material, by flooring type and pattern: straight-lay LVP, nail-down hardwood, glue-down engineered, herringbone. Patterns and diagonals cost more, and the line should say why.
req_5_text: If you supply the flooring, show the product name, color and square footage including waste (often 5 to 15%). If the client bought their own, say so, and note any leftover boxes you left on site.
req_6_text: Baseboard or quarter round by the linear foot, transition strips and stair nosing per piece, appliance pull-out and furniture moving per room if you charge for them.
what_to_include_outro: With each part of the job priced in its own unit, the homeowner can match every line to what they see on the floor, and the conversation stays about the result rather than the bill.
sample_breakdown_intro: Replacing carpet with luxury vinyl plank in a kitchen, dining room and hallway: carpet and pad removal, leveling low spots, installation, material with 10% waste, quarter round and three transitions. Tax rules vary; some states tax the whole job, others only the flooring material. This example applies 6% to the full invoice.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Remove and haul away carpet and pad
Self-leveling compound, low spots in dining room
Luxury vinyl plank, 7 in. Oak Harbor, incl. 10% waste
Quarter round, supplied, painted and installed
Transition strips (kitchen to tile, two doorways)

sample_breakdown_notes: Kitchen, dining room and hall, 450 sq ft measured. Two unopened boxes of LVP left in the garage for future repairs. Refrigerator and range moved and reset. Manufacturer's warranty on product; 1-year installer warranty on workmanship. Avoid heavy furniture without felt pads.

industry_notes.title: Material deposits
industry_notes.text: Flooring material is often half the job and is ordered days or weeks ahead. Many installers invoice a deposit when the order is placed, then deduct it on the final invoice. The deposit invoice should name the product and quantity ordered.

industry_notes.title: Subfloor surprises
industry_notes.text: You rarely see the subfloor until the old floor is up. Tell the client before you start that rot, squeaks or low spots are billed as found, and get a quick OK by text before doing extra prep so the line isn't a shock.

industry_notes.title: Labor-only jobs
industry_notes.text: When the client supplies flooring bought elsewhere, say 'material supplied by owner' on the invoice and bill installation and supplies only. Many installers also note that they're not responsible for defects in material they didn't sell.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes flooring installers make on invoices

mistakes.title: Waste not explained
mistakes.text: Billing 495 sq ft of material for a 450 sq ft room without saying why looks like padding. Write 'incl. 10% waste' in the line.

mistakes.title: Prep folded into installation
mistakes.text: Rolling leveling and patching into the per-foot price makes your rate look high next to competitors. Show prep as its own line so the base price compares fairly.

mistakes.title: Forgetting trim and transitions
mistakes.text: Quarter round, reducers and stair nosing are easy to leave off and add up to hundreds of dollars. List them every time, even when the price is small.

pro_tip: Keep your measurements per room in the invoice notes. When the same client calls a year later to do the bedrooms, or needs a board replaced, you have the product, color and area without measuring again.
format_pdf_desc: A PDF keeps the square footage, waste allowance and product names fixed, which matters when the homeowner files a warranty claim with the flooring manufacturer. Many manufacturers ask for proof of professional installation, and a dated PDF invoice is that proof.

faqs.question: What should a flooring invoice include?
faqs.answer: Your business name and license number where required, the client and job address, rooms and measured square footage, removal and disposal, subfloor prep, installation labor, material with waste, trim and transitions, tax where it applies, deposits paid, the balance and your warranty terms.

faqs.question: How do I show a flooring deposit on the final invoice?
faqs.answer: Send the deposit as its own invoice when you order material. On the final invoice, add the deposit as a line with a negative amount and its date, or note it in the notes, so the balance due is clear.

faqs.question: Should I bill flooring material and labor separately?
faqs.answer: Yes. Separate lines let the client compare your installation price with other quotes, and some states tax material and labor differently. It also makes labor-only jobs easy to invoice.

faqs.question: Is flooring installation taxable?
faqs.answer: It depends on the state. Some tax the full job, some tax only the material, and some treat installed flooring as a home improvement with its own rules. Check your state's rule and apply it the same way on every invoice.

faqs.question: Can I use this flooring invoice template for free?
faqs.answer: Yes. Open the example in the free online generator, change the rooms, square footage and products, and download the PDF. The Invoicor iPhone app saves your per-foot rates and common products so the next invoice is quick.

h1: Free Tile Installation Invoice Template & Example
subtitle: For tile setters and tiling contractors: how to invoice showers, backsplashes and floors with demo, waterproofing, tile by size and pattern, niches, trim and setting materials on their own lines.
intro_paragraph: Tile jobs are judged by what you can see, but most of the cost sits behind the tile: tearing out the old shower, flattening walls, the waterproofing membrane, backer board and thinset. A tile installation invoice should make that hidden work visible, and it should price the visible part fairly too, because a 2x2 mosaic floor takes far longer per square foot than a 12x24 wall tile. When each step has its own line with square footage or a count, the homeowner understands why their shower costs what it does.
what_to_include_intro: Clients compare tile prices per square foot, so make that comparison fair. Include these parts.
req_1_text: Name the space and the surfaces ('hall bath shower: three walls to ceiling plus floor; 80 sq ft wall, 15 sq ft floor'). Backsplashes are often measured in square feet, accent bands in linear feet.
req_2_text: Removing old tile, mortar beds and drywall, and disposing of the debris. A cast mortar bed takes much more effort than tile on drywall, so say what you removed.
req_3_text: Backer board, membrane systems, shower pans and flood testing. In wet areas this is the line that protects the house; name the method so the client knows the work was done properly.
req_4_title: Tile setting by size and pattern
req_4_text: Price tile labor per square foot by tile size and layout. Large format, mosaics, herringbone and diagonal layouts each take different time, and separate lines show why the rates differ.
req_5_text: Shower niches, benches, curbs, mitered or trimmed edges and accent strips are usually priced per piece or per linear foot. List each one rather than folding it into the per-foot price.
req_6_title: Materials and who supplied the tile
req_6_text: Thinset, grout, sealer and edge trim as one materials line or several. Say whether the tile was supplied by you or by the homeowner, and note leftover tile left on site for future repairs.
what_to_include_outro: Written this way, the invoice tells the story of the bathroom from bare studs to grout, and it keeps a record of the materials that matters if a repair is ever needed.
sample_breakdown_intro: A hall bathroom shower remodel: demo of old tile, a waterproofing membrane, 12x24 porcelain on the walls, a 2x2 mosaic shower floor, one recessed niche and setting materials. The homeowner bought the tile. Tax rules vary; some states tax labor on home improvement work and some don't. This example taxes the invoice at 5%.

Backer board and liquid waterproofing membrane, walls and pan

industry_notes.title: Owner-supplied tile
industry_notes.text: Homeowners often buy their own tile to choose it in person or save money. Bill labor and setting materials only, note 'tile supplied by owner', and agree in writing how breakage, shortages and lot color differences are handled.

industry_notes.title: Minimum charges
industry_notes.text: Small jobs like a single backsplash or a few cracked tiles take nearly a full day once you count setup, cure time and a return trip to grout. Many setters use a minimum job charge; show it as its own line so it's clear why a 20 sq ft job isn't 20 times your rate.

industry_notes.title: Taxes and permits
industry_notes.text: States differ on whether tile labor is taxed, and some tax tile sold separately from installation. Shower and bathroom remodels may also need a permit depending on your city. Check your state and local rules and note any permit fee as its own line.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes tile installers make on invoices

mistakes.title: One rate for every tile
mistakes.text: Charging the same per foot for mosaic floors and large wall tile hides the real time spent. Split them by size and layout.

mistakes.title: Waterproofing left off
mistakes.text: If the membrane and flood test aren't on the invoice, the client may think you skipped them. List the method, it's your best proof of quality.

mistakes.title: No grout and tile record
mistakes.text: Without the grout color and tile details, matching a repair years later is guesswork. Put them in the notes every time.

pro_tip: Before you close up the walls, take photos of the waterproofing, the niche framing and the flood test, and send them to the client by text with a short note. Then add a line in the invoice notes saying the photos were sent. It builds trust in the work nobody will see again.
format_pdf_desc: A PDF records the tile, grout color and waterproofing method in a form nobody can change, which helps if the home is sold and an inspector or buyer asks how the shower was built. It also prints cleanly for the homeowner's remodel file.

faqs.question: What should a tile installation invoice include?
faqs.answer: Your business name and license number where required, the client and job address, the area and surfaces, demo, substrate and waterproofing, tile labor by size and layout, niches and details, setting materials, who supplied the tile, tax where it applies, deposits paid, the balance and the curing instructions.

faqs.question: How do tile installers charge, per square foot or per job?
faqs.answer: Most price tile setting per square foot by size and pattern, then add demo, prep and details like niches per piece. Small jobs often carry a minimum charge. List each part on the invoice so the per-foot rate isn't confused with the total.

faqs.question: How do I invoice a deposit for a shower remodel?
faqs.answer: Send a separate invoice for the deposit before work starts. On the final invoice, show the deposit as a line with a negative amount and its date, or mention it in the notes, so the client sees the balance due.

faqs.question: Is tile installation taxable?
faqs.answer: It depends on the state. Some tax installation labor, some tax only the tile and materials, and some treat bathroom remodels as home improvements with their own rules. Check your state's rule and keep it consistent.

title: Drywall Invoice Template & Example (Free PDF) | Invoicor
meta_description: Free drywall invoice template with a basement example: hanging, taping to Level 4, board, corner bead and haul-off by the square foot. Download a PDF.
h1: Free Drywall Invoice Template & Example
subtitle: For drywall hangers, tapers and finishers: how to bill hanging, finishing levels, texture, patches and board by the square foot, so the customer sees what each coat cost.
intro_paragraph: Drywall is priced in square feet, but customers see walls, not square feet. A clear drywall invoice turns the job back into something they can picture: which rooms were hung, what finish level the walls were taped to, which ceilings got texture and how much board went up. That detail matters most when a painter arrives next and asks why a wall shows joints under raking light, or when a general contractor checks your bill against the square footage on the plans.
what_to_include_intro: A drywall invoice should let anyone check your measurements and your finish. Include these parts.
req_1_text: State the board area you hung and finished, ideally split by room or by walls and ceilings. Ceilings take longer, and many finishers charge more for them; showing them separately explains the price.
req_2_text: Name the finish level (Level 3 for texture, Level 4 for flat paint, Level 5 for a skim coat under critical lighting). It's the single line that prevents most arguments about how smooth the walls should be.
req_3_text: List the sheets by size and type: 1/2 inch regular, 5/8 inch Type X for garage firewalls, moisture-resistant board for bathrooms. Code-required fire board on a garage wall is worth naming on paper.
req_4_text: Corner bead, L-bead at windows, arches and texture (orange peel, knockdown, popcorn removal) all add time. Bill them as their own lines by the linear foot or square foot.
req_5_text: Small repairs are usually priced per patch or with a trip minimum, not per square foot. Say how many patches, roughly how big, and whether the price includes primer or matching texture.
req_6_text: Scrap board and mud buckets pile up fast. If disposal is extra, put it on its own line; if it's included, say so in the notes so the customer knows the dumpster was your cost.
what_to_include_outro: With square footage, finish level and materials on the page, the invoice also works as a record of what's behind the paint, which helps the next trade and any future buyer of the house.
sample_breakdown_intro: A basement finish: about 1,600 square feet of board on walls and ceilings, taped and finished to Level 4 for flat paint, with metal corner bead on the soffits and window returns. Tax rules vary; this example assumes a state that taxes the whole job at 6%.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Hang 1/2 in. drywall, walls and ceilings (labor)
Tape and finish to Level 4, three coats and sanding
Metal corner bead, soffits and window returns (installed)

sample_breakdown_notes: Finish level: Level 4, ready for primer and flat paint. Ceilings sprayed with no texture. Mechanical room left unfinished as agreed. Let the joint compound cure at least 24 hours before priming. Walls inspected with the homeowner on completion.

industry_notes.title: Per square foot or per board
industry_notes.text: Some crews price by the board hung, others by the square foot of finished wall. Pick one way and stick to it, and if you count boards, also show the square footage so a contractor can compare your bid with others.

industry_notes.title: Working under a general contractor
industry_notes.text: On new construction you often bill the GC, not the homeowner. Put the job address, the lot or unit number and the GC's purchase order on the invoice, and bill each phase (hang, then finish) if that's how the contract pays.

industry_notes.title: Taxes
industry_notes.text: States handle drywall differently: some tax repair labor, some treat new installation as a capital improvement that isn't taxed, and in many the contractor pays the tax when buying the board. Check your state's rule before you add tax to the invoice.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes drywall contractors make on invoices

mistakes.title: No finish level
mistakes.text: Writing 'tape and finish' without a level invites the customer to expect a Level 5 wall for a Level 3 price. Name the level on every finishing job.

mistakes.title: Hiding the ceilings
mistakes.text: Lumping overhead work into one wall price makes your rate look high. Split ceilings from walls so the extra labor is visible.

mistakes.title: Patch jobs with no minimum
mistakes.text: Three doorknob holes can eat half a day with drying time between coats. Show a trip or minimum charge instead of pricing small patches as if they took minutes.

pro_tip: Measure the room again on the day you finish and write the final square footage on the invoice, not the number from your bid. Change orders like an added closet or a soffit happen on almost every drywall job, and the final measurement is what both sides can check with a tape.
format_pdf_desc: A PDF keeps the square footage, finish level and board list fixed, so the general contractor or homeowner can file it with the permit papers and hand it to the painter without anything shifting.

faqs.question: What should a drywall invoice include?
faqs.answer: Your business name and license number if your state requires one, the customer and job address, the date, the square footage hung and finished by area, the finish level, board type and count, beads and texture, patches, disposal, tax where it applies, the total and your payment terms.

faqs.question: How do drywall contractors charge?
faqs.answer: Most charge per square foot of board, often with separate rates for hanging and for finishing, or per board hung. Repairs are usually per patch or a minimum per visit. Texture, Level 5 skim coats and high ceilings are priced as extras.

faqs.question: How do I invoice a drywall deposit?
faqs.answer: Send a separate invoice for the deposit when the job is booked. On the final invoice, show the deposit as its own line with a negative amount, or mention it in the notes, so the balance due is correct.

faqs.question: Is drywall installation taxable?
faqs.answer: It depends on the state and on whether the work is new construction or a repair. Some states tax the labor, some only the materials, and some treat installation as a non-taxable improvement. Check your state's rule and apply it the same way on every invoice.
