title: Masonry Invoice Template & Example (Free PDF) | Invoicor
meta_description: Free masonry invoice template for bricklayers and stone masons: a filled-in example with repointing, brick steps, matched brick and mortar. Download a PDF.
h1: Free Masonry Invoice Template & Example
subtitle: For bricklayers, block layers and stone masons: how to invoice repointing, rebuilds, new walls and materials by the square foot, the brick or the job.
intro_paragraph: Masonry lasts for decades, and so does the question of who did it and what was used. A masonry invoice is the place to record the mortar type, the brick or stone you matched, the area you repointed and the steps you rebuilt. Homeowners keep it for insurance and resale, historic districts may ask for it, and when a chimney needs work again in fifteen years, the next mason will want to know what's in the joints.
what_to_include_intro: A masonry invoice should describe the work as precisely as a mason would on site. Include these parts.
req_1_text: Name each structure: chimney, front steps, retaining wall, foundation, fireplace surround. Customers often book one repair and add another on site, so separate lines keep each one clear.
req_2_text: Square feet of wall face for repointing and veneer, linear feet for caps and copings, the count of courses or steps for rebuilds. Measured units let the customer check the bill against what they see.
req_3_text: The material, the count or tonnage, and whether it was matched to existing work, salvaged or new. Matching old brick takes time to source, and that effort belongs on the invoice.
req_4_text: Write the mortar type (Type N, S or a lime mortar for older soft brick). Using the wrong mortar on historic brick can damage it, so the record protects both you and the owner.
req_5_text: Scaffolding, a lift or a mixer rental for a tall chimney or a long wall are real costs. Bill them on their own line, by the day if the rental was by the day.
req_6_text: How long to keep traffic off new steps, when sealer can go on, and how to treat efflorescence if white salt appears. Put it in the notes so the customer has it in writing.
what_to_include_outro: Written this way, the invoice doubles as a small maintenance record for the house, which is exactly what a buyer's inspector asks for when they see fresh mortar.
sample_breakdown_intro: Two repairs on one house: repointing the upper part of a brick chimney and rebuilding three crumbling front steps with brick matched to the original. Tax rules vary; this example assumes a state that taxes the whole job at 5%.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Repoint chimney, grind out and refill joints above roofline
Rebuild brick front steps, 3 steps, 5 ft wide (labor)
Type N mortar, sand and masonry supplies

sample_breakdown_notes: Mortar: Type N, tinted to match. Keep foot traffic off the new steps for 3 days and don't use de-icing salt this winter. Light white haze (efflorescence) can appear in the first months; brush it off dry. Workmanship warranty: 2 years on the step rebuild.

industry_notes.title: Repairs versus new work
industry_notes.text: Repointing and tuckpointing are mostly labor and are usually priced per square foot, while a new wall or patio is priced by the job with materials listed. Keep the two kinds of work on separate lines even on one invoice.

industry_notes.title: Weather and phases
industry_notes.text: Mortar can't cure in freezing weather, so bigger jobs often stop and restart. If the contract pays by phase, invoice each finished phase and name it ('foundation walls complete') so the customer knows what they're paying for.

industry_notes.title: Taxes
industry_notes.text: Some states tax masonry repair labor, some only tax the materials, and some treat new masonry on a home as a capital improvement. Check your state's rule and keep it consistent across invoices.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes masons make on invoices

mistakes.title: One lump sum for everything
mistakes.text: 'Chimney and steps: $4,245' gives the customer nothing to check and nothing to keep. Split the structures and show the square feet and brick count.

mistakes.title: Leaving out the mortar
mistakes.text: Without the mortar type, the next mason has to guess. Write it on every invoice, especially for brick older than about 1930.

mistakes.title: Forgetting the sourcing time
mistakes.text: Hunting salvage yards for matching brick is part of the job. If it took a trip or two, bill it instead of absorbing it.

pro_tip: Keep a small sample of the matched brick and mortar color with the job name written on it, and note on the invoice that you have it. When the customer calls back for the other side of the chimney, you can match it again without a second search.
format_pdf_desc: Masonry outlives most paperwork, so a PDF that stays readable and unchanged is the right form: homeowners file it with the house records and hand it to an inspector or buyer years later.

faqs.question: What should a masonry invoice include?
faqs.answer: Your business name and license details where required, the customer and job address, the date, each structure worked on, measured quantities, the brick, block or stone used, the mortar type, equipment rental, tax where it applies, the total, care notes and your warranty.

faqs.question: How do masons charge for repointing?
faqs.answer: Most charge per square foot of wall face, with a higher rate for chimneys, tall walls or soft historic brick that has to be raked out by hand. Some charge by the day for small jobs. Say which method you used on the invoice.

faqs.question: How do I bill a deposit for a masonry job?
faqs.answer: Send a separate deposit invoice when the customer books, often to cover the brick and stone order. On the final invoice, list the deposit as a line with a negative amount, or note it, so the balance is right.

faqs.question: Can I use this as a bricklayer invoice template?
faqs.answer: Yes. Replace the repointing lines with your brick or block count, the wall area and the course height, and keep the mortar and materials lines. The same layout works for concrete block foundations and stone veneer.

faqs.question: Is this masonry invoice template free?
faqs.answer: Yes. Open it in the free online generator, edit the structures, quantities and prices, and download the PDF. With the Invoicor iPhone app you can save customers and your usual rates and duplicate a past invoice for a similar job.

h1: Free Fence Installation Invoice Template & Example
subtitle: For fence contractors and installers: how to invoice wood, vinyl, chain-link and aluminum fences by the linear foot, with gates, removal, permits and the deposit you already took.
intro_paragraph: Fences are sold by the linear foot, and nearly every fence job has a deposit, a gate or two and an old fence that has to go. A good fence installation invoice puts all of that in order: how many feet of which style and height, how many gates, what was torn out and hauled away, what the permit cost and how much the customer already paid. It's also a record of where the fence stands, which neighbors and future buyers sometimes care about more than the price.
what_to_include_intro: A fence invoice should match what the customer can walk and count in their yard. Include these parts.
req_1_text: The total run in feet with the material and height: '150 ft, 6 ft cedar board-on-board privacy'. If different sections use different styles, give each its own line.
req_2_text: Each gate with its width, single or double, and the hardware (self-closing hinges, a pool-code latch, a drop rod). Gates take far more labor per foot than the fence line, so price them separately.
req_3_text: Post size, spacing and how they were set (concrete, gravel, driven). Upgrades like 6x6 gate posts or steel posts in wood fences belong on their own line.
req_4_text: Tearing out an old fence, pulling old concrete footings, clearing brush along the line or hand-digging near utilities. Bill it per foot or as a flat fee and say what you hauled away.
req_5_text: City permit fees and HOA approval are often passed through at cost. Note that the line was marked through the 811 call-before-you-dig service before digging, with the ticket number if you have it.
req_6_text: Show the deposit paid as a credit so the balance is right, and add your workmanship warranty and the manufacturer's warranty on vinyl or aluminum panels.
what_to_include_outro: An invoice laid out this way answers the three calls fence companies get most: what did I pay for, what's left to pay, and is the gate sag covered.
sample_breakdown_intro: A backyard privacy fence replacing an old chain-link fence: 150 feet of 6-foot cedar with one walk gate. The customer paid a $2,000 deposit on a separate invoice when they signed. Tax rules vary; this example assumes a state where the installer pays sales tax on the lumber at purchase, so no tax is added to the customer's invoice.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: 6 ft cedar privacy fence, posts set in concrete every 8 ft (installed)
Walk gate, 4 ft wide, steel frame, self-closing hinges and latch
Remove and haul away old chain-link fence and footings
Upgrade to 6x6 posts, corners and gate
City fence permit (passed through at cost)

sample_breakdown_notes: Total job $5,965.00, less $2,000.00 deposit. Fence set 6 inches inside the property line per the survey pins the homeowner showed us. Utilities marked before digging. Let cedar weather 60 to 90 days before staining. Workmanship warranty: 2 years, including gate adjustment.

industry_notes.title: Deposits for materials
industry_notes.text: Most fence companies take a deposit at signing to order lumber or panels. Send it as its own invoice, then show it as a negative line on the final invoice so the customer sees the full job price and what's still due.

industry_notes.title: Property lines
industry_notes.text: Installers usually rely on the owner to show the line or provide a survey. Note on the invoice whose markers you used. If a neighbor disputes the fence later, that sentence matters.

industry_notes.title: Taxes
industry_notes.text: In many states a fence attached to the ground is treated as an improvement to real property, so the installer pays tax on materials instead of charging it. Other states tax the job or the materials separately. Check your state's rule before adding tax.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes fence contractors make on invoices

mistakes.title: Gates folded into the footage
mistakes.text: Pricing a double drive gate as 12 more feet of fence loses money. List each gate as its own line with its width and hardware.

mistakes.title: No credit for the deposit
mistakes.text: A final invoice that shows the full price without the deposit makes customers think they're being billed twice. Always show what was already paid.

mistakes.title: Removal left vague
mistakes.text: 'Remove old fence' without saying whether footings were pulled and debris hauled away leads to disputes about the leftover concrete. Spell out what you took.

pro_tip: Walk the finished fence with the customer and count the footage together before you send the invoice. Bids are often measured from a drawing, and a 140-foot run that turned into 150 feet around a tree is easy to agree on in the yard and hard to explain by text a week later.
format_pdf_desc: A PDF holds the footage, gate list and deposit credit exactly as you sent them, and HOAs and permit offices that ask for proof of the work accept a PDF without fuss.

faqs.question: What should a fence installation invoice include?
faqs.answer: Your business name and license number where required, the customer and property address, the date, linear feet with style and height, gates and hardware, post and footing details, removal of an old fence, permits, the deposit credit, tax where it applies, the balance due and your warranty.

faqs.question: How do fence companies charge?
faqs.answer: Usually per linear foot installed, with the price depending on material and height, plus a flat price per gate. Removal of an old fence is often per foot. Rocky soil, slopes and hand-digging near utilities are common extras.

faqs.question: How do I show the deposit on a fence invoice?
faqs.answer: Send a separate invoice for the deposit when the customer signs. On the final invoice, add the deposit as a line with a negative amount, or write it in the notes, so the balance due is correct.

faqs.question: Do I charge sales tax on fence installation?
faqs.answer: It depends on your state. Many treat an installed fence as a real property improvement where the contractor pays tax on the materials, while others tax the customer. Check your state's rule and keep it consistent.

h1: Free Pool Service Invoice Template & Example
subtitle: For pool cleaners and pool maintenance companies: how to invoice a month of weekly visits, chemicals, filter cleans, openings, closings and repairs on one clear bill.
intro_paragraph: Pool service is a route business: the same pools, the same day each week, and one invoice per customer at the end of the month. The hard part isn't the weekly visit, it's everything around it. A customer who sees $308 instead of the usual $160 wants to know why, and the answer (a filter clean, a phosphate treatment, a cracked O-ring) has to be on the invoice. A clear pool service invoice keeps the regular charge steady and makes every extra easy to understand.
what_to_include_intro: A pool service invoice should show the routine and the exceptions separately. Include these parts.
req_1_text: Name the plan (weekly full service, chemical-only, biweekly) and the month or dates it covers. The customer should see right away that this is the regular bill.
req_2_text: The number of visits with their dates. Months with five service days, or a skipped week for a storm, change the total, and listing the dates ends the question.
req_3_text: Say whether chlorine, acid and stabilizer are in the plan price. Extra treatments like algaecide, phosphate remover or a shock after a pool party go on their own lines.
req_4_text: Filter cartridge or DE cleans, salt cell cleaning, and repairs such as pump seals, O-rings or a new motor. List the part and the labor so the customer can tell maintenance from repair.
req_5_text: Free chlorine, pH and alkalinity from the last visit, or the range for the month. It shows the work behind the clear water and helps if a customer's plaster or liner ever becomes a warranty question.
req_6_text: Openings, closings, winterizing and green-to-clean recoveries are one-time jobs. Bill them separately from the monthly plan, with what was done (cover removed, lines blown out, plugs installed).
what_to_include_outro: Laid out this way, the invoice looks the same every month, so the extras stand out and the customer trusts the routine charge without asking.
sample_breakdown_intro: One month of weekly full service for a residential in-ground pool, plus a filter cartridge clean, a phosphate treatment and a pump lid O-ring replaced on site. Tax rules vary; this example taxes the whole invoice at 7%.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Filter cartridge clean, remove and hose all cartridges
Pump lid O-ring, part and installation

sample_breakdown_notes: Last visit readings: free chlorine 3 ppm, pH 7.5, alkalinity 90 ppm. Pump lid O-ring was cracked and drawing air; replaced. Filter pressure back to normal after the clean. Next filter clean recommended in about 3 months. Payment due by the 10th.

industry_notes.title: Monthly billing for weekly visits
industry_notes.text: Most pool companies bill once a month, either a flat monthly fee or a per-visit price times the visits. Per-visit billing is fairer in five-visit months; a flat fee is simpler. Tell new customers which one you use before the first bill.

industry_notes.title: Repairs need approval
industry_notes.text: Small parts are often replaced on the spot, but a pump motor or heater repair should be approved first. Mention on the invoice that the customer approved it, and when, for anything above the amount you agreed to fix without asking.

industry_notes.title: Taxes
industry_notes.text: States differ: some tax pool cleaning as a service, some tax only the chemicals and parts, and some tax neither for residential pools. Check your state's rule and apply it the same way every month.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes pool service companies make on invoices

mistakes.title: Extras without an explanation
mistakes.text: A bigger bill with no reason gets a phone call or a cancellation. Give each extra its own line and a word on why it was needed.

mistakes.title: No visit dates
mistakes.text: Customers who work all day never see you. Listing the dates of each visit shows they got what they pay for.

mistakes.title: Seasonal work mixed into the plan
mistakes.text: Hiding an opening or a green-pool recovery inside the monthly line makes the plan look like it went up. Bill one-time jobs on their own lines.

pro_tip: Send each customer's invoice on the same day every month, right after your last route day. Customers on a steady rhythm pay on a steady rhythm, and an invoice that always arrives on the first stops feeling like a surprise.
format_pdf_desc: Pool customers often forward the monthly PDF to a spouse, a landlord or an HOA, and a PDF arrives looking the same on every phone, with the visit dates and water readings intact.

faqs.question: What should a pool service invoice include?
faqs.answer: Your business name, the customer and pool address, the invoice date, the service plan and period, the visit dates, whether chemicals are included, extra treatments, filter cleans and repairs with parts, recent water readings, tax where it applies, the total and the due date.

faqs.question: How do I invoice weekly pool cleaning every month?

faqs.question: Should chemicals be listed separately on a pool invoice?
faqs.answer: If your plan includes routine chemicals, say so in the plan line and list only extra treatments such as algaecide, phosphate remover or shock. If you charge chemicals separately, list each product and quantity.

faqs.question: Is pool service taxable?
faqs.answer: It depends on the state. Some tax pool maintenance, some tax only the chemicals and parts, and some exempt residential service. Check your state's rule and keep it consistent on every invoice.

faqs.answer: Yes. Open the example in the free online generator, change the visits, extras and prices, and download the PDF. The Invoicor iPhone app keeps your route customers and your regular services saved for each month.

h1: Free Window Cleaning Invoice Template & Example
subtitle: For window cleaners working homes and storefronts: how to invoice per window or per pane, inside and outside, with screens, tracks, ladders and hard water stains.
intro_paragraph: Window cleaning prices are built from counts: how many windows, inside or outside or both, how many screens, which ones need a ladder. Customers rarely count their own windows, so an invoice that says '$443' with no breakdown looks like a guess. A good window cleaning invoice lists the count and the rate for each part of the job, shows the extras like hard water stain removal separately, and makes it easy for a homeowner to book the same job again next season, or for a shop owner to approve the monthly storefront route.
what_to_include_intro: A window cleaning invoice should let the customer count along. Include these parts.
req_1_text: Say whether you price per window, per pane or per side, and give the count. French panes and divided lites take longer, so say so if they were priced at a higher rate.
req_2_text: Exterior and interior cleaning are separate jobs with separate prices. Listing them on their own lines lets the customer drop or add one next time without asking for a new price.
req_3_text: Screen washing and track and sill detailing are the add-ons customers notice most. Give each a count and rate, and note any screens that were bent or torn before you started.
req_4_text: Second- and third-story windows, skylights and windows over a roof need ladders or a water-fed pole. If height changes your price, note which windows were high work.
req_5_text: Hard water stain removal, post-construction cleanup (paint, stickers, mortar) and glass protection coatings are priced per window or per hour. Bill them on their own lines.
req_6_text: For storefronts on a route, name the schedule (every two weeks, monthly) and the visit dates covered. For homes, a note like 'spring clean, next suggested in fall' sets up the next booking.
what_to_include_outro: With counts on the page, the invoice also becomes your quote for next time: same house, same windows, same lines, a new date.
sample_breakdown_intro: A spring clean for a two-story house with 28 standard windows, cleaned inside and outside, plus 24 screens, track detailing and stain removal on the back sliding door. Tax rules vary; this example assumes a state that taxes the service at 6%.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes window cleaners make on invoices

mistakes.title: One price for the whole house
mistakes.text: A single total hides the work and makes it hard to quote the same job later. List counts for windows, screens and tracks.

mistakes.text: Torn screens, cracked seals and fogged double panes get blamed on the last person who touched them. Write existing damage in the notes.

intro_paragraph: Pressure washing jobs are quoted by surface: so many square feet of siding, a driveway, a deck, the gutter faces. Customers see the result in an afternoon, but they don't always see the method, and soft washing vinyl with a low-pressure detergent is a different job from blasting concrete with a surface cleaner. A clear pressure washing invoice lists each surface, how it was cleaned and how it was measured, and records what couldn't be fully removed, like old rust or oil that soaked deep into the concrete.
what_to_include_intro: A pressure washing invoice should list each surface the way the customer will walk past it. Include these parts.

req_4_text: Deck and fence washing often includes a brightener and sometimes a sealer or stain. List the products and say how long the wood must dry before sealing if that's a separate visit.
req_5_text: If you used the customer's water spigot, say so; if you brought water for a commercial site, bill it. Note second-story work, roof access or moving furniture if they changed the price.
req_6_text: Mention that plants were pre-wet and rinsed, outlets and lights covered, and windows rinsed after the house wash. It shows care and answers the 'did you kill my hydrangeas' call before it happens.
what_to_include_outro: An invoice built this way tells the customer exactly what got clean, how, and what to expect next time, which is what brings them back every spring.

h1: Tree Service Invoice Template, Free and Filled In
subtitle: For arborists and tree removal crews: how to bill removals, pruning, stump grinding and cleanup so the homeowner sees exactly which tree got what.
intro_paragraph: Tree work is expensive, loud and very visible, so homeowners read the bill closely. They want to see which tree came down, whether the stump went with it and who hauled the wood away. A tree service invoice that names each tree, its size and the work done on it heads off the classic argument: 'I thought the stump was included.' It also gives the customer something to show their HOA, their insurer or the neighbor whose fence was near the drop zone.
what_to_include_intro: Bill tree work tree by tree. These are the parts a clear tree removal invoice needs.
req_1_text: Species, rough height or trunk diameter, and where it stands ('red oak, about 40 ft, back left corner by the shed'). On a property with a dozen trees, this is the only way to know which one the line refers to.
req_2_text: Removal, crown thinning, deadwood removal, raising the canopy, cabling. Keep the arborist terms but add a plain word or two, so the customer understands what a crown reduction actually was.
req_3_text: Most crews price stumps by the inch of diameter or per stump with a minimum. Write the diameter on the line and say how deep you ground and whether the grindings were left or removed.
req_4_text: Say whether brush was chipped on site, hauled away or left in a pile, and what happened to the logs: removed, cut to firewood length or stacked for the owner. This is the line customers most often assume.
req_5_text: Crane, bucket truck, rigging over a roof or a tight backyard with no truck access all change the price. A short note on the line explains why one removal costs twice another of the same height.
req_6_text: If the city required a removal permit, note the permit number and any fee you paid. Add your insurance or license details where your state or town asks for them, and note any lawn damage or ruts you agreed to repair.
what_to_include_outro: An invoice written tree by tree turns a big, scary number into a list of jobs the customer watched you do, which makes it much easier to pay.
sample_breakdown_intro: A residential job: one large oak removed near the house with rigging, its stump ground, a maple thinned, and all debris chipped and hauled away. Tax rules vary by state and town; this example adds 5% sales tax to the whole job.

sample_breakdown_notes: Stump grindings raked into the hole and left on site. Logs removed, no firewood kept. Small ruts by the side gate to be seeded at no charge on the next visit. Payment due within 14 days.

industry_notes.title: Storm work and emergency calls
industry_notes.text: After a storm, a tree on a roof or across a driveway is billed at a higher rate and often by the hour. Write the date and time of the call and the hours on site. If the homeowner plans an insurance claim, a clear, itemized invoice is what the adjuster will ask for.

industry_notes.title: Deposits on big removals
industry_notes.text: For crane jobs or multi-day removals, many crews ask for a deposit to book the crew and equipment. Send a separate invoice for the deposit, then show it on the final invoice as a negative line or in the notes, so the balance is easy to check.

industry_notes.title: Taxes
industry_notes.text: Whether tree trimming and removal are taxable depends on the state; some treat it as landscaping service, others as nontaxable labor. Check your state's rule once and apply it the same way on every tree service invoice.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes tree services make on invoices

mistakes.title: Stump left vague
mistakes.text: 'Tree removal' with no word about the stump is the most common dispute in the trade. Put stump grinding on its own line or say 'stump left at grade'.

mistakes.title: No tree descriptions
mistakes.text: Lines like 'Tree #2' mean nothing a month later. Name the species and location so the customer, and you, can match the bill to the yard.

mistakes.title: Forgetting cleanup terms
mistakes.text: If the logs stay or the chips stay, say so. Customers who expected a spotless yard will call back and ask for a discount.

pro_tip: Walk the property with the customer before you start and write the tree list in their words ('the big one by the swing set'). Use the same names on the invoice. When the bill matches the walk-through, there's nothing left to argue about.
format_pdf_desc: A PDF keeps your per-tree lines and cleanup terms exactly as written, which matters when the homeowner forwards the bill to an insurer, an HOA or a property manager. It also prints cleanly for customers who still pay tree crews by check.

faqs.question: What should a tree service invoice include?
faqs.answer: Your business name and contact details, any license or insurance details your area asks for, the customer and job address, the date, each tree with species, size and location, the work done on it, stump grinding, debris and wood handling, permit fees, tax where it applies, the total and your payment terms.

faqs.question: How do tree services charge for stump grinding?
faqs.answer: Usually by the inch of diameter measured at ground level, often with a minimum per stump, or a flat price per stump. Whatever you use, write the diameter and the depth on the invoice so the price is easy to check.

faqs.question: Should I charge a deposit for tree removal?
faqs.answer: Many crews do for large or crane jobs. Send one invoice for the deposit, then a final invoice that lists the full job and subtracts the deposit as a negative line or mentions it in the notes.

faqs.question: Is tree removal taxable?
faqs.answer: It depends on where you work. Some states tax tree and landscaping services, others don't, and a few treat storm cleanup differently. Check your state's rule and keep it consistent across invoices.

intro_paragraph: Snow removal is billed in bursts. Nothing for weeks, then three storms in five days and a parking lot that needs plowing at 4 a.m. before the store opens. A snow removal invoice that lists each storm date, each push and every bag of salt is the record both you and the client rely on, especially for commercial lots where slip-and-fall claims make documentation matter.
what_to_include_intro: Whether you charge per push or per season, a snow plowing invoice should cover these parts.
req_1_text: List each date you serviced the property, and the time if the contract has an open-by deadline. Property managers compare this against their own weather records and security cameras.
req_2_text: Per push, per inch trigger (for example, plow at 2 in or more), hourly or seasonal flat rate. Say which one on the invoice, so a client on a per-push contract understands why a snowy February costs more than January.

req_4_text: Rock salt, treated salt or calcium chloride, by the bag, by the ton or per application. Materials are a real cost, and clients notice when the line is missing and the walks are still icy.
req_5_text: After a big storm, snow may need to be moved with a loader or trucked off site. This is usually billed by the hour and should be its own line, separate from the normal push.
req_6_text: For seasonal contracts, name the season (for example, November 1 to March 31) and which installment this invoice is. For per-push clients, give the billing period the invoice covers.
what_to_include_outro: With dates, areas and materials on the page, a snow invoice stops being 'plowing, $1,300' and becomes a log the client can check in two minutes.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes snow removal contractors make on invoices

mistakes.title: No storm dates

h1: Locksmith Invoice Template and Receipt Example
subtitle: For mobile and shop locksmiths: how to bill lockouts, rekeys, lock changes and key cutting, with the call-out fee and hardware listed so nobody feels overcharged.
intro_paragraph: A locksmith often meets the customer at the worst moment of their day: locked out in the rain, or just back from a break-in. They agreed to a price on the phone and they'll compare it to the bill. Locksmithing also has a reputation problem with bait-and-switch operators, so an honest, itemized locksmith invoice is one of the best ways to show you're the real thing. It also doubles as the receipt the customer needs for a landlord, a renter's insurance claim or their own records.
what_to_include_intro: A clear locksmith invoice or receipt separates the trip, the labor and the hardware. Include these parts.
req_1_title: Service call and time of day
req_1_text: The trip charge, and whether it was a regular, after-hours, weekend or holiday call. Write the time you arrived; it explains an after-hours rate without a conversation.
req_2_text: Lockout (car, home or commercial), rekey, lock change, lock repair, safe opening, master key system. Say whether entry was non-destructive or the lock had to be drilled.

req_4_text: Brand, model, finish and grade for any lock, deadbolt or smart lock you installed. Customers need this for warranty claims, and landlords want to know what's on their doors.
req_5_text: How many keys, of what kind: standard, high-security, restricted keyway or transponder car keys. Car key programming is its own line, since the blank and the programming are priced differently.
req_6_text: Many locksmiths note that ID or proof of residence was checked before opening a lockout. Add your license number where your state licenses locksmiths, and the vehicle VIN for car key work.
what_to_include_outro: With trip, labor and hardware separated, the customer can see the phone quote in the bill, and you have a record if anyone later asks why you opened that door.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes locksmiths make on invoices

mistakes.title: One lump sum
mistakes.text: 'Lockout and rekey, $338' looks like the bait-and-switch customers fear. Itemize the call, the labor and the parts.

h1: Appliance Repair Invoice Template with a Filled-In Example
subtitle: For appliance repair technicians: how to bill the diagnostic, the parts and the labor, with the model, serial and fault details customers and warranty companies ask for.
intro_paragraph: When a fridge stops cooling or a washer won't drain, the customer is paying to get back to normal and wants to know it was worth fixing instead of replacing. An appliance repair invoice that names the machine, the fault you found, the parts with their numbers and the time it took answers that question. It's also the paper a home warranty company, a landlord or the manufacturer will ask for if the same appliance fails again.
what_to_include_intro: Appliance repair is diagnostic work plus parts. A good repair technician invoice covers these parts.
req_1_text: Type of appliance, brand, model number and serial number from the rating plate. It identifies the exact machine, matters for warranty and recall checks, and saves time if you come back.
req_2_text: What the customer reported ('fridge warm, freezer frosted over') and what you found ('failed defrost heater, ice blocking evaporator fan'). This is the line that shows the customer what they paid for.
req_3_text: Most technicians charge a fixed fee to come out and diagnose, and some credit it toward the repair if the customer goes ahead. If you credit it, show the credit on the invoice instead of just leaving the fee off.
req_4_text: Each part on its own line with the manufacturer part number and price. Customers can look parts up online, so honest part lines with numbers build trust better than a single 'parts' total.
req_5_text: Hours or a flat repair price, depending on how you charge. If a second visit was needed because a part had to be ordered, say so and show whether the return trip was charged.
req_6_text: How long your labor is guaranteed and what the parts warranty is. Say clearly that the warranty covers the repaired fault, not the whole appliance.
what_to_include_outro: With the machine, the fault and the parts on paper, the customer can see the repair made sense, and you have the history ready if they call about the same model next year.

industry_notes.title: Home warranty and third-party jobs
industry_notes.text: When a home warranty company dispatches you, the customer often pays a service fee and the company pays the rest under its own terms. Keep the claim or dispatch number in the notes and follow the company's billing rules; send the homeowner only what they owe.

industry_notes.title: Parts ordered, second visit
industry_notes.text: Many repairs need a part that isn't on the truck. Some technicians bill the diagnostic on the first visit and the parts and labor after the return trip; others bill once at the end. Pick one way and explain it to the customer up front.

industry_notes.title: Taxes
industry_notes.text: Most states tax parts as goods, and some also tax repair labor on tangible property while others exempt it. Invoicor applies one tax rate per invoice, so check your state's rule and how your accountant wants parts and labor shown.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes appliance repair techs make on invoices

mistakes.title: No model or serial number
mistakes.text: Without them, a warranty claim or recall check is guesswork, and on a callback you can't confirm it's the same machine. Copy them from the rating plate every time.

mistakes.title: A single 'parts' line
mistakes.text: Customers who look up a part online and find it cheaper start doubting the whole bill. List each part with its number; your price can include your handling, just be clear.

mistakes.title: Diagnostic fee left unexplained
mistakes.text: If the customer decides not to repair, they still owe the diagnostic. Say so before you start, and put it on the invoice as its own line.

pro_tip: Write down the model and serial number before you open the panel, and type them into the invoice notes while you wait for the test cycle. On a callback, your past invoice for that machine tells you exactly which parts went in and when.
format_pdf_desc: Home warranty companies, landlords and manufacturers ask for repair records in a fixed format. A PDF holds the model number, part numbers and warranty terms exactly as written and opens on any phone or office computer.

faqs.question: What should an appliance repair invoice include?
faqs.answer: Your business details, the customer and address, the date, the appliance type, brand, model and serial number, the reported problem and your diagnosis, the diagnostic fee, each part with its part number, labor, tax where it applies, the total, payment terms and your warranty.

faqs.question: Can I use this as an appliance repair receipt?
faqs.answer: Yes. If the customer pays on the spot, mark the invoice as paid and share the PDF; it then serves as the receipt. In the Invoicor app you can set its status to paid, so your own records match.

faqs.question: Should the diagnostic fee be credited toward the repair?
faqs.answer: That's your choice. Many technicians credit it if the customer goes ahead with the repair. If you do, keep the fee on the invoice and add the credit as a negative line, so the customer sees the saving.

faqs.question: Is appliance repair taxable?
faqs.answer: Parts are taxable in most states; repair labor is taxed in some states and exempt in others. Check your state's rule, and since an invoice uses one tax rate, ask your accountant how to show mixed parts and labor.

faqs.question: Can I use this appliance repair invoice template for free?
faqs.answer: Yes. Open the example in the free online generator, enter your appliance, parts and labor and download the PDF. The Invoicor iPhone app saves your common parts and labor rates for the next call.

h1: Junk Removal Invoice Template and Hauling Example
subtitle: For junk haulers and cleanout crews: how to bill by truckload volume, add the item fees disposal sites charge you, and show what went where.
intro_paragraph: Junk removal is priced on something the customer can't measure: how much of your truck their stuff filled. That makes the invoice the moment of truth. A junk removal invoice that states the load size, lists the items with special disposal fees and notes the extras like stairs or a long carry turns 'that seems like a lot' into 'that makes sense.' It also gives estate executors, landlords and realtors the itemized paper they need for their own accounts.
what_to_include_intro: Show the volume, the special items and the labor. A hauling invoice template should include these parts.
req_1_text: Quarter, half, three-quarter or full truckload, with the cubic yards if you know them ('half load, about 7.5 cu yd'). Volume is the core of the price, so make it the first line.
req_2_text: A short list of the main items: couch, dresser, boxes, yard waste, construction debris. It shows the customer you took everything you agreed to, and it settles any question about a forgotten item.
req_3_text: Mattresses, tires, refrigerators and freezers (refrigerant), TVs and electronics, paint. Landfills and recyclers charge extra for these, and many towns have rules for them. Give each its own line.
req_4_text: Stair carries, long walks from the door to the truck, disassembly of furniture or a shed, or a crew working several hours in a hoarding cleanout. Name each extra so it doesn't look like a hidden fee.
req_5_text: Where the load went: landfill, transfer station, recycler or donation center. Many customers care that usable furniture was donated, and some ask for a donation receipt for their taxes.
req_6_text: Cleanouts are often paid by someone who wasn't there: an estate, a property manager or a realtor. The job address and date on the invoice let them match the bill to the property.
what_to_include_outro: An invoice that shows volume, items and extras is easy to approve, even for the executor or landlord who never saw the pile.
sample_breakdown_intro: A garage and spare bedroom cleanout: half a truckload of household items, two mattress sets, an old refrigerator, four tires and a two-flight stair carry. Tax rules vary; many states don't tax hauling services, and this example charges no sales tax.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Half truckload, approx. 7.5 cu yd (furniture, boxes, garage items)
Mattress or box spring disposal fee

sample_breakdown_notes: Dresser, bookshelf and two chairs donated to a local thrift store. Refrigerator taken to a certified appliance recycler. Remaining load to the county transfer station. Garage swept after loading. Payment due on completion.

industry_notes.title: Quote on site, confirm on the invoice
industry_notes.text: Most haulers give a price after seeing the pile, then load. If the load turned out bigger or smaller than quoted, adjust the volume line and say why. Customers accept a change they can see in the truck.

industry_notes.title: Estate and rental cleanouts
industry_notes.text: Estates, landlords and realtors often pay by check after the job and need the property address and an itemized bill for their records. For multi-day cleanouts, invoice each day or each load so the balance doesn't surprise anyone.

industry_notes.title: Taxes
industry_notes.text: Many states don't charge sales tax on junk hauling, but some tax waste removal services or add local disposal surcharges. Check your state's rule and your county's, and apply them the same way every time.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes junk removal companies make on invoices

mistakes.title: No load size
mistakes.text: A total with no volume feels made up. Always state the fraction of the truck or the cubic yards.

mistakes.title: Hidden item fees
mistakes.text: Adding $80 for mattresses without a line for it looks like padding. Itemize every special-disposal fee.

mistakes.title: No disposal details
mistakes.text: Customers increasingly ask where their stuff went. A note on donations and recycling answers it and sets you apart from the cheapest crew.

pro_tip: Save your load sizes and item fees as products: quarter, half, three-quarter and full truck, mattress, tire, fridge, stairs. With the truck loaded, you build the invoice in a minute while the customer is still standing in the empty garage, which is the best moment to get paid.
format_pdf_desc: Estate executors, property managers and realtors keep junk removal bills with the property's paperwork. A PDF shows the load size, item fees and disposal notes exactly as written, and it prints cleanly for whoever cuts the check.

faqs.question: What should a junk removal invoice include?
faqs.answer: Your business details, the customer and job address, the date, the load size, a short list of items removed, special disposal fees (mattresses, tires, appliances), labor extras like stairs, where the load went, tax where it applies, the total and payment terms.

faqs.question: How do junk removal companies price a job?
faqs.answer: Most price by the volume of the truck the load fills, from a minimum load to a full truck, plus fees for items that cost more to dispose of. Some price by weight or by the hour for heavy cleanouts.

faqs.question: Should I charge extra for mattresses, tires and appliances?
faqs.answer: Most haulers do, because landfills and recyclers charge more for them. Put each on its own line so the customer sees it's a disposal cost, not a markup.

faqs.question: Is junk removal taxable?
faqs.answer: In many states hauling isn't taxed, but some states tax waste removal and some counties add disposal surcharges. Check the rules where you work and keep them consistent on every invoice.

title: Carpet Cleaning Invoice Template & Example | Invoicor

h1: Carpet Cleaning Invoice Template with Upholstery Example
subtitle: For carpet and upholstery cleaners: how to bill by room or square foot, add stairs, spot treatment and protector, and set honest expectations about stains.
intro_paragraph: Carpet cleaning isn't house cleaning. You bring a truck-mounted or portable extraction unit, price by the room or the square foot, and the customer judges the result on one or two stains they've stared at for months. A carpet cleaning invoice that lists every room, the stairs, the spot and pet treatments and any upholstery makes the price easy to follow. It also records which stains were treated and which were permanent, before the customer forgets you warned them.
what_to_include_intro: Rooms, extras and stain notes are what customers read. A carpet cleaning invoice should cover these parts.
req_1_text: Either a count of rooms with a size limit ('up to 200 sq ft each') or the total square feet. Name the rooms, so a family that thinks the hallway was a room can see how you counted.
req_2_text: Hot water extraction (steam cleaning), low-moisture encapsulation, or dry compound. The method affects drying time and price, and some carpet warranties ask for a specific one.
req_3_text: Stairs are slow, hand-tool work and are usually priced per step. Put the step count on the line rather than folding them into a room price.
req_4_text: Pet urine enzyme treatment, red drink or coffee stains, rust or wax removal. Price them per spot or per area, and say on the invoice which ones came out and which may have set permanently.
req_5_text: Sofas, loveseats, chairs, mattresses and area rugs are priced per piece or per square foot. Note the fabric type when it matters, since some fabrics can only be cleaned dry.
req_6_text: Carpet protector applied by square foot, expected drying time and what to avoid: furniture back on carpet only with tabs or blocks, no walking in socks on wet areas. These notes save you a callback.
what_to_include_outro: An invoice that counts the rooms and names the stains tells the customer you looked closely, and that's what earns the next booking in six months.
sample_breakdown_intro: A house with pets: four carpeted rooms and a staircase cleaned with hot water extraction, three pet spots treated, a three-seat sofa cleaned and protector applied. Tax rules vary; this example adds 7% sales tax to the whole job.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Hot water extraction, room up to 200 sq ft (living, hall, 2 bedrooms)
Pet urine enzyme treatment, per spot

sample_breakdown_notes: Drying time 6 to 10 hours; keep windows open or fans on. Furniture set on protective tabs; leave them 24 hours. Bedroom 2 spot near the closet faded but not fully removed (old dye stain, likely permanent). Payment due on completion.

industry_notes.title: Minimums and coupon pricing
industry_notes.text: Many carpet cleaners advertise a low per-room price with a job minimum. If the minimum applies, show it as its own line so the customer sees why three small rooms cost the same as four.

industry_notes.title: Rental move-outs and property managers
industry_notes.text: Tenants and landlords often need a dated carpet cleaning invoice to settle a security deposit. Put the unit address and move-out date on it, and the property manager's work order number if they ordered the job.

industry_notes.title: Taxes
industry_notes.text: Some states tax carpet and upholstery cleaning as a service, others don't, and protector sold as a product may be treated differently. Check your state's rule and apply it the same way on every invoice.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes carpet cleaners make on invoices

mistakes.title: Not defining a room
mistakes.text: If a room means up to 200 sq ft, say so. Otherwise a big open living area turns into an argument about whether it's one room or three.

mistakes.title: Promising stains will come out
mistakes.text: Writing 'stain removal' implies a guarantee. Write 'spot treatment' and note the result, especially on old pet and dye stains.

mistakes.title: Skipping the care notes
mistakes.text: Rust marks from furniture put back too early often get blamed on the cleaner. A line about drying time and furniture tabs protects you.

pro_tip: Before you start, walk the rooms with the customer and agree on which spots are the priority. Write those spots into the invoice notes with the result. Customers who see their worst stain mentioned by name know you paid attention, and they book again.
format_pdf_desc: Tenants hand carpet cleaning invoices to landlords to get their security deposit back, and landlords keep them with the unit's file. A dated PDF with the rooms and address listed can't be edited and is accepted as proof the job was done.

faqs.question: What should a carpet cleaning invoice include?
faqs.answer: Your business details, the customer and address, the date, the rooms or square footage, the cleaning method, stairs, spot and pet treatments, upholstery or rugs, protector, any minimum charge, tax where it applies, the total, and drying and care notes.

faqs.question: Should I charge carpet cleaning by the room or by the square foot?
faqs.answer: Room pricing is easier for homeowners to understand; square-foot pricing is fairer for large or open spaces and common for commercial work. If you price by the room, state the size limit on the invoice.

faqs.question: How do I invoice upholstery cleaning?
faqs.answer: Add each piece as its own line: sofa, loveseat, chair, ottoman or mattress, with the fabric type if it affects the method. The same invoice can hold carpet and upholstery work.

faqs.question: Is carpet cleaning taxable?
faqs.answer: It depends on the state. Some tax carpet and upholstery cleaning, others treat it as a nontaxable service. Check your state's rule and keep the same tax setting on every invoice.

faqs.answer: Yes. Open the example in the free online generator, change the rooms and prices and download the PDF. The Invoicor iPhone app saves your room, stair and treatment prices, so repeat customers take a minute to invoice.

h1: Free Interior Design Invoice Template & Example
subtitle: For interior designers and decorators: how to bill design hours, furniture and fabric purchases, markup, deposits and delivery so clients see exactly what they paid for.
intro_paragraph: Interior design clients pay for two very different things: your time and taste, and the sofa, rug and drapery you order for them. When both land on one vague invoice, clients start asking what the markup was or why a lamp cost more than the one they saw online. A clear interior designer invoice separates design fees from purchased goods, names every piece with its room and vendor, and shows the deposit you took when you placed the order. That clarity protects your margin and makes the next project easier to sell.
what_to_include_intro: Whether you bill hourly, a flat design fee or cost plus markup, an interior design invoice should cover these parts.
req_1_text: Name the project ('Hughes residence, living and dining') and, on each line, the room the item is for. When an order spans six rooms and four vendors, room labels are how the client checks the invoice against the design board.
req_2_title: Design fees, by phase or hour
req_2_text: Bill concept, space planning, selections and installation days as phases or as hours with a rate. If you agreed a flat fee in the letter of agreement, show which installment this is (for example, 'design fee, 2 of 3').
req_3_text: For each piece: the item, size, finish or fabric, and quantity. 'Sofa, 96 in, performance linen, oatmeal' is something the client recognizes when it arrives; 'upholstery' is not.
req_4_text: Say whether goods are billed at retail, at net cost plus a stated markup, or at net cost with a procurement fee. Whichever you choose, use the same method across the whole project, as your agreement describes.
req_5_text: Freight from the vendor, the receiving warehouse fee, storage while the room is not ready, and white-glove delivery and placement. These costs are real and easy to forget until they eat the markup.
req_6_text: Show the deposit already paid for ordered goods and note that custom pieces (made-to-order upholstery, cut fabric, custom drapery) usually can't be cancelled or returned once ordered.
what_to_include_outro: An invoice built this way reads like a summary of the design itself: room by room, piece by piece, with no surprises about where the money went.
sample_breakdown_intro: A furnishing invoice for a living room: a custom sofa and wool rug billed at net cost plus 20%, custom drapery, a pair of side tables, and receiving and delivery, with the furnishing deposit paid at order. Design hours were billed on a separate invoice. Tax rules vary; this example taxes the whole furnishing invoice at 7%.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Living room: sofa, 96 in, performance linen (net $3,200 + 20%)
Living room: area rug, 9 x 12 ft, hand-knotted wool (net $950 + 20%)
Custom drapery panels, lined, with rod and hardware

sample_breakdown_notes: Custom sofa and drapery are made to order and non-returnable. Rug may shed for the first few weeks; vacuum without a beater bar. Storage after 30 days at the receiving warehouse is billed at $45 per month. Design hours for September are on invoice 1042.

industry_notes.title: Separate fees from goods
industry_notes.text: Many designers send design hours on one invoice and furnishings on another. It keeps the conversation about your time apart from the conversation about product, and it helps when only one of them is taxable. Invoicor uses one tax rate per invoice, so splitting them also keeps the tax line right.

industry_notes.title: Markup and trade pricing
industry_notes.text: Whether you show net cost and markup or a single client price is a business choice, but it should match what your letter of agreement says. If you promised to pass on trade discounts, show the net price on the line, as in the example above.

industry_notes.title: Sales tax and resale certificates
industry_notes.text: In many states, furniture and fabric you resell to a client are taxable, and designers buy them tax-free from vendors with a resale certificate. Design services themselves are taxed in some states and not in others. Check your state's rule and ask your accountant before the first big order.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes interior designers make on invoices

mistakes.title: Ordering before the deposit clears
mistakes.text: A custom sofa you can't cancel becomes your problem if the client changes their mind. Invoice the furnishing deposit first and place the order once it's paid.

mistakes.title: Hiding freight and receiving
mistakes.text: Freight, warehouse receiving and delivery crews can add hundreds of dollars per room. List them as their own lines, or your markup quietly pays for them.

mistakes.title: Vague item names
mistakes.text: 'Accessories, $1,200' invites questions. Name each piece or group by room, so the client can match the invoice to what's in their home.

pro_tip: Keep your standard fees (design hour, installation day, receiving per piece, delivery per room) as saved products in the app. Each furnishing invoice then starts from the same building blocks, and only the pieces and their prices change from project to project.
format_pdf_desc: Furnishing invoices often run to many lines and several pages, and clients forward them to a partner or an accountant. A PDF keeps every room, item and markup line exactly where you put it, on any screen or printer.

faqs.question: What should an interior design invoice include?
faqs.answer: Your business name and contact, the client and project address, the invoice number and date, design fees by phase or hour, each furnishing item with room, size and finish, your pricing method (retail or net plus markup), freight and delivery, tax where it applies, deposits already paid, the balance due and your payment terms.

faqs.question: How do interior designers bill for furniture?
faqs.answer: The common methods are retail price, net (trade) cost plus a markup, or net cost plus a separate procurement fee. Pick the one your agreement names and use it on every line. Invoice a deposit before you order custom pieces, then bill the balance on delivery.

faqs.question: How do I invoice a deposit for furnishings?
faqs.answer: Send a separate invoice for the deposit when the client approves the selections. When the pieces are delivered, send the final invoice and show the deposit as a line with a negative amount, or mention it in the notes, so the balance is clear.

faqs.question: Do interior designers charge sales tax?
faqs.answer: Usually on furnishings and other goods you resell, in states with sales tax. Design fees are taxed in some states and exempt in others, and the rules for installation vary too. Check your state's rule; billing fees and goods on separate invoices makes it easier to apply.

faqs.question: Can I use this interior design invoice template for free?
faqs.answer: Yes. Open the example in the free online generator, replace the rooms and items with your project and download the PDF. The Invoicor iPhone app also saves your clients and standard fees, so the next room's invoice takes a few minutes.

h1: Free Remodeling Invoice Template for Home Renovation
subtitle: For remodelers and renovation contractors: how to invoice kitchens, bathrooms and additions in stages, with change orders, allowances and payments already received.
intro_paragraph: A remodel is a long job with a lot of money moving in stages: a deposit at signing, payments as the cabinets go in and the counters are templated, and a final bill at the walkthrough. Homeowners are living in the mess the whole time, so every invoice gets read closely. A good home renovation invoice ties each charge to the contract, lists change orders separately with their own approval, and shows what has already been paid. That way the final invoice is a formality instead of a negotiation.
what_to_include_intro: A kitchen remodel invoice, a bathroom renovation invoice or a basement finish all need the same core parts.
req_1_text: Your contractor license number (many states require it on paperwork), the contract date and the job address. It ties the invoice to the signed scope the homeowner agreed to.
req_2_text: Say which payment this is: 'Progress payment 2 of 4, cabinets installed'. Milestones tied to visible work are easier for homeowners to approve than percentages of an abstract total.
req_3_text: Break the work into demolition, framing, plumbing, electrical, cabinets, countertops, tile and paint. Use units where they fit: linear feet of cabinets, square feet of tile or counter.
req_4_text: Each change order gets its own line with its number and the date it was approved. Moving a sink 18 inches is a small sentence and a real cost; keep it visible.
req_5_text: If the contract had an allowance for tile, fixtures or appliances, show the allowance, what the homeowner actually picked and the difference, up or down.
req_6_text: List the deposit and earlier progress payments with dates, then the balance due now. Add lien waiver or warranty notes if you provide them at final payment.
what_to_include_outro: With these parts in place, the homeowner can hold the invoice next to the contract and see that every dollar has a reason.
sample_breakdown_intro: The final invoice for a mid-size kitchen remodel: demolition, 22 linear feet of cabinets, quartz countertops, a tile backsplash, lighting by a licensed electrician and one approved change order, less the deposit and first progress payment. Tax rules for remodeling vary; in this example the contractor paid sales tax on materials when buying them and charges none to the homeowner.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Demolition and haul-off, existing cabinets and flooring
Cabinets, shaker style, supply and install
Quartz countertops, template, fabricate and install
Under-cabinet lighting and 4 GFCI outlets (licensed electrician)
Change order #1 (approved Oct 2): relocate sink 18 in

sample_breakdown_notes: Final payment due within 7 days of the walkthrough. Punch list completed Oct 28. Workmanship warranty: 1 year from completion; cabinet and countertop manufacturer warranties apply separately. Lien waivers from the electrician and countertop fabricator provided with this invoice.

industry_notes.title: Deposit limits
industry_notes.text: Some states limit how much a contractor can take up front on a home improvement contract. California, for example, caps the down payment at $1,000 or 10% of the contract price, whichever is less. Check your state before you set your payment schedule.

industry_notes.title: One invoice per stage
industry_notes.text: Bill each milestone on its own invoice as the work is done. In the Invoicor app you can duplicate the previous progress invoice, change the stage and amounts, and keep the same client and job details.

industry_notes.title: Tax on remodeling work
industry_notes.text: In many states a contractor improving real property pays sales tax on materials and doesn't charge it on the job; in others, parts of the work are taxable to the homeowner. The rules differ a lot. Ask your accountant and check your state's rule once, then apply it the same way every time.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes remodelers make on invoices

mistakes.title: Verbal change orders
mistakes.text: 'Sure, we can move the sink' turns into a dispute at the end. Write each change order down, get it approved before the work, and give it its own line on the invoice.

mistakes.title: Billing ahead of the work
mistakes.text: Asking for the cabinet payment before the cabinets are in damages trust and, in some states, breaks the rules. Tie each payment to work the homeowner can see.

mistakes.title: Forgetting allowance overages
mistakes.text: When the homeowner picks tile above the allowance, the difference has to show up somewhere. Track selections against allowances as you go, not at the final walkthrough.

pro_tip: Number your change orders and keep a short list of them in the invoice notes of every progress invoice: number, description, amount, approved date. The homeowner sees the running total grow in small steps, so nothing feels sudden on the final bill.
format_pdf_desc: Remodeling invoices end up in a homeowner's files next to the contract, and sometimes with a lender or an insurance adjuster. A PDF can't be altered by accident and prints the same as you sent it.

faqs.question: What should a remodeling invoice include?
faqs.answer: Your business name and contractor license number, the homeowner and job address, the contract date, the stage being billed, the work by trade with units, change orders with their numbers and approval dates, allowance differences, payments already received, the balance due, terms and warranty notes.

faqs.question: How do contractors bill for a kitchen remodel?
faqs.answer: Usually with a deposit at signing (within your state's limit), progress payments at milestones such as rough-in, cabinet install and countertop install, and a final payment after the walkthrough. Each stage gets its own invoice that lists what was done.

faqs.question: How do I show the deposit on the final remodeling invoice?
faqs.answer: Send the deposit as its own invoice at signing. On the final invoice, list the deposit and each earlier progress payment as a line with a negative amount, or in the notes, so the balance due is easy to check.

faqs.question: Do I charge sales tax on a home renovation?
faqs.answer: It depends on the state. In many, contractors pay tax on materials and don't charge it on the finished job; elsewhere some labor or materials are taxable to the customer. Check your state's rule with your accountant before you invoice.

faqs.answer: Yes. Open the example in the free online generator, change the scope and amounts to your job and download the PDF. The Invoicor iPhone app saves your clients and standard line items, and you can duplicate each progress invoice to start the next one.

h1: Free Garage Door Repair Invoice Template & Example
subtitle: For garage door technicians and installers: how to invoice service calls, spring replacements, openers and new doors, with the part specs and warranties homeowners ask about.
intro_paragraph: Most garage door calls start with a loud bang and a car stuck inside. The homeowner wants the door working today, and they will pay, but they also wonder afterward whether $600 was fair. A garage door repair invoice answers that by naming exactly what was replaced: spring size and cycle rating, how many rollers, which cables, and what the opener needed. Clear parts lines and a written warranty turn a stressful emergency into a customer who calls you again when the opener finally dies.
what_to_include_intro: Repair, tune-up or full installation, a garage door invoice works best with these parts.
req_1_text: The trip charge or diagnostic fee, and whether it's waived or credited when the customer approves the repair. Say it plainly so the customer knows what they'd pay if they said no.
req_2_text: Torsion or extension, wire size, length and cycle rating ('pair, 0.225 x 30 in, 10,000 cycles'). Specs back up the price and tell the next technician what's on the door.
req_3_text: Rollers, cables, drums, hinges, bearings and weather seal, each with a count. A list of small parts is more convincing than one 'hardware' line.
req_4_text: Brand and model of a new opener, or what was done to the old one: logic board, gear kit, sensor alignment, remote and keypad programming.
req_5_text: Labor as hours or a flat repair price, plus any evening, weekend or holiday surcharge. If emergency rates apply, state the rate the customer agreed to on the phone.
req_6_text: Note the balance test, auto-reverse and photo-eye checks you did, and the warranty on parts and labor, with periods for each.
what_to_include_outro: That level of detail takes a minute to write and saves a long phone call when the customer's neighbor says they paid less.
sample_breakdown_intro: A broken torsion spring on a two-car door: the service call, a matched pair of springs, labor to install and balance, new rollers and lift cables, and a safety check of the opener. Tax rules vary; this example taxes the whole invoice at 6%.

Labor: spring replacement and door balance
Photo-eye realignment and opener force test

sample_breakdown_notes: Door: 16 x 7 ft steel, insulated. Both springs replaced as a pair. Auto-reverse and photo-eye tested and working. Warranty: springs 3 years, rollers and cables 1 year, labor 90 days. Lubricate rollers and hinges every 6 months.

industry_notes.title: Flat-rate price books
industry_notes.text: Many garage door companies quote flat prices per repair (spring pair, cable set, roller set) instead of hourly labor. If you work that way, keep the line names the same on every invoice so customers and your techs see consistent prices.

industry_notes.title: Installs for builders and property managers
industry_notes.text: New door installs for builders or apartment complexes often need a purchase order or unit number on the invoice. Ask for it before the job, put it in the notes, and bill each building or phase on its own invoice.

industry_notes.title: Taxes on parts and labor
industry_notes.text: States treat garage door work differently: some tax parts and labor, some only the parts, and a few treat a new door installation as a real property improvement. Invoicor applies one tax rate per invoice, so check your state's rule and set the rate to match.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes garage door technicians make on invoices

mistakes.title: No spring specs
mistakes.text: 'Springs replaced, $400' looks expensive and tells nobody what was installed. Write the wire size, length and cycle rating.

mistakes.title: Unwritten emergency rates
mistakes.text: A Sunday-night surcharge the customer doesn't remember agreeing to becomes a dispute. Put the after-hours rate on its own line and mention when it was agreed.

mistakes.title: Warranty without periods
mistakes.text: 'Lifetime warranty' with no detail on what it covers leads to free callbacks for unrelated problems. List parts and labor warranties separately, with how long each lasts.

pro_tip: Save your most common repairs as products in the app: spring pair by size, roller set, cable pair, opener tune-up, service call. On site you pick the lines, adjust the quantity and share the PDF before you leave the driveway, while the customer is still happy the door works.
format_pdf_desc: Homeowners often need a garage door invoice for a home warranty claim, an insurance claim after a car hit the door, or a landlord. A PDF keeps the parts list and warranty terms intact and is easy to forward.

faqs.question: What should a garage door repair invoice include?
faqs.answer: Your business name, license number where required, the customer and address, the date, the service call fee, each part with specs and quantity, labor or flat repair prices, any after-hours surcharge, tax where it applies, the total, safety checks performed and the warranty on parts and labor.

faqs.question: How much detail should I give about the springs?
faqs.answer: Enough that another technician could order the same springs: type (torsion or extension), wire size, length, wind direction if relevant, and cycle rating. It also explains why a high-cycle spring costs more than a standard one.

faqs.question: How do I invoice a new garage door installation?
faqs.answer: List the door (size, model, insulation, color), the opener if included, removal and disposal of the old door, installation labor and any extras like a keypad or new weather seal. If you take a deposit to order the door, send it as a separate invoice and show it on the final invoice as a negative line or in the notes.

faqs.question: Is garage door repair taxable?
faqs.answer: It depends on your state. Some tax both parts and labor, some tax only parts, and installs may count as real property improvements. Check your state's rule and keep it consistent on every invoice.

title: DJ Invoice Template for Weddings & Events (Free) | Invoicor
meta_description: Free DJ invoice template: wedding reception hours, ceremony sound, uplighting, overtime and travel in a filled-in example, less the retainer.
h1: Free DJ Invoice Template for Weddings and Events
subtitle: For mobile DJs and wedding DJs: how to invoice performance hours, MC duties, sound and lighting add-ons, overtime and travel, with the retainer you took at booking.
intro_paragraph: A DJ booking is often made a year ahead and paid in two or three parts, with the last payment due before the music starts. By then the couple has added uplighting, a second sound system for the ceremony on the lawn, and maybe an extra hour on the night. A DJ invoice keeps all of that straight: the package and its hours, each add-on, the overtime rate, travel, and the retainer already paid. Couples and party hosts get a clear number, and you don't have to chase anyone after the last song.
what_to_include_intro: Whether it's a wedding, a corporate party or a school dance, a DJ services invoice should include these parts.
req_1_text: Event date, venue name and address, start and end time, and the client's name and phone. The venue and timing also justify setup time and any travel charge.
req_2_text: The package name and what it covers: number of hours, MC duties (grand entrance, toasts, announcements), a planning meeting and the music request process.
req_3_text: Ceremony sound with wireless mics, uplighting with the number of fixtures, a dance floor light show, a photo booth or a monogram projection. Each one is a separate line with its price.
req_4_text: The hourly rate for extra time, and on the final invoice, the hours actually played past the contracted end. If the host asked for overtime on the night, note who approved it.
req_5_text: Mileage beyond your included radius, parking, tolls, a hotel for far-away weddings, and any load-in charge for venues with stairs or long carries.
req_6_text: The non-refundable retainer paid at booking, any other payments, and when the balance is due (many DJs ask for it a week or two before the event).
what_to_include_outro: Laid out this way, the invoice doubles as the run-sheet for the night: the client can see what's booked and you can see what you need to bring.
sample_breakdown_intro: A wedding with a five-hour reception package, a separate sound system for an outdoor ceremony, 12 uplights, one overtime hour requested on the night and 60 miles of travel beyond the included radius, less the $500 retainer. Many states don't tax DJ services, but some do; this example has no sales tax. Check your state's rule.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Wedding reception DJ and MC, 5 hours
Ceremony sound system, 2 wireless mics, garden setup
Overtime, approved by the couple at 10:30 pm

sample_breakdown_notes: Event: June 14, Willow Creek Barn, ceremony 4:30 pm, reception 6:00-11:00 pm, extended to 12:00 am. Setup from 2:30 pm. Retainer is non-refundable. Balance of the original package was due 14 days before the event; overtime and travel are due within 7 days.

industry_notes.title: Retainer, then balance
industry_notes.text: Most wedding DJs take a retainer to hold the date and the balance before the event. Send the retainer as its own invoice at booking. On the final invoice, show the retainer as a line with a negative amount or in the notes, so the couple sees what's left.

industry_notes.title: Overtime after the fact
industry_notes.text: Overtime is usually decided on the night, after the balance has been paid. Either bill it on a short follow-up invoice or agree in your contract that it's paid before you play past the end time.

industry_notes.title: Corporate and school events
industry_notes.text: Companies and schools often pay by check or bank transfer against a purchase order and need a W-9 from you. Put the PO number on the invoice and send the W-9 with it to avoid a payment delay.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes DJs make on invoices

mistakes.title: No end time on the invoice
mistakes.text: Without the contracted end time written down, overtime looks like a surprise. Put start and end times on every invoice for the event.

mistakes.title: Bundling add-ons into one price
mistakes.text: 'Wedding package, $2,000' hides that uplighting and ceremony sound were extras. List them separately, so the couple values them and next year's clients can see what they cost.

mistakes.title: Missing the balance due date
mistakes.text: If the invoice doesn't say the balance is due two weeks before the event, it often gets paid in cash at the end of the night, or not at all. Write the date.

pro_tip: Add your payment link (PayPal, Stripe or similar) to the invoice so the couple can pay the balance from the PDF on their phone. Wedding couples juggle dozens of vendors; the one who's easiest to pay gets paid first.
format_pdf_desc: Couples forward DJ invoices to parents who are paying, and corporate clients pass them to accounts payable. A PDF keeps the event details, add-ons and retainer exactly as you wrote them for everyone who opens it.

faqs.question: What should a DJ invoice include?
faqs.answer: Your business name and contact, the client, event date, venue and times, the package with hours and MC duties, each equipment add-on, the overtime rate and any overtime played, travel and venue fees, tax if your state charges it, the retainer paid, the balance due and its due date.

faqs.question: How much is a typical wedding DJ retainer?
faqs.answer: Many DJs ask for a fixed amount (often a few hundred dollars) or a percentage of the package, commonly 25% to 50%, to hold the date. Whatever you choose, write it in the contract and say whether it's refundable.

faqs.question: How do I invoice a DJ deposit?
faqs.answer: Send a separate invoice for the retainer when the client books. Before the event, send the final invoice with the retainer shown as a line with a negative amount, or in the notes, and the balance due date.

faqs.question: Do DJs charge sales tax?
faqs.answer: In many states, DJ and entertainment services aren't taxed, but some states tax them or tax equipment rental separately. Check your state's rule before your first booking of the year and keep it the same on every invoice.

h1: Free Event Planner Invoice Template & Example
subtitle: For event and wedding planners: how to invoice planning packages, coordination hours, vendor management and costs you paid for the client, with the retainer already taken.
intro_paragraph: Event planners spend months on work the client never sees: vendor calls, timelines, floor plans, contract reviews. Then on the day, everything happens at once. Your invoice is where that invisible work gets named. A clear event planning invoice shows the package and what it covers, any hours or meetings beyond it, assistants for the day, and the costs you paid on the client's behalf, kept apart from your fee. Clients who see that breakdown understand what they paid for and recommend you to the next couple or company.
what_to_include_intro: Weddings, corporate retreats, galas and milestone birthdays all bill differently, but a wedding planner invoice and a corporate event invoice share these parts.
req_1_text: The event name and date, the venue, guest count and the client contact. For companies, add the department, the PO number and who approves invoices.
req_2_text: Full planning, partial planning or day-of coordination, a flat fee, a percentage of the event budget or hourly. Name the basis and, for installments, which payment this is.
req_3_text: Lead planner and assistant coordinators with their hours on the day, including setup and teardown. Large events need more people, and the client should see why.
req_4_text: Extra vendor meetings, extra site visits, a rehearsal, a welcome dinner or a second event. Price them as the contract says, as hours or flat add-ons.
req_5_text: Anything you paid for the client, such as signage, favors, a rush delivery or a vendor's on-site meal, at cost or with your agreed handling fee. Keep receipts in case the client asks.
req_6_text: Note which vendors the client pays directly and which ones you pay and pass on. It avoids the classic question of whether the florist was in your fee.
what_to_include_outro: An invoice like this keeps your fee, your team's time and other people's costs in separate boxes, which is where most planner billing disputes start.
sample_breakdown_intro: The final invoice for a 140-guest wedding on a partial planning package: the package fee, an assistant coordinator on the day, two vendor meetings beyond the package, rehearsal coordination and signage the planner bought for the couple, less the 50% retainer. Planning services are untaxed in many states but not all; this example has no sales tax. Check your state's rule.
