Assistant coordinator, wedding day incl. setup and teardown
Vendor meetings beyond package (caterer tasting, rentals walkthrough)
Reimbursable: welcome sign and seating chart printing (at cost)

sample_breakdown_notes: Wedding: Sept 20, Harbor View Hall, 140 guests. Caterer, florist, DJ and photographer were paid directly by the couple and aren't included here. Printing receipt available on request. Balance due within 10 days. Thank you for letting us plan your day.

industry_notes.title: Installments over months

industry_notes.title: Percentage-of-budget fees
industry_notes.text: If you charge a percentage of the event budget, name the budget figure you used and the percentage on the line ('15% of $42,000 event budget'). When the budget changes, the client sees why the fee moved.

industry_notes.title: Taxes and reimbursements
industry_notes.text: Some states tax event planning or treat it as part of a taxable event package, and goods you buy and resell to the client can be taxable even where your service isn't. Check your state's rule and keep reimbursements at cost separate from fees.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes event planners make on invoices

mistakes.title: Mixing fees and vendor costs
mistakes.text: Rolling the signage or the rush delivery into your fee makes your fee look bigger and hides real costs. Keep reimbursables on their own lines, marked at cost.

mistakes.title: Not billing scope creep
mistakes.text: The third extra site visit and the surprise welcome brunch add up. If the contract prices extras, invoice them; if it doesn't, add a clause before the next booking.

mistakes.title: A final invoice after the event
mistakes.text: After the wedding, the couple is on a honeymoon and the energy is gone. Bill the package balance before the event and only true extras afterward.

pro_tip: Keep a running list of extras in your planning notes as they happen: date, what was asked, the agreed price. When it's time for the final invoice, the lines are already written and the client remembers asking for each one.
format_pdf_desc: Planner invoices get passed around: to parents who are paying, to a company's finance team, to a co-host splitting the bill. A PDF looks the same for each of them and keeps your fee and reimbursed costs in clearly separate lines.

faqs.question: What should an event planner invoice include?

faqs.question: How do wedding planners structure payments?
faqs.answer: Usually a retainer at signing (often 25% to 50% of the package), one or more installments during planning, and the balance a few weeks before the wedding. Extras that happen on the day are billed afterward.

faqs.question: How do I show the retainer on the final invoice?
faqs.answer: Send the retainer as a separate invoice when the client signs. On the final invoice, list it, and any installments, as a line with a negative amount or in the notes, so the client can see the balance at a glance.

faqs.question: Should I mark up costs I pay for the client?
faqs.answer: Some planners pass costs through at cost, others add a handling fee. Either is fine if your contract says so. Label the lines clearly ('at cost' or 'cost plus 10% handling') so the client isn't left guessing.

intro_paragraph: Flowers are bought for a date that can't move, and many are ordered weeks ahead from growers and wholesalers. A florist invoice that lists each arrangement, its quantity and its main flowers, plus delivery, setup and rentals, tells the client exactly what will arrive and protects you when the bridesmaid count changes the week before.
what_to_include_intro: Wedding work, corporate weekly arrangements or sympathy pieces, a flower shop invoice should cover these parts.

req_2_text: Bridal bouquet, bridesmaid bouquets, boutonnieres, corsages and flower crowns, each with a quantity. Counts are where last-minute changes happen, so make them easy to update.

req_5_text: Delivery, on-site setup time and late-night teardown are labor. List them as their own lines, with times if the venue limits access.
req_6_text: The deposit paid to reserve the date, the balance due date, and a line saying you may substitute flowers of similar color and value if the market or weather requires it.
what_to_include_outro: This turns the invoice into the order sheet your team works from on the day before the event, and the client's checklist on the day.

industry_notes.title: Final counts before you buy

mistakes_title: Three mistakes florists make on invoices

mistakes.title: Rentals without a return note

format_pdf_desc: Couples check a florist invoice against the mood board, and venues sometimes ask for it to plan load-in. A PDF keeps the counts, delivery times and substitution note clear and the same for everyone who opens it.

faqs.question: How much deposit do wedding florists take?

faqs.question: How do I show the deposit on a florist invoice?
faqs.answer: Send the deposit as a separate invoice when the client books. On the final invoice, show it as a line with a negative amount or in the notes, so the balance due after the final count is clear.

faqs.question: Do florists charge sales tax?
faqs.answer: In most states with a sales tax, flowers are taxable because they're tangible goods. Delivery, labor and rentals may be taxed differently depending on the state. Check your state's rule before you set up your invoices.

h1: Free Massage Therapy Invoice Template & Example

intro_paragraph: Most massage clients pay at the end of the session, so an invoice can feel like overkill. It isn't. Clients who claim the cost through a health savings account, a flexible spending account or an employer wellness benefit need a written receipt with your license number, the date and the type of treatment. Corporate chair massage events, hotel and spa contracts and package buyers all expect a proper invoice too. A clear massage therapist invoice also settles questions about late cancellations and prepaid packages before they turn into awkward conversations on the table.
what_to_include_intro: A massage therapy invoice doubles as a receipt. These are the parts that make it useful for you and for the client.
req_1_text: Your name or studio name, address, phone and state massage license number. Many reimbursement forms ask for it, and some states expect licensed therapists to show it on client paperwork.
req_2_text: Write each session as a separate line: the date, the length in minutes and the technique (Swedish, deep tissue, prenatal, sports, lymphatic drainage). Length drives price, so it should never be vague.
req_3_text: Hot stones, cupping, aromatherapy, CBD oil or an extra 15 minutes belong on their own lines with their own price, so the client sees why the total is higher than the menu rate.
req_4_text: When a client buys a package of five or ten sessions, name the package, the number of sessions and the expiry date if you have one. When a session is paid from a package, show it as redeemed with a zero amount so both of you can count what is left.
req_5_text: If a client adds a tip to an invoice, list it as its own line. If you charge for no-shows or late cancellations, include the date and refer to your policy (for example, 24 hours' notice).
req_6_text: For clients using an HSA or FSA, a short note with the treatment, the date paid and, where they have one, a reference to their doctor's letter of medical necessity makes their claim much easier.
what_to_include_outro: With these details on the page, the same document works as a bill, a receipt and a record of the client's treatment history.
sample_breakdown_intro: A month of treatment for a regular client recovering from a running injury: two Swedish sessions, one longer deep tissue session with hot stones, and aromatherapy on two visits. industry_notes.title: Packages paid up front
industry_notes.text: Selling a pack of sessions at a lower per-session price is common. Invoice the package once when it's bought, then keep a note on each visit receipt of how many sessions remain. Check your state's rules on whether prepaid packages or gift certificates can expire.

industry_notes.title: Corporate and event work
industry_notes.text: Chair massage at offices, conferences and races is usually billed by the hour per therapist, plus travel and setup. Ask the company for its purchase order or vendor number before the event and put it on the invoice.

industry_notes.title: Taxes and medical massage
industry_notes.text: Some states tax massage services and others don't, and a few treat massage prescribed by a doctor differently from relaxation massage. Check your state's rule, and talk to a tax professional if you bill insurance or work in a medical office.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes massage therapists make on invoices

mistakes.title: Writing just 'massage'
mistakes.text: A line that says 'Massage, $135' doesn't tell the client or their benefits plan what they paid for. Add the length, the technique and the date.

mistakes.title: Losing track of package sessions
mistakes.text: Without a running count, clients forget how many prepaid sessions they have left and disputes follow. Note the remaining balance on every receipt.

mistakes.title: Missing license number

faqs.question: Can I give a massage receipt for HSA or FSA reimbursement?

faqs.question: How do I invoice a massage package?

faqs.question: Is massage therapy subject to sales tax?
faqs.answer: In many states it isn't, but some states do tax massage services, and the rules can differ for medical or spa massage. Check your state's revenue department and apply the same rule on every invoice.

h1: Free Translation Invoice Template & Example
subtitle: For freelance translators and small language services: how to invoice per word, per page or per hour, with the language pair, word count and certification details agencies and direct clients expect.
intro_paragraph: Translators get paid in more ways than most freelancers: per source word, per target word, per page for certified documents, per hour for editing, and with minimum fees for short jobs. Agencies often pay against your invoice only after matching it to their purchase order, and direct clients want to understand why a two-page contract costs what it does. A translator invoice that states the language pair, the word count method and the turnaround removes the guesswork and gets approved faster.
what_to_include_intro: A good translation invoice shows the client exactly how the price was counted. Include these parts.
req_1_text: Name the source and target language (Spanish to English, German to English) and the document or file ('Supplier agreement v3, 9 pages'). Agencies process dozens of jobs a week and need to match yours quickly.
req_2_text: State the count and whether it's source words or target words, and which tool counted it. For CAT tool jobs with fuzzy matches, give the weighted count or list repetitions and new words separately.
req_3_text: Per word, per page, per line or per hour: write the unit next to the rate ('$0.14/word'). If you charge a minimum fee for short texts, say so on the line rather than inflating the rate.
req_4_text: Certified translations of birth certificates, diplomas or court papers are usually priced per page. List the certificate of accuracy and any notary or shipping costs on their own lines.
req_5_text: Proofreading by a second linguist, editing machine translation output, formatting or desktop publishing, glossary work and rush delivery are all separate charges. Name each one so it isn't mistaken for the translation itself.

what_to_include_outro: A deposit invoice is short, often a single line. The details above turn that line into a record both sides can rely on when the final invoice arrives.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Deposit: 30% of $4,000.00 project price, built-in bookcase and window seat (quote Q-118, accepted Mar 2)

sample_breakdown_notes: Deposit invoice #1047. Due by Mar 9 to hold the build slot starting Mar 23. Non-refundable once the timber is ordered on Mar 10. The balance of $2,800.00 is due on completion, on a final invoice that will subtract this deposit.

industry_notes.title: Tax can be due on the deposit
industry_notes.text: In many VAT countries, VAT is due on a deposit when it's paid, not when the work is finished. The deposit invoice then shows VAT on the deposit amount, and the final invoice charges VAT only on the rest. US sales tax works differently and varies by state. Check your local rule before the first one.

industry_notes.title: Deposit, down payment or retainer
industry_notes.text: A down payment or an advance payment is the same document as a deposit. A retainer is not: it pays ahead for availability or hours over a period, often month after month. A deposit belongs to one job and is used up by that job's final invoice.

industry_notes.title: How the final invoice takes it off
industry_notes.text: The final invoice lists the full price, then a negative line: 'Less deposit, invoice #1047, paid Mar 8: -$1,200.00'. The balance due is what's left. Quote the number and the payment date so the client's bookkeeper can match both payments to one job.

mistakes_title: Three deposit invoice mistakes

mistakes.title: Asking for the deposit in the quote only
mistakes.text: A quote that says '30% upfront' isn't something a client's accounts team can pay. Send a numbered deposit invoice with a due date.

mistakes.title: Forgetting the deposit on the final invoice
mistakes.text: The final invoice bills the full $4,000, and the client either overpays by $1,200 or refuses to pay anything until it's fixed. Before you send a final invoice, look up every deposit invoice for that client and job.

mistakes.title: No refund terms
mistakes.text: When a client cancels, an unclear deposit turns into an argument. If the invoice and the agreement both say when the deposit stops being refundable, there's little to argue about.

pro_tip: Repeat the deposit invoice number in the notes of the final invoice, not only on the negative line. If the deposit came from another account, that note is how the client's bookkeeper connects the two payments.
format_pdf_desc: A PDF looks the same on the client's phone and in their accounts system, so the deposit amount, the job price and your refund terms can't shift or be edited along the way.

faqs.question: Is a deposit invoice a real invoice?
faqs.answer: Yes. It has an invoice number, a date, your details and the client's, and an amount due, so it belongs in your records like any other invoice. The difference is that it bills work that isn't done yet.

faqs.question: Should a deposit invoice show the full project price?
faqs.answer: Yes. Show the agreed total and the share you're asking for, so the client sees what's left and you both have the agreed price in writing. If extra work changes it later, the final invoice shows the change.

faqs.question: How do I show the deposit on the final invoice?
faqs.answer: List the work at its full price, then a negative line for the amount received. In the free generator a line item can have a negative price, so the subtraction prints on the PDF. The app doesn't accept negative prices: there, bill the balance as the line and name the deposit invoice in its details and the notes. The final invoice template shows a complete example.

faqs.question: What if the client cancels after paying the deposit?
faqs.answer: If it's refundable, pay it back and keep a record that ties the refund to the deposit invoice; in many VAT countries you also issue a credit note. If it isn't, point to the terms the client accepted. Local consumer law can limit what you may keep, so check it.

faqs.question: Does Invoicor track whether a deposit was paid?
faqs.answer: Not as a deposit. You can mark the deposit invoice paid like any invoice, but the app doesn't link it to the final invoice or keep a running balance. When the job ends, write the final invoice with a negative line for the deposit.

title: Final Invoice Template (Free, PDF) | Invoicor
meta_description: Free final invoice template: bill the full price, subtract the deposit and every earlier invoice by number, and show the balance due. Download a PDF.
h1: Free Final Invoice Template
subtitle: Close a job that was paid in parts: the full price, every earlier invoice taken off by number and date, and the balance that settles the account.
intro_paragraph: A final invoice is the last bill on a job that was paid in parts. It restates the whole job at its full price, takes off every invoice the client has already had, and asks for what's left. That makes it the one document where the whole job adds up: the contract, the changes, the deposit, the stage payments and the balance. Done badly, the client pays twice for the same work or holds the payment. Below: the six fields that matter, a sample for a $12,000 job after a $3,000 deposit and a $4,500 progress invoice, and how tax works when earlier invoices already charged it.
what_to_include_intro: The final invoice answers one question for the client: is this really everything? Each field below helps it answer yes.
req_1_text: Write 'Final invoice' in the first line or at the start of the notes (the PDF's heading says Invoice). It tells the client nothing else is coming for this job, and it tells their accounts team to reconcile it against the earlier payments before paying. Use it only when the job is truly finished.
req_2_text: Start from the contract price and add every approved change on its own line. The total of these lines is the job's real price. If you bill only the remaining work, the client can't see how you reached the balance.
req_3_title: Every earlier invoice, by number and date
req_3_text: Subtract each earlier invoice on its own negative line: the deposit, then each progress or milestone invoice. Quote the invoice number and the date it was paid, such as 'Less progress invoice #1052, paid Jun 12'. One combined line for 'payments received' hides mistakes.
req_4_text: Name the job and the contract or quote it settles, with its number or date. A client with several jobs running needs to know which one this invoice closes, and which deposit and stage payments belong to it.
req_5_title: The balance due, with a date
req_5_text: End on one clear number: the amount that settles the job. Give it a due date and your payment details.
req_6_title: Its own number in your sequence
req_6_text: The final invoice takes the next number in your normal sequence, like every invoice before it. It refers to the earlier numbers; it doesn't reuse one or add a suffix like '-F'.
what_to_include_outro: If the full price minus the earlier invoices doesn't equal the balance, the client will notice. Check the math against your own list of invoices for the job before you send.
sample_breakdown_intro: The last invoice on a $12,000 shop interior build-out. The client paid a $3,000 deposit (invoice #1038) and a $4,500 progress invoice (#1052). The sample assumes no sales tax on these services. Tax rules vary, so check yours.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Shop interior build-out, contract price (agreement of Apr 2)
Change order 1: extra display wall, approved May 20

sample_breakdown_notes: Final invoice #1066 for agreement of Apr 2. Full price $12,000.00. Earlier invoices: #1038 deposit $3,000.00 and #1052 progress $4,500.00, both paid. Balance of $4,500.00 due by Jul 15. No further invoices will follow for this agreement.

industry_notes.title: Tax on the remaining amount only
industry_notes.text: If the deposit and progress invoices already charged VAT or sales tax, the final invoice charges tax on what's left, not on the full price again. Many VAT countries also expect the tax already invoiced to be shown on the final invoice. Germany is strict about this on a Schlussrechnung, so follow your local rule or ask your accountant.

industry_notes.title: Final means the job is closed
industry_notes.text: The latest invoice in a series isn't automatically a final one. Call an invoice final when the job or contract ends and its balance settles the account.

industry_notes.title: Keep the job's invoices together
industry_notes.text: Before you write the final invoice, list every invoice you sent for the job and whether it was paid. Invoicor doesn't link invoices or keep a running balance, so that list is yours to keep: a note in the client's file works.

mistakes_title: Three final invoice mistakes

mistakes.title: Billing only the last stage
mistakes.text: A final invoice that lists only the remaining work hides how the balance was reached. The client can't tell whether the deposit was counted. Restate the full price, then subtract.

mistakes.title: Subtracting a lump sum
mistakes.text: 'Less payments received: $7,500' is hard to check. One line per earlier invoice, with its number and date, makes each amount checkable.

mistakes.title: Charging tax twice
mistakes.text: When the earlier invoices charged tax and the final invoice applies tax to the full price again, the client pays tax twice on the same part of the job. Apply tax only to the remaining amount. Invoicor uses one tax rate per invoice, so the rate falls on what the lines add up to: subtract first, and the tax is on the remaining amount.

pro_tip: Send the final invoice with a short list of every invoice on the job, in the notes or your email: number, date, amount, paid or open. The client's accounts team checks that list first, so make it match theirs.
format_pdf_desc: A PDF fixes the full price, each subtraction and the balance in one layout, so the number the client approves is the number that reaches their accounts team.

faqs.question: What's the difference between a final invoice and a regular invoice?
faqs.answer: A regular invoice bills a piece of work. A final invoice closes a job that was paid in parts: it shows the full price, subtracts every earlier invoice and asks for the balance.

faqs.question: How do I subtract a deposit on a final invoice?
faqs.answer: Below the work lines, add a negative line such as 'Less deposit, invoice #1038, paid Apr 9: -$3,000.00', and one for each progress or milestone invoice. The free generator accepts negative prices. The app doesn't: there, bill the balance on one line and list each earlier invoice by number in the notes. The deposit invoice template covers the first half of the pair.

faqs.question: What if the client hasn't paid an earlier invoice yet?
faqs.answer: Don't bury it in the balance. Either subtract only the paid invoices and list the open one in the notes as still due, or subtract all of them and note that invoice #1052 remains unpaid. Either way, the client sees the full amount they owe.

faqs.question: Is a final invoice the same as a final bill or closing invoice?
faqs.answer: Yes. Final bill, closing invoice and final invoice all mean the last invoice that settles a job. Whatever the name, it should show the full price, the earlier invoices and the balance.

faqs.question: Can I change a final invoice after sending it?
faqs.answer: Not in place. In Invoicor a sent invoice is locked: duplicate it, correct the copy, send that, and mark the old one cancelled. In many countries the expected route is a credit note against the wrong invoice, so check what your accountant prefers.

title: Milestone Invoice Template (Free, PDF) | Invoicor
meta_description: Free milestone invoice template: bill each accepted stage of a project with its share of the total and what's paid so far. Sample included, PDF download.
h1: Free Milestone Invoice Template
subtitle: Bill a project in the stages your contract sets, one invoice per accepted deliverable, with its share of the total and a clear count of what's been paid.
intro_paragraph: A milestone invoice bills one stage of a project once that stage is delivered and accepted. The stages come from the contract: design 30%, build 50%, launch 20%. Each milestone is a deliverable, not a date and not a measure of effort. That's the difference from progress billing, where a contractor bills for how much of the work is complete, and from a retainer, where the client pays for time whether or not anything ships. This page covers what to put on it, a sample for milestone 2 of 3 on a $9,000 project, and how the stages should add up to the contract.
what_to_include_intro: A client approves a milestone invoice by checking it against the contract. Make that check easy with these six fields.
req_1_title: The milestone, named as in the contract
req_1_text: Use the milestone's number and name exactly as the contract has them: 'Milestone 2 of 3: Build'. If the contract says 'Beta release' and the invoice says 'Development phase', the client's accounts team will ask which payment it is.
req_2_text: Quote the agreement or statement of work by its number or date. Clients with several projects need it to match the invoice to a budget, and you need it if a stage is ever disputed.
req_3_text: Describe the deliverable in a few words and state when the client accepted it: 'Build delivered Aug 7, accepted by email Aug 14'. Under most milestone contracts, acceptance is what makes the payment due, so it belongs on the invoice and not only in your inbox.
req_4_text: Show the milestone's percentage or fixed amount next to the full contract value: '50% of $9,000.00'. The client sees the stage in proportion, and anyone reading the invoice later sees the whole deal it belongs to.
req_5_text: List the earlier milestone invoices by number with what was paid, plus what remains after this one. 'Paid to date: $2,700.00 (invoice #2031). Remaining after this invoice: $1,800.00.' This running count keeps the last stage from being a surprise.
req_6_title: Extra work on its own lines
req_6_text: Work the client asked for outside the milestones, such as a change request, goes on a separate line with its own reference. Folding it into the milestone amount makes the stage look pricier than the contract says, and it gets queried.
what_to_include_outro: Taken together, the stage invoices should equal the contract value plus approved changes, with nothing missing.
sample_breakdown_intro: Milestone 2 of 3 on a $9,000 customer portal project, split 30% design, 50% build, 20% launch. Milestone 1 was paid on invoice #2031. The sample assumes the services aren't subject to sales tax: tax rules vary by state and country, so check yours.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Milestone 2 of 3: Build (50% of $9,000.00), delivered Aug 7, accepted Aug 14, per SOW-14
Change request CR-3: data export feature, approved Jul 28

sample_breakdown_notes: Invoice #2044, due Sep 13 (net 30). Contract value $9,000.00. Paid to date: $2,700.00 (invoice #2031, Milestone 1: Design). After this invoice, $1,800.00 remains for Milestone 3: Launch. Change requests are billed outside the contract value.

industry_notes.title: Milestone billing is not progress billing
industry_notes.text: The two get mixed up. Progress billing charges for the share of the work that's done, measured as a percentage and typical in construction. Milestone billing charges a fixed amount when a defined deliverable is accepted. If your contract measures completion rather than deliverables, a progress invoice is the closer fit.

industry_notes.title: Acceptance terms decide when you can bill
industry_notes.text: Many milestone contracts give the client a set number of days to accept or reject a deliverable, and treat silence as acceptance after that. If yours does, the invoice can quote it: 'Deemed accepted Aug 14 under clause 6'. If the contract says nothing, get acceptance in writing before you invoice.

industry_notes.title: Tax on each stage
industry_notes.text: In many VAT countries, each milestone invoice is taxed on its own date, so it carries VAT on that stage's amount. In the US, whether a service or a digital deliverable is taxable depends on the state. Invoicor applies one tax rate per invoice, so a stage that mixes taxed and untaxed work may need two invoices; ask your accountant.

mistakes_title: Three milestone invoice mistakes

mistakes.title: Invoicing before acceptance
mistakes.text: Sending the invoice the day you deliver, before the client has signed off, invites them to reject both. Wait for acceptance, or the date the contract deems it accepted, and quote that date.

mistakes.title: Stages that don't add up
mistakes.text: Rounding a third of $10,000 to $3,333 three times leaves $1 unbilled, and a renegotiated split can leave more. Make the last milestone the remainder of the contract value, so the stages always total the contract exactly.

mistakes.title: No running total
mistakes.text: Each invoice on its own looks fine, but without 'paid to date' and 'remaining' the client loses track, and so do you.

pro_tip: Start each new milestone invoice by duplicating the previous one. The contract reference, client details and payment terms carry over; you change the milestone line, the acceptance date and the running totals in the notes.
format_pdf_desc: A PDF keeps the milestone name, the acceptance date and the running totals fixed, which is what a client's project manager forwards to finance for approval.

faqs.question: How do I split a project into milestones?
faqs.answer: Tie each milestone to something the client can see and accept, such as a signed-off design, a working build or a launch. Give each one a fixed share of the total in the contract.

faqs.question: Can the first milestone be paid upfront?
faqs.answer: Yes. Many contracts make the first payment due on signing, before any deliverable exists. That payment is really a deposit, so bill it on a deposit invoice that names the contract, then bill the later stages as milestones. The last invoice should list both.

faqs.question: What if the client rejects a milestone?
faqs.answer: Don't invoice it yet. Fix what the contract's acceptance criteria require, deliver again, and invoice on acceptance. If you already sent the invoice, mark it cancelled rather than leaving it open, then issue a new one once the stage is accepted.

faqs.question: Where do change requests go?
faqs.answer: Bill approved change requests on the next milestone invoice, on their own lines with the change reference, or on a separate invoice. Keep them out of the milestone amount itself, so each stage still matches the contract figure.

faqs.question: How is the last milestone invoice different?
faqs.answer: The last milestone bills the final stage and closes the contract, so it often doubles as the final invoice. Restate the contract value, list every earlier milestone invoice by number, and mark it final. The final invoice template shows that layout.

title: Retainer Invoice Template (Free, PDF) | Invoicor
meta_description: Free retainer invoice template: bill a monthly fee for hours or availability, with included hours, overage and unused-hour terms. Sample and PDF.
h1: Free Retainer Invoice Template
subtitle: Bill a fixed fee in advance for a month of availability or a block of hours, with what's included, what happens to unused hours and extra work on its own lines.
intro_paragraph: A retainer invoice bills a fixed fee, paid ahead, for a period of your time. Lawyers, consultants, agencies and freelancers use it when a client wants them on call or wants a set number of hours each month. Unlike a deposit, it doesn't belong to one job that ends. Unlike a milestone, nothing has to be delivered before it's due. The client pays for access, and the invoice has to spell out what that access includes: the period, the hours or scope, what happens to hours that go unused, and how extra work is charged. This page covers the fields, a sample for May with 20 included hours and 3 hours over, and how to send one each month.
what_to_include_intro: A retainer invoice repeats every period, so small gaps add up. These six fields make each month's invoice complete on its own.
req_1_text: State the exact dates: 'Retainer, May 1 to May 31'. The client is paying for a stretch of time, so the period is the main thing being billed.
req_2_text: Write the included hours or scope in one line: '20 hours of consulting', 'up to 4 contract reviews', 'on-call support on weekdays'. This is what the client measures your work against, so match the wording in your agreement.
req_3_text: Say which kind of retainer this is. An advance retainer is prepaid work: hours are drawn down against it. An availability retainer pays to keep you on call, and the fee is earned whether the client uses you or not.
req_4_text: Tell the client what happens to hours they didn't use: carried into the next period, carried over up to a cap, or lost at month end. One sentence in the notes, taken from the agreement, saves a conversation after every quiet month.
req_5_text: Hours beyond the included amount go on a separate line with the count and the rate: '3 hours beyond retainer, April, at $160.00'. Keeping them apart from the fee shows the client the retainer price didn't change.
req_6_text: A retainer is paid ahead, so the due date should fall on or before the first day of the period. A retainer due at the end of the month is really an hourly invoice with a minimum.
what_to_include_outro: Get these lines right once, and each new retainer invoice only needs a new period, a new date and any overage.
sample_breakdown_intro: A consultant's retainer for May: 20 hours included for a fixed fee, paid in advance. In April the client used 23 hours, so the 3 extra hours are billed here at the agreed overage rate. The sample assumes the consulting isn't subject to sales tax. Service tax rules differ by place, so check yours.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Monthly retainer, May 1 to May 31: up to 20 hours of consulting (agreement R-07)
Hours beyond retainer, April (23 used, 20 included)

sample_breakdown_notes: Invoice #3118, due May 1. The retainer fee is payable in advance; May work starts on receipt. Unused hours don't roll over (agreement R-07, clause 3). Any May overage goes on the June invoice at $160.00 per hour.

industry_notes.title: Client money may have rules of its own
industry_notes.text: For lawyers and some other professions, an advance retainer can count as the client's money until it's earned, with rules about where it's held and when you may draw on it. Those rules differ by state and country. Check your licensing body's guidance before you set up the invoice.

industry_notes.title: When the fee counts as income
industry_notes.text: An availability retainer is usually earned when its period starts. An advance against future work may only be earned as you do the work. That can change when you record the income or charge VAT, so ask your accountant which applies to your agreement.

industry_notes.title: Sending it every month
industry_notes.text: Invoicor doesn't send recurring invoices. At the start of each period, duplicate last month's retainer invoice, change the dates and the period, update or delete the overage line, and send it. Give the copy the next number in your sequence so your records stay in order.

mistakes_title: Three retainer invoice mistakes

mistakes.title: Hiding overage in the fee
mistakes.text: Raising the retainer line from $2,800 to $3,280 in a busy month makes the fee look unstable, and the client can't see why. Keep the fee fixed and add a separate overage line with hours and rate.

mistakes.title: No rule for unused hours
mistakes.text: If the agreement and the invoice say nothing, clients often assume unused hours carry over indefinitely. After a few quiet months you owe a backlog of free work.

mistakes.title: Billing the retainer after the month
mistakes.text: Invoicing on the 31st for the month just finished turns the retainer into credit you're extending. If the client stops paying, the work is already done. Date the invoice before the period and make it due by the first day.

pro_tip: Keep a simple hours log per client and month next to your invoices. When you bill overage, give the dates and the task for each extra hour in the line or the notes.
format_pdf_desc: A PDF lets the client file each month's retainer next to the last one in the same layout, so the fixed fee, the period and any overage are easy to compare.

faqs.question: What's the difference between a retainer and a deposit?
faqs.answer: A deposit is part of the price of one job, paid before it starts and subtracted on the final invoice. A retainer pays for a period of availability or a block of hours, usually again each month, and isn't subtracted from a later bill.

faqs.question: Should a retainer invoice list the hours worked?
faqs.answer: The fee line doesn't need them, since the fee is fixed. Many clients still want a summary of hours used against the included amount, and you need one when you bill overage. Put the summary in the notes or send a short report with the invoice.

faqs.question: Do unused retainer hours roll over?
faqs.answer: Only if your agreement says so. No rollover, one month of rollover, or rollover up to a cap are the usual choices. Repeat yours on each invoice.

faqs.question: Is a retainer refundable?
faqs.answer: It depends on the kind and your agreement. An availability retainer is usually earned for its period, while unused advance payments for work may have to be returned when the engagement ends. Check your profession's rules before you promise either way.

faqs.question: Can I charge a different rate for hours over the retainer?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the agreement says so. Some retainers price the included hours below the normal rate and bill overage at the full rate; others use one rate for both. Show the rate on the overage line so the client can check it.

title: Hourly Invoice Template (Free, PDF) | Invoicor
meta_description: Free hourly invoice template: bill hours times rate with a clear timesheet summary, rush rates and rounding. Fill in the sample and download a PDF.
h1: Free Hourly Invoice Template
subtitle: Bill time worked as hours times rate, with a short timesheet summary your client can check line by line.
intro_paragraph: An hourly invoice charges for time, not for a finished deliverable. Every line is built from two numbers: the hours worked and the rate for those hours. That makes it the most transparent way to bill, and the one clients question most. A good hourly invoice answers the questions first: which day, which task, how many hours, at which rate, and why a higher rate applies where it does. Below: the timesheet summary, rounding, standard and rush rates side by side, and an agreed cap. The sample bills three working days at two rates.
what_to_include_intro: The client already agreed to your rate. What they want from the invoice is proof of the hours. Build every line so it can be checked against your own time records.
req_1_title: One line per day or per task
req_1_text: Group hours the way your client thinks about the work: by task for a project ("Migrate mailboxes, 3.5 h"), by date when they pay for your presence. Avoid one line reading "42 hours of work": it hides what the client needs to approve it.
req_2_text: Write 2.25 hours, not 2 h 15 min, so the quantity multiplies cleanly by the rate. 15 minutes is 0.25, 20 minutes is 0.33, 45 minutes is 0.75. Our free hours calculator adds up start and end times if you logged them on paper.
req_3_text: Put the hourly rate on each line, even when it repeats. A second rate (rush, weekend, travel) then stands out on its own row instead of hiding in a blended total.
req_4_text: Say in the notes how you round: to the nearest quarter hour, to the next six minutes, or with a one-hour minimum per call-out. Clients accept rounding they were told about, not rounding they discover.
req_5_text: Give the date range the invoice covers, for example "Work from October 6 to October 13". Back-to-back periods mean no hours fall between two invoices and none are billed twice.
req_6_title: The cap, if there is one
req_6_text: When the client approved "up to 30 hours", show where this invoice leaves them: "Hours billed this month: 11.25 of 30". It builds trust and gives you a moment to ask for more hours before you go over.
what_to_include_outro: Keep your own time log behind the invoice. The invoice is the summary; the log is what you show if a client asks how Tuesday turned into six hours.
sample_breakdown_intro: An IT support contractor bills a small office for one week: three working days at $85 per hour, plus one same-day request at the agreed rush rate of 1.5 times. No sales tax is shown: many US states don't tax this service, but rules vary, so check yours.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Oct 6: new router setup and firewall rules (standard)
Oct 8: laptop setup for two new hires (standard)
Oct 8: same-day printer outage, requested 4 pm (rush 1.5x)
Oct 13: backup check and staff password reset (standard)

sample_breakdown_notes: Work from October 6 to October 13. Time rounded to the nearest quarter hour. Rush rate (1.5x) applies to requests for same-day work, as agreed in the service terms. Hours billed this month: 11.25 of the 30-hour cap. Payment due within 14 days.

industry_notes.title: Track time somewhere else first
industry_notes.text: Neither the Invoicor app nor the free generator has a timer. Keep your hours in a notebook, calendar or time app, then type the totals in. In the app, save "Standard hour" and "Rush hour" as products once and add them to each new invoice in a tap.

industry_notes.title: Minimums and travel time are terms, not surprises
industry_notes.text: A one-hour minimum per visit, or travel at half rate, is fair only if the client agreed before the work. Put it in your quote or service agreement, then repeat it in the invoice notes.

industry_notes.title: Hourly is not a retainer
industry_notes.text: An hourly invoice bills the exact hours worked. A retainer bills a fixed sum for reserved time, used or not, and a monthly invoice bills an agreed fee for a period of service. If the client pays the same amount every month, one of those fits better.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes on hourly invoices

mistakes.title: A total of hours with no breakdown
mistakes.text: "Consulting, 18 hours, $1,530" makes the client do the detective work. The usual result is a delayed payment and an email asking for details.

mistakes.title: Mixing rates in one line
mistakes.text: Billing 4 standard and 1.5 rush hours as "5.5 hours at $96.59" is correct math and confusing to read. Use one row per rate, so each line can be checked on its own.

mistakes.title: Going over the cap without asking
mistakes.text: If the client approved 20 hours and the invoice says 26, the extra six are a negotiation, not a bill. Ask before you pass the cap and record the approval in the notes.

pro_tip: Write each line's description in the past tense, as an outcome: "Restored the shared drive after the outage" reads like value delivered, while "Worked on drive" reads like time spent. Same hours, same rate, fewer questions.
format_pdf_desc: A PDF keeps your hours and rates exactly as you sent them, so the client's approval and your records always match the same numbers.

faqs.question: How do I calculate an hourly invoice?
faqs.answer: Multiply each line's hours by its rate, then add the lines up. Discount and tax come after the subtotal. In the free generator, hours go in the quantity field and the rate in the price field; the totals calculate for you.

faqs.question: Should I attach a timesheet to an hourly invoice?
faqs.answer: On short invoices, the lines are the timesheet: date, task and hours. For long engagements, summarize by day or week and keep the detailed log ready if asked. Some clients, agencies in particular, require a signed timesheet with every invoice: follow their process.

faqs.question: How should I round billable time?
faqs.answer: Pick one rule and state it. The nearest quarter hour is common for services; many professionals bill in six-minute units (0.1 hour). Round each entry, not only the weekly total.

faqs.question: Can I charge a different rate for rush or weekend work?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the client agreed before the work started. Show the higher rate on its own line with a short reason, like "rush 1.5x" or "Saturday rate".

faqs.question: How often should I send an hourly invoice?
faqs.answer: Weekly or every two weeks suits steady work: the hours are fresh and the amounts stay small. Monthly suits clients with a monthly payment run. For one-off jobs, invoice when the work is done.

faqs.question: Does Invoicor track my hours?
faqs.answer: No. The app makes the invoice; it doesn't run a timer. Enter the hours you tracked as quantities. The free hours calculator can add up a day's start and end times first.

title: Monthly Invoice Template (Free, PDF) | Invoicor
meta_description: Free monthly invoice template for ongoing service: show the service period, visits made and skipped visits credited. Fill in the sample, get a PDF.
h1: Free Monthly Invoice Template
subtitle: One invoice per month for ongoing service: the period, what was delivered that month, any credits, and a clear due date.
intro_paragraph: A monthly invoice bills a client once per calendar month for service that keeps going: weekly visits, maintained equipment, a standing lesson slot, a rented item. The price is agreed once, as a flat monthly fee or a price per visit. Each invoice then shows what happened in that month: were all visits made, was one skipped and credited, was anything extra added? Clients pay these in their regular payment run, so the period and the number matter as much as the amount. Below: the structure, credits for skipped visits, and a fast way to make next month's invoice from this one.
what_to_include_intro: Because the client sees nearly the same invoice every month, what changes is what they read. Make the period, the visit count and any adjustments easy to spot.
req_1_text: Write the exact period: "Service period: October 1 to 31, 2026". The issue date alone isn't enough. Bookkeepers match invoices to months, and a clear period stops a month from being paid twice or skipped.
req_2_title: A number that shows the month
req_2_text: A scheme with the year and month helps both sides: INV-2026-10, then INV-2026-11. Keep it sequential and unique. Give one-off jobs a suffix or their own series so the monthly run stays readable.
req_3_title: The fee and how it's built
req_3_text: State the basis: a flat fee ("Monthly plant care, 4 visits included") or a price per visit times the visits made. If the fee is flat, say how a five-week month is handled.
req_4_text: When a visit was skipped, add a negative line: "Credit: October 23 visit skipped, office closed". Quietly lowering the fee looks like a price change; a visible credit shows the agreement still stands.
req_5_text: Anything not covered by the monthly fee, like a replacement part, an extra visit or a one-time job, goes on its own line with its own price. Listing it separately keeps next month's invoice clean when you copy this one.
req_6_title: A due date that fits their payment run
req_6_text: Many businesses pay suppliers on fixed days. Ask which, and set the due date before that run. "Due November 15" is clearer than "Net 15" when the invoice may sit in an inbox.
what_to_include_outro: If the client receives the same invoice every month with only the period changing, the one month something differs (a credit, an extra) is the one they'll read closely. Make that line obvious and explained.
sample_breakdown_intro: An office plant care service bills October: four weekly visits in the flat fee, one visit skipped (office closed) and credited at the per-visit price, and one replacement plant added. The sample assumes a state with 6% sales tax on both service and plant; tax rules vary, so check yours.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Monthly plant care, October 1 to 31 (4 weekly visits)

sample_breakdown_notes: Invoice INV-2026-10. Service period October 1 to 31, 2026. Visits made: October 2, 9 and 16; October 23 skipped at the client's request and credited at $65 per visit. Payment due November 15.

industry_notes.title: Monthly, not automatic
industry_notes.text: Many billing tools call this a recurring invoice and send it on a schedule. Invoicor doesn't send recurring or scheduled invoices. Open last month's invoice, tap duplicate, and change the period, the number and any credits. Client, fee line and notes carry over.

industry_notes.title: Monthly invoice or retainer?
industry_notes.text: A monthly invoice bills service delivered in the month. A retainer bills in advance for time or availability reserved. If you invoice on the 1st for work not yet done, you're closer to a retainer, and the wording should say so.

industry_notes.title: Mark last month paid before you copy it
industry_notes.text: Set the previous invoice to paid when the money arrives, then duplicate it. The status list shows which months are settled and which are overdue, so a missed payment doesn't hide behind a newer invoice.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes on monthly invoices

mistakes.title: Copying last month without changing the period
mistakes.text: An invoice that still says "September" in November gets rejected or paid as a duplicate. Before sending, check the period, the number and the due date.

mistakes.title: Skipped visits left out silently
mistakes.text: Bill the full fee for a skipped visit without a word, and the client asks for every credit at once months later. Credit it, or state in the agreement that the fee covers skipped visits.

mistakes.title: Extras added to the main fee
mistakes.text: Raising the main line from $260 to $405 for a replacement plant makes next month's copy wrong and hides what changed. Keep the base fee fixed and put extras on their own lines.

pro_tip: Send the monthly invoice on the same day every month, ideally the first working day after the period ends. Clients build it into their routine, the gap between months stays even, and a late payment is easy to spot.
format_pdf_desc: A PDF per month gives the client a fixed document for each period that files neatly by month and can't change after it was sent.

faqs.question: When should I send a monthly invoice?
faqs.answer: For service delivered during the month, right after it ends, when all visits and credits are known. For a fixed fee with nothing to adjust, some businesses invoice on the 1st. Choose one and stay with it.

faqs.question: How do I bill a month with five weekly visits?
faqs.answer: With a price per visit, bill five. With a flat fee, the usual approach is that it covers every week, so it stays the same; some businesses define it as four visits and bill a fifth as an extra. Write the rule in the agreement and the notes.

faqs.question: How do I show a credit on a monthly invoice?
faqs.answer: Add a line with a negative price and a short reason, such as "Credit: October 23 visit skipped". The client sees the full fee and the adjustment. The free generator accepts negative prices for exactly this. The app doesn't: there, lower the month's quantity or fee and put the reason in the line's details.

faqs.question: Can I pro-rate the first or last month?
faqs.answer: Yes. Bill the share of the month or the visits made, and say so: "Service from October 15, 2 of 4 visits". Agree the method, by days or by visits, before the first invoice.

faqs.question: Does each monthly invoice need its own number?
faqs.answer: Yes, even if the content repeats. Sequential numbers are expected in most countries and help your accountant. Year and month in the number make the run easy to read.

title: Labor and Materials Invoice Template (Free) | Invoicor
meta_description: Free labor and materials invoice template: labor lines, itemized materials with markup, trip and disposal fees, and sales tax. Fill it in, get a PDF.
h1: Free Labor and Materials Invoice Template
subtitle: Bill the work and the parts on separate lines, with the tax only where it applies.
intro_paragraph: A labor and materials invoice splits a job's price in two: what you charged for your work and what you charged for the things you installed or used. Trades also call it a time and materials invoice or a parts and labor invoice. The split matters three ways. The client sees what the job cost in parts versus skill. Sales tax often applies to one part and not the other. And on time and materials work, with no fixed price, the invoice is the only place the client can check both. Below: labor lines, itemized materials and markup, trip and disposal fees, and tax. The sample is a door frame repair with three labor hours and five material lines.
what_to_include_intro: Each line should belong clearly to labor, materials or a fee. If a client can't tell which group a line sits in, the split loses its purpose.
req_1_title: Labor as hours times rate, or a flat price
req_1_text: On time and materials work, list labor as hours and a rate, with what was done: "Remove and replace rotted jamb, 3 h at $78". On a job priced per task, a flat labor line is fine if it names the task.
req_2_title: Materials with quantity, unit and unit price
req_2_text: Give each material its own line in the unit it's sold in: 3 tubes of caulk, 1 box of screws, 12 linear feet of trim. "Materials: $200" invites the client to price the job at the hardware store.
req_3_text: Markup pays for sourcing, pickup, storage and returns. Build it into unit prices and state it once in the notes ("materials include a 15% handling charge"), or show cost and markup separately. Hiding it causes disputes.
req_4_text: Trip charges, dump fees or a shop supplies charge are neither labor nor a specific material. Give each its own line and a plain name, so it reads as a fee for a reason, not padded labor.
req_5_title: Tax shown on the right base
req_5_text: In many US states, materials are taxable and repair labor isn't, but rules differ by state and by type of work (repair versus new construction). Label the tax line with its base, such as "7% on materials", and check your state's revenue department.
req_6_title: A reference to the quote or work order
req_6_text: Time and materials jobs often start with an estimated range or a not-to-exceed amount. Put that reference and limit in the notes, so the client can compare the total to what they approved.
what_to_include_outro: Our trade templates (plumbing, electrician, HVAC, handyman and others) show the same structure with each trade's own parts and rules.
sample_breakdown_intro: A repair contractor replaces a rotted exterior door frame: three labor hours, a trip charge, five material lines and a disposal fee. Material prices include a 15% markup on cost. The sample assumes a state with 7% sales tax on materials only; tax rules vary by state, so check yours.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Labor: replace rotted jamb and threshold
Material: primed pine jamb kit, 36 in

sample_breakdown_notes: Work order WO-0412, approved as time and materials, not to exceed $600. Material prices include a 15% handling charge on cost. Labor billed in half-hour steps. Payment due on completion.
industry_notes_title: Labor and materials invoice rules worth knowing

industry_notes.title: Time and materials versus fixed price
industry_notes.text: On a fixed-price job, the client pays the quoted total and the split is mostly for tax and clarity. On time and materials, the client pays actual hours and parts, so the invoice is the proof. Agree which applies before you start, with a cap for time and materials.

industry_notes.title: One tax rate per invoice
industry_notes.text: The Invoicor app and the free generator apply one tax rate to the whole invoice, with no per-line setting. If only materials are taxable where you work, one clean option is two invoices: materials with tax, labor without. Ask your accountant what your state prefers.

industry_notes.title: Keep the supplier receipts
industry_notes.text: Supplier receipts back up your material prices if a client or auditor asks, so file them with the job. The client's invoice needs item, quantity and price, not your cost, unless the contract is cost-plus.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes on labor and materials invoices

mistakes.title: Taxing the whole subtotal
mistakes.text: Applying the materials rate to labor too overcharges the client where labor is exempt. Check what's taxable in your state and let the tax fall only on that part.

mistakes.title: Labor folded into material prices
mistakes.text: Raising part prices to cover install time makes parts look overpriced and labor look free, and breaks the tax split. Keep install time on labor lines, even when it's short.

mistakes.title: Forgetting the small stuff
mistakes.text: Screws, caulk, filler and blades add up across a year. If your contract allows it, bill them as material lines or one stated shop supplies line instead of absorbing them.

pro_tip: Save your most-used materials as products in the app, marked-up price included. Prices stay consistent and you stop guessing the markup on site.
format_pdf_desc: A PDF fixes the labor hours, material prices and tax line as agreed, which is what a client compares against the work order and what you keep for the job file.

faqs.question: What is the difference between labor and materials and time and materials?
faqs.answer: Same invoice: work and parts on separate lines. "Time and materials" usually also means no fixed price upfront, so the client pays actual hours and parts. "Parts and labor" is the name in repair trades. This layout fits all three.

faqs.question: Should I show my markup on materials?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily per line, but the client should know it exists: build it into the unit price and add one sentence in the notes. On cost-plus contracts, show cost and markup on separate lines.

faqs.question: Is labor taxable on an invoice?
faqs.answer: It depends on the state and the work. Many US states tax materials and not repair labor; some tax certain labor, and new construction often has its own rules. Check your state's department of revenue.

faqs.question: How do I bill for a trip or service call?
faqs.answer: First line, flat price: "Trip charge, $45". If you credit it when the client goes ahead with the job, add a negative line right below, so fee and credit sit side by side.

faqs.question: What if the job goes over the estimate?
faqs.answer: Tell the client before you pass the agreed limit and get approval in writing, then note it: "Approved October 14 to exceed $600 by up to $150". An overrun first heard of on the invoice is a common reason these invoices go unpaid.

title: Expense Reimbursement Invoice Template (Free) | Invoicor
meta_description: Free reimbursement invoice template for passing costs on to a client: list each expense, at cost or with a markup, with receipts. Fill it in, get a PDF.
h1: Free Expense Reimbursement Invoice Template
subtitle: For businesses and freelancers billing a client for costs they paid on the client's behalf: travel, fees and supplies, at cost or with an agreed markup.
intro_paragraph: This is the invoice a business or freelancer sends to a client to recover costs paid for that client's job. It is not an employee's expense report to an employer. You paid for the flight, the venue or the printing; the contract says the client covers it; now you bill it. The price isn't your work but a list of what you spent, each line backed by a receipt, at cost or with an agreed markup. Bill these on their own reimbursement invoice or as an expenses section on your regular one. Below: what each line needs, receipts and markup, and the tax difference between a rebilled cost and a true disbursement.
what_to_include_intro: A client approving an expense invoice wants to tick off each cost against a receipt and the contract. Give them what they need to do that.
req_1_title: One line per expense, with date and vendor
req_1_text: List each cost separately: "Oct 14: flight Chicago to Denver, receipt 1". Date and vendor let the client match the line to the trip and the receipt. Group only many small items of one kind, like taxis on one trip.
req_2_text: Number your receipts and put the number on each line. Send copies as a separate file with the invoice. When accounts asks for receipt 4, you both know which one.
req_3_title: At cost or with markup, as the contract says
req_3_text: Many contracts say expenses pass on at cost; others allow a handling fee, often on purchases, not travel. Show any markup on its own line ("Handling fee 10% on printing, contract section 6") so the costs still match the receipts.
req_4_text: Name the project, event or purchase order the costs belong to. Clients often pay expenses from a different budget than fees, and a reference sends your invoice to the right person instead of a general inbox.
req_5_title: Amounts in the currency you'll be paid in
req_5_text: For costs paid in another currency, convert to the invoice currency and say how: "converted at the card rate on the statement". The client then pays one total in one currency.
req_6_title: A clear link to the main invoice
req_6_text: When fees and expenses go on separate invoices, cross-reference the numbers in the notes. A client won't approve one and forget the other, and your bookkeeper can match payments.
what_to_include_outro: Check the contract before you buy anything you plan to pass on. Pre-approval for large costs (flights, hotels, equipment rental) avoids the one argument a reimbursement invoice can't win: "we never agreed to that".
sample_breakdown_intro: A freelance workshop facilitator bills the costs of a two-day on-site workshop, separate from the fee invoice. Travel and venue are at cost; printing carries a 10% handling fee the contract allows. No sales tax in this US example; whether rebilled costs are taxed varies by state and country, so check yours.
sample_breakdown_notes: Expenses for the October 15 to 16 workshop, PO 7731. Fees on invoice INV-0088. Receipts 1 to 7 sent as a separate PDF. Travel and venue at cost; handling fee per contract section 6. Due within 30 days.
industry_notes_title: Expense reimbursement invoice rules worth knowing

industry_notes.title: Disbursement or rebilled cost: the tax difference
industry_notes.text: In VAT countries, a cost you pass on is usually part of your own supply and gets VAT like your fee. A true disbursement, paid as the client's agent, can stay outside VAT. In the UK, HMRC's VAT guide (Notice 700, section 25.1, checked November 2026) lists eight conditions, including that you recover only the exact amount paid.

industry_notes.title: In the US, check your state
industry_notes.text: Some states treat reimbursed expenses as part of a taxable sale when the service is taxable; others don't, and rebilled materials can be taxable on their own. There's no single US rule, so check your state's revenue department.

industry_notes.title: Not an employee expense report
industry_notes.text: Employees claiming costs back usually use their employer's expense form, not an invoice. This page is for a business billing a separate client.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes on reimbursement invoices

mistakes.title: A markup the contract doesn't allow
mistakes.text: Adding 15% to travel when the contract says "at cost" turns a routine invoice into a trust problem, usually found when the client checks a receipt. Add only a handling fee the agreement names.

mistakes.title: Waiting months to bill
mistakes.text: Expenses billed long after the project are harder to approve: budgets are closed and contacts have moved on. Bill them with the fee invoice or within the month.

mistakes.title: Personal costs mixed in
mistakes.text: A dinner with friends or an unapproved seat upgrade makes every other line suspect. Bill only what the contract covers.

pro_tip: Photograph each receipt when you get it and name the file with its future line number ("R3-taxi-oct15"). When you build the invoice, lines and receipt files already line up.
format_pdf_desc: A PDF sits next to the receipt copies in the client's approval workflow and keeps every amount exactly as the receipts show it.

faqs.question: Can I charge a client for expenses on an invoice?
faqs.answer: Yes, when your agreement says the client pays them. The contract should name which costs are billable, whether at cost or marked up, and whether large items need approval first.

faqs.question: Should expenses go on the same invoice as my fee?
faqs.answer: Either works. One invoice with an expenses section is simpler for small jobs. A separate one is better when expenses come from another budget or arrive later than the fee.

faqs.question: Do I have to attach receipts?
faqs.answer: Most clients ask, and some contracts require them above a set amount. Send numbered copies matching the lines, and keep the originals for your taxes.

faqs.question: Is it legal to mark up reimbursed expenses?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, if the client agreed. It's a contract question, and in VAT countries a marked-up cost can't be a disbursement. Without an agreed markup, bill the exact cost.

faqs.question: Do I charge VAT or sales tax on reimbursed expenses?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. In most VAT countries a rebilled cost gets VAT at your fee's rate; only true disbursements stay outside. In the US it depends on the state. Ask your accountant before the first expense invoice.

faqs.question: How do I invoice an expense paid in another currency?
faqs.answer: Convert it and say how; the card statement rate is the simplest proof. The free generator supports 38 currencies, so you can also bill in the client's currency if the contract says so.

title: Service Invoice Template (Free, PDF) | Invoicor
meta_description: Free service invoice template for any business that bills work, not goods. See a filled-in sample, then make your own PDF in the free generator.
h1: Free Service Invoice Template
subtitle: For any business that bills work rather than things sold: how to describe the service, date it, price it and set terms.
intro_paragraph: A service invoice bills for time, skill or a result, not a physical product. Nothing ships, so the words on the page are the client's only proof of what they're paying for. That makes the description the key field: what was done, when and for whom. This is the general document behind consultants, agencies, trainers, repair firms and any business that sells work. Selling items? Use the sales invoice. If your trade has its own template, the templates hub lists it.
what_to_include_intro: The legal basics are the same as any invoice. What changes is how you prove the work. These six fields do that.
req_1_text: Write the line the way the client would describe the job to their manager. "Quarterly staff workshop, Denver office, 14 attendees" gets approved. "Professional services" gets questioned.
req_2_title: The service date, separate from the invoice date
req_2_text: You often bill days after the work. Put the service date or date range in the line details and keep the invoice date as the day you issue it. Many tax authorities ask for the date of supply when the two differ.
req_3_title: The pricing basis on each line
req_3_text: Services are priced by the hour, by the visit or session, or as a flat fee for a defined scope. Show which one each line uses: "6 hours at $150" or "Flat fee: onboarding package". Mixing bases on one invoice is fine.
req_4_title: A reference the client gave you
req_4_text: Larger clients route invoices by purchase order number, project code or contact name. Ask for it before you bill and put it in the notes, or the invoice can sit in an accounts inbox with no owner.
req_5_title: Tax treatment of the service, stated
req_5_text: Whether a service is taxed depends on where you are and what the service is. Many US states tax few services; most VAT countries tax them by default. State the rate you applied, or say that no tax applies.
req_6_title: Payment terms with a real due date
req_6_text: Write the terms (for example net 15) and the due date itself, plus how to pay: bank details or your own payment link. The client can't return the work, so a clear due date is your main lever.
what_to_include_outro: Get these right and the invoice explains itself: the client approves it without calling you, and you have a dated record of what you delivered.
sample_breakdown_intro: A training company bills one month of work: a flat-fee workshop, two site visits and hourly coaching calls. Three lines, three pricing bases. The sample assumes a US state that doesn't tax these services, so there is no tax line. Tax rules vary: check yours.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Customer service workshop, half day, Denver office (Mar 4), flat fee
One-to-one coaching calls, team leads (Mar 5 to 28)

sample_breakdown_notes: Services delivered March 4 to 28. PO 4471-B, approved by the operations manager. No sales tax applies to these training services in the client's state. Payment due net 15 by bank transfer.

industry_notes.title: Services and goods are often taxed differently
industry_notes.text: US sales tax was built around goods, and each state decides which services it taxes. In the UK, the EU and most VAT countries, services are generally taxed, but where a service counts as supplied can depend on who and where the client is. Selling abroad? Check the place-of-supply rule first.

industry_notes.title: Mixed jobs need a decision
industry_notes.text: Some service jobs include parts. Supplies used up in the work usually stay part of the service; items sold alongside it may be taxed even if the labor isn't. The labor and materials invoice is built for that case. Invoicor uses one tax rate per invoice, so ask your accountant how to show a split.

industry_notes.title: Numbering doesn't change because the work repeats
industry_notes.text: Every invoice needs its own number, even for the same fee every month. In Invoicor you duplicate last month's invoice, change the dates and the service period, and it gets the next number. Never reuse a number with a new date.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes on service invoices

mistakes.title: Billing a label instead of the work
mistakes.text: "Consulting: $2,000" tells the person who approves invoices nothing if they weren't in the meetings. They hold the bill until someone explains it. One more sentence per line buys a faster approval.

mistakes.title: Leaving out when the service happened
mistakes.text: An invoice dated April 2 for February work looks like an error to the client and can put revenue in the wrong tax period for you. Put the service dates on the lines or in the notes.

mistakes.title: Charging tax because the last job had it
mistakes.text: Taxability follows the service, not your habit. A repair may be taxed where training isn't, even in one state. Check each service type once, write down the answer, and don't copy the rate from an old invoice.

pro_tip: Send the invoice the day the work ends, while the client still feels the value. A bill that arrives three weeks later competes with a fading memory of the work. For month-long jobs, bill at month end and name the period.
format_pdf_desc: A PDF keeps your descriptions and dates exactly as written, opens the same on any device, and files straight into the client's accounts system.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a service invoice and a sales invoice?
faqs.answer: A service invoice bills work: hours, visits, sessions or a project fee. A sales invoice bills goods: items with a SKU, a unit price and often shipping. A service invoice leans on descriptions and service dates; a sales invoice on quantities, delivery and returns.

faqs.question: How do I write an invoice for services rendered?
faqs.answer: List each service on its own line with what you did, when and for whom. Add the quantity and rate, then the subtotal, any tax and the total, followed by terms, a due date and how to pay. "Services rendered" works as a heading, not as a description.

faqs.question: Do I charge sales tax or VAT on services?
faqs.answer: It depends on your country, state and the service. Many US states tax only some services; most VAT countries tax services by default, with exceptions such as some health and education services. Check your tax authority's guidance and state the treatment on the invoice.

faqs.question: Should I bill hourly or a flat fee on a service invoice?
faqs.answer: Bill the way you agreed. Hourly suits open-ended work and shows the time behind the price; a flat fee suits a defined scope. If you mostly bill time, the hourly invoice template covers rates, rounding and timesheets.

faqs.question: What payment terms are usual for services?
faqs.answer: Due on receipt, net 15 and net 30 are the most common. One-off jobs often use due on receipt; business clients often ask for net 30. Always write the actual due date, not only the term.

title: Sales Invoice Template for Goods (Free PDF) | Invoicor
meta_description: Free sales invoice template for selling goods: SKUs, unit prices, shipping and sales tax or VAT. See a sample order, then make your PDF free.
h1: Free Sales Invoice Template for Goods
subtitle: For makers, resellers and wholesalers: how to list products, price shipping, apply sales tax or VAT and set returns terms.
intro_paragraph: A sales invoice bills for goods that leave your shelf and arrive at the buyer's door. It has to match the order line for line, so the buyer can check the box against the paper and book the stock. The weight is on quantities, unit prices, product codes and delivery. It isn't a receipt: an invoice asks for payment, a receipt confirms it. And it isn't a commercial invoice, which travels with goods across a border. This page covers the domestic sale of goods.
what_to_include_intro: Buyers read a sales invoice next to their purchase order and the packing slip. These six fields make that check quick.
req_1_title: Item name and SKU on every line
req_1_text: Give each product its name, variant and the SKU you use. "Soy candle, 8 oz, Cedar (CND-08)" can be matched to a shelf, a purchase order and a reorder. Save your products once and pick them per order.
req_2_title: Quantity and unit price, not just a line total
req_2_text: Show the units and the price per unit, then the amount. A buyer who got 22 candles instead of 24 needs the unit price to work out the credit. Name the unit if it isn't obvious: case of 12, kilogram.
req_3_title: Shipping and handling as their own line
req_3_text: Put delivery on a separate line instead of inside the prices. The buyer sees what the goods cost and what moving them cost, and since some US states tax delivery and others don't, the tax is easier to check.
req_4_title: Sales tax or VAT, at the rate that applies
req_4_text: Goods are taxed in most places, at a rate set by where the sale is taxed and what the product is. Show the rate and the amount. A buyer who resells may give you an exemption certificate: keep it and note it.
req_5_text: Write when the goods shipped and where they went, if that isn't the billing address. The delivery date often counts as the date of supply for tax, and the address settles which tax applies.
req_6_text: One line on returns protects both sides: how many days to report damage or missing items, whether returns are accepted, and who pays return shipping. Match what your price list already says.
what_to_include_outro: With these in place the invoice matches the order and the box, so the buyer pays without a reconciliation email.
sample_breakdown_intro: A candle maker bills a boutique hotel for four products it uses in its rooms, not for resale, plus one shipping line. The sample assumes a US state that taxes the goods and the delivery charge at a combined 7%. Many states treat shipping differently: check yours.
sample_breakdown_notes: Shipped October 14 to the hotel's receiving dock, 220 Pine St. PO HTL-0932. Report damaged or missing items within 7 days. Unopened items returnable within 30 days at the buyer's cost. Payment due net 30.

industry_notes.title: Where the sale is taxed
industry_notes.text: In the US, an order shipped to another state may be taxed where the buyer is, once your sales into that state pass its threshold. Each state sets and changes its own, so check its revenue department. In the EU, sales of goods to consumers in other member states have their own VAT rules.

industry_notes.title: Selling to a reseller
industry_notes.text: Many US states let a shop that resells your goods give you a resale certificate, so you charge no sales tax and keep the certificate on file. In VAT countries a registered business buyer usually pays the VAT and reclaims it, so you still charge it at home.

industry_notes.title: Corrections go on a new document
industry_notes.text: If a box arrives short or a price was wrong, don't edit the sent invoice. Issue a corrected invoice or credit that names the original number. In Invoicor a sent invoice is locked: duplicate it, correct the quantity or price on the copy, send it and mark the original cancelled. Where your country expects a credit note instead, check with your accountant.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes on sales invoices

mistakes.title: One line for the whole order
mistakes.text: "Candle order: $961" can't be checked against what arrived, or used to credit one broken item. List every product with its quantity and unit price.

mistakes.title: Forgetting tax on shipping, or charging it wrongly
mistakes.text: Shipping is a common sales tax slip. Some states tax delivery of taxable goods, others don't if it's billed separately. Decide once per state you ship to, and keep shipping on its own line.

mistakes.title: Sending an invoice when the buyer already paid
mistakes.text: A customer who paid at checkout needs a receipt, not a request for money. An invoice for a paid order confuses their books and invites double payment. Use invoices for orders paid later, such as trade accounts.

pro_tip: Print the invoice number on the packing slip in the box. When a buyer reports a missing item they quote the slip, you open the same invoice, and it takes one email instead of five.
format_pdf_desc: A PDF keeps SKUs, quantities and totals in fixed columns, prints cleanly next to a packing slip, and files without anything shifting.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a sales invoice and a receipt?
faqs.answer: A sales invoice asks for payment for goods, usually by a due date. A receipt confirms payment already made. Paid at the moment of sale: give a receipt. Bought on terms: send an invoice and mark it paid when the money arrives.

faqs.question: Is a sales invoice the same as a commercial invoice?
faqs.answer: No. A sales invoice bills a domestic sale. A commercial invoice travels with goods shipped abroad and adds what customs need, such as the HS code, origin and weights.

faqs.question: Do I have to show a SKU on a sales invoice?
faqs.answer: Usually not by law: a clear product name is the minimum in most places. But a SKU makes matching, reorders and returns faster, and business buyers expect it.

faqs.question: How do I add shipping to a sales invoice?
faqs.answer: Add it as its own line, like "Ground shipping, 3 boxes", and check whether delivery is taxed where you are. Invoicor applies one tax rate to the whole invoice, so if shipping is treated differently from the goods, ask your accountant how to show it.

faqs.question: What payment terms suit a sale of goods?
faqs.answer: Retail customers usually pay up front and get a receipt. Trade buyers often get net 30 once they have an account. For a new buyer's first order, many sellers ask for payment before shipping.

title: Commercial Invoice Template for Export (Free) | Invoicor
