meta_description: Free commercial invoice template for shipping goods abroad: HS codes, origin, weights and Incoterms per line. See a UK-to-US sample, make your PDF.
h1: Free Commercial Invoice Template for Export
subtitle: The invoice that travels with goods across a border: the fields customs and carriers read, and what still needs its own form.
intro_paragraph: A commercial invoice is the bill for an export sale, written so customs at the other end can understand the shipment. It names the seller, the buyer and whoever receives the goods, and gives each item's description, value, origin, weight and tariff code. Customs use it to classify the goods and set duties; carriers ask for it before they move an international parcel. Invoicor makes the invoice PDF, with the HS code and origin in each line's details. It doesn't file customs declarations or carrier forms, and the PDF's heading reads Invoice: write 'Commercial invoice' in the first line and the notes, and ask your carrier whether they need their own form or a heading that says Commercial Invoice.
what_to_include_intro: Customs and carriers look for the same core facts, and a missing one is a common reason a shipment is held.
req_1_text: List your business as the exporter, with any customs number you use, such as an EORI number in the UK and EU. Then the buyer who pays, and the consignee in the notes if the goods go elsewhere.
req_2_title: A precise description of each item
req_2_text: "Gifts" or "samples" won't get through. Say what each item is, what it's made of and what it's for: "Stoneware coffee mug, glazed, 350 ml, household use". Customs classify from this text.
req_3_title: HS code and country of origin per line
req_3_text: The HS code classifies the product for tariffs: six digits shared worldwide, often more digits nationally. Origin is where the goods were made, not where they shipped from. Write both in the line details.
req_4_title: Quantity, weight and value in a stated currency
req_4_text: Give units, unit value and line total in one currency named on the invoice, plus weight per line or per shipment and the number of packages. Customs check that the value fits the goods.
req_5_title: Incoterms and the reason for export
req_5_text: State the Incoterms rule you agreed, such as DAP or DDP with the named place: it shows who pays freight and import duties. Add the reason for export: sale, sample, repair or return.
req_6_text: Most carriers expect a short statement that the information is true and correct, with the signer's name and the date. Put it in the notes and sign the printed copy, or follow your carrier's instructions.
what_to_include_outro: These fields turn a normal invoice into one customs can work with. Check your carrier's list too: some want extra details or their own form as well.
sample_breakdown_intro: A homeware maker in England ships an order to a Boston shop under DAP Boston, priced in pounds. It assumes UK rules: exported goods are usually zero-rated for VAT with proof of export, so VAT is 0%. US duties are the buyer's under DAP. The HS codes are examples: check yours.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Stoneware coffee mug, glazed, 350 ml. HS 6912.00, origin UK, 0.4 kg each
Wool throw blanket, 130 x 180 cm. HS 6301.20, origin UK, 1.1 kg each
Paper notebook, A5, cloth cover. HS 4820.10, origin UK, 0.3 kg each
International freight to Boston, 4 cartons, 55 kg gross

sample_breakdown_notes: Incoterms 2020: DAP Boston, MA. Reason for export: sale. Consignee: Harbor Home Goods, Boston. I declare that the information on this invoice is true and correct. Signed: J. Price, Director, 12 November.

industry_notes.title: Incoterms decide who pays the duties
industry_notes.text: Incoterms are published by the International Chamber of Commerce; the current set is Incoterms 2020. Under DAP the buyer pays import duties and taxes; under DDP the seller does. Agree the rule before you quote, since DDP duties come out of your margin.

industry_notes.title: Classification is your responsibility
industry_notes.text: The exporter or importer answers for the HS code, not the carrier. Use the customs authority's tariff tool: the UK Trade Tariff on GOV.UK, or the US Harmonized Tariff Schedule from the US International Trade Commission. A wrong code can mean the wrong duty.

industry_notes.title: The invoice is one document among several
industry_notes.text: A shipment can also need an export declaration, a certificate of origin, a packing list or a carrier form. Invoicor makes the invoice; your carrier, forwarder or customs broker will tell you what else is needed.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes on commercial invoices

mistakes.title: Undervaluing to save the buyer duty
mistakes.text: Declaring less than the real price is a false declaration: customs can hold or seize the goods and fine the importer. Declare what the buyer pays. For a gift or sample, say so and give a realistic value.

mistakes.title: Confusing origin with where it shipped from
mistakes.text: A product made in Portugal and shipped from your UK warehouse has Portuguese origin. Origin can change the duty rate and trade-deal benefits, so check it per item.

mistakes.title: No currency, or a total in two currencies
mistakes.text: Customs convert your value into their own currency, so they need to know yours. Pick one for the whole invoice, name it, and keep every line and the freight in it.

pro_tip: Save each product with its HS code, origin and weight in its details. Every export order then starts with the customs data in place, and you only change quantities, buyer and date.
format_pdf_desc: Carriers and customs brokers ask for the commercial invoice as a PDF to attach to the shipment. It keeps codes and weights in place and prints cleanly for the outside of the box.

faqs.question: When do I need a commercial invoice?
faqs.answer: Whenever goods cross a customs border, including most courier parcels: for sales, and usually for samples, gifts and returns with the reason stated. Documents alone usually don't need one: check with your carrier.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a commercial invoice and a sales invoice?
faqs.answer: Both bill for goods. A commercial invoice adds what customs need: HS codes, origin, weights, Incoterms, the reason for export and a signed declaration. A domestic sale only needs a sales invoice.

faqs.question: Where do I put the HS code on the invoice?
faqs.answer: On each item's line, after the description or in the line details, with the country of origin. Each line item in the free generator has a details field for this.

faqs.question: Do I charge VAT on an export?
faqs.answer: In the UK and many VAT countries, exported goods are usually zero-rated if you keep evidence of export. Rules differ for consumer sales and within trade blocs, so check HMRC's export guidance or your own tax authority's.

faqs.question: Can Invoicor create the customs forms too?
faqs.answer: No. Invoicor makes the invoice PDF with the customs details you add per line. Declarations, certificates of origin and carrier forms come from your carrier, forwarder, broker or the customs authority.

title: Invoice Without VAT Template (Free PDF) | Invoicor
meta_description: Free invoice without VAT template for sellers not VAT registered or below the threshold. See a UK sample with the right note, then make your PDF.
h1: Free Invoice Without VAT Template
subtitle: For sole traders and small businesses that don't charge VAT: what the invoice must show, what to write, and what changes when you register.
intro_paragraph: An invoice without VAT is a normal invoice from a seller who doesn't charge VAT, usually because they aren't registered. That's common for new sole traders, side businesses and small firms below their country's threshold. It still needs a number, dates, both parties' details and a clear description. What it must not do is look like a VAT invoice: no VAT line, no VAT number. A note saying why is good practice, and required in some countries. The main example is the UK, with notes on Australia and EU schemes.
what_to_include_intro: Leaving VAT off is easy. Making the invoice complete for a client who expects a VAT line takes these six points.
req_1_title: The usual invoice details, in full
req_1_text: GOV.UK's invoicing guidance (checked November 2026) lists the basics for any UK invoice: a unique number, your and the client's names and addresses, a description, the supply date, the invoice date, the amount and the total owed.
req_2_title: No VAT line and no VAT number
req_2_text: If you aren't registered you can't charge VAT and have no VAT number to show. Leave the tax rate at 0: Invoicor's PDF then shows a tax line of 0%, with no VAT charged, so the note below is what tells the client why. A "VAT 0%" line suggests you're registered and zero-rating the sale.
req_3_text: Add a line such as "Not registered for VAT. No VAT has been charged." In the UK that's good practice, not fixed wording. Some EU countries require a note: in Germany, a reference to the exemption under §19 UStG.
req_4_title: Prices that are the final price
req_4_text: Your rate is what the client pays. Don't show a figure "plus VAT" or a gross and net split you don't charge. If you quoted the client a price before, the invoice total should match it exactly.
req_5_title: A company or registration number where it applies
req_5_text: A limited company usually shows its registered number and registered office whatever its VAT status. The free generator has a registration number field, separate from the tax ID.
req_6_title: Payment details that are easy to use
req_6_text: Give your bank name and account details or IBAN, and a due date. Ask the client to use the invoice number as the payment reference.
what_to_include_outro: The client sees at once that no VAT is due and why, and your records show you didn't collect tax you couldn't charge.
sample_breakdown_intro: A UK sole trader who isn't VAT registered bills a small business for a website copy refresh. The sample assumes UK rules, in pounds, with no tax line and a note saying why. Rules differ by country and change: check HMRC or your own tax authority.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Website copy rewrite, 5 pages (home, about, 3 services)
Call to agree the brief and final review

sample_breakdown_notes: Not registered for VAT. No VAT has been charged. Work supplied 3 to 21 November. Payment due within 14 days by bank transfer; please use the invoice number as the reference.

industry_notes.title: Your client can't reclaim VAT that isn't there
industry_notes.text: A registered client reclaims VAT only from a valid VAT invoice. Yours has none, so there's nothing to reclaim and nothing to add. For a client who can't reclaim VAT anyway, such as a private person, your price simply looks lower.

industry_notes.title: Crossing the threshold changes the invoice
industry_notes.text: Most VAT countries require you to register once taxable turnover passes a threshold that each government sets and changes. HMRC publishes the current UK figure. From your effective date you charge VAT, show your VAT number and issue VAT invoices.

industry_notes.title: Australia and EU small-business schemes
industry_notes.text: In Australia, a business not registered for GST can't issue a tax invoice or include GST; it issues an ordinary invoice (see the ATO's guidance). Many EU countries exempt sellers below a turnover limit, such as Germany's Kleinunternehmer rule in §19 UStG, each with its own conditions and wording: check your tax authority.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes on invoices without VAT

mistakes.title: Charging VAT before you're registered
mistakes.text: Adding 20% to look established isn't allowed before you're registered, and you'd owe what you collected. If it already happened, ask HMRC or an accountant how to correct it.

mistakes.title: A 0% line without a note
mistakes.text: Invoicor always prints the tax line, so an invoice without VAT shows "Tax (0%)". On its own that can read as a registered business zero-rating the sale, which is a different status. The note "Not registered for VAT" right below the lines makes your status clear.

mistakes.title: Missing the moment you must register
mistakes.text: Sellers often keep issuing no-VAT invoices months after they should have registered, and the tax can then come out of their own pocket. Keep a running turnover total so you see the threshold coming.

pro_tip: Keep one finished invoice with the no-VAT note, your bank details and terms, and duplicate it for each new client. Nothing to retype, and no stray tax rate from another invoice.
format_pdf_desc: A PDF shows the exact total with your note in place, can't be edited to add a VAT line later, and is easy to keep with your records.

faqs.question: Can I issue an invoice if I'm not VAT registered?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every business should invoice its clients. Not being registered just means no VAT on the invoice; it still needs a number, dates, both parties' details, a description and the total.

faqs.question: What do I write on an invoice when I'm not VAT registered?
faqs.answer: In the UK, "Not registered for VAT. No VAT has been charged." works well. Some countries require set wording: in Germany, sellers under the small-business rule refer to §19 UStG. Check your tax authority.

faqs.question: Do I need a VAT number on my invoice?
faqs.answer: Only if you're registered for VAT. A company registration number is different: limited companies usually show it whatever their VAT status.

faqs.question: Is an invoice without VAT the same as a VAT-exempt invoice?
faqs.answer: Not quite. An unregistered seller charges no VAT on anything. A registered seller can also make exempt supplies, such as some health or financial services, and states the exemption on that invoice. Check which applies to you.

faqs.question: What happens to invoices I issued before registering?
faqs.answer: They stay without VAT. From your effective registration date, new invoices carry VAT. If registration is backdated, HMRC's guidance explains how to account for sales in that period, or ask an accountant.

title: Freelance Invoice Template (Free PDF) | Invoicor
meta_description: Free freelance invoice template with a filled-in sample. Add what your client's accounts team needs to pay you, then download a clean PDF.
h1: Free Freelance Invoice Template
subtitle: One invoice for freelancers in any field, self-employed or sole trader: what a client's accounts team checks before it pays, plus a sample to edit.
intro_paragraph: A freelance invoice is usually read by two people. The person who hired you knows the work. The person who pays you, often someone in accounts payable, only knows what's on the page. If your legal name, the PO number or your bank details are missing, the invoice goes back in the queue. This template is built for that second reader, in any field and any country. UK sole traders and the self-employed send the same document. US independent contractors have extra tax paperwork, covered on its own page.
what_to_include_intro: Clients with an accounts team process invoices against a checklist. Match it the first time and you get paid on the terms you agreed.
req_1_title: Your legal name, not only your trading name
req_1_text: Accounts teams pay the supplier set up in their system. If you trade as 'North Studio' but the bank account is in your own name, show both: 'Jane Smith, trading as North Studio'. A name that doesn't match the account holder can get a payment held for checks.
req_2_title: Your tax ID where the client needs it
req_2_text: Many clients need a tax or registration number before they can pay a new supplier: a VAT number in the EU, a UTR or VAT number in the UK, an ABN in Australia. Put it under your address. If you aren't registered for anything, leave the field empty.
req_3_title: The client's PO or reference number
req_3_text: Larger companies match each invoice to a purchase order or cost-center code. Ask for it when you agree the work and copy it exactly. Without it, the invoice can sit in a shared inbox while someone works out whose budget it is.
req_4_title: Lines that match how you priced the job
req_4_text: A project fee is one line with the agreed scope in the details. Hours or days beyond that scope get their own lines with quantity and rate. Then the client can approve the fee straight away and query only the extra.
req_5_title: Usage rights when you sell creative work
req_5_text: If you license writing, images, music or code, say what the client gets and when: 'Full usage rights transfer on payment in full' or 'Licensed for web use for 12 months'. A written term beats a vague expectation, and it's one more reason to pay on time.
req_6_title: VAT, or a clear no-VAT note
req_6_text: If you're registered for VAT or GST, show your number, the rate and the tax amount. If you aren't, add a line such as 'Not registered for VAT'. For a business client abroad, reverse-charge wording may apply. Check your tax office's rules for where you and the client are based.
what_to_include_outro: With these six details, someone who has never met you can approve the invoice.
sample_breakdown_intro: A project fee plus two hours of extra work the client asked for after sign-off. The sample assumes a freelancer who isn't registered for VAT or sales tax, so there's no tax line. Tax rules vary by country: check yours.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Project fee: launch content package, per proposal dated Oct 6
Extra revisions requested Oct 28 (beyond the two rounds in scope)

sample_breakdown_notes: PO 4500-1187. Payment due within 14 days by bank transfer to the account above; please quote invoice FR-2026-031. Not registered for VAT. Full usage rights to the delivered content transfer on payment in full.

industry_notes.title: Self-employed, sole trader, freelancer: same document
industry_notes.text: The label changes by country, the invoice doesn't. A UK sole trader, a US self-employed consultant and an EU freelancer all show who they are, who the client is, a unique number, the date, what was supplied, the amount and any tax. Some countries require extra fields, so check your local list once.

industry_notes.title: Number invoices in one unbroken series
industry_notes.text: Use one sequence across all clients, such as FR-2026-001 and FR-2026-002, not a fresh '001' per client. Tax offices in many countries expect invoice numbers to be unique and in order.

industry_notes.title: Payment terms come from the contract
industry_notes.text: If your proposal says 14 days, the invoice says 14 days. If you signed the client's supplier agreement, its longer terms may apply instead, so read it before you print 'due on receipt'.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes freelancers make on invoices

mistakes.title: Sending it to the wrong person
mistakes.text: Your contact approves the work but may not pay it. Ask where invoices go, often a shared accounts payable address, and copy your contact.

mistakes.title: Bundling extra work into the fee
mistakes.text: Raising the project fee to cover extra hours hides the change, and the client stops to ask why the number differs from the proposal. Keep the agreed fee and add the extra time on its own dated line.

mistakes.title: Bank details that don't work across borders
mistakes.text: A domestic account number alone often can't be paid from abroad. For international clients, add your IBAN, SWIFT (BIC) and bank name, and invoice in the currency your contract names.

pro_tip: When you agree a new job, ask: 'What do you need on the invoice for it to be paid first time?' The answer might be a PO number, a project code or a supplier form. In the Invoicor app, write it in the client's notes so you see it each time, and put it in every invoice's notes; duplicating their last invoice copies it.
format_pdf_desc: Accounts teams file and forward invoices as PDFs. A PDF keeps your layout, can't be edited by mistake on its way, and opens anywhere.

faqs.question: What should a freelance invoice include?
faqs.answer: Your name and address, the client's name and address, a unique invoice number, the issue and due dates, the work with quantities and rates, the total, and how to pay. Add your tax ID and the tax if you're registered, and the client's PO number if they gave one.

faqs.question: Do I need to charge VAT or sales tax as a freelancer?
faqs.answer: Only if you're registered or required to be. In the UK and EU that depends on your turnover and the work; in the US, on the state and the service. If you aren't registered, don't add tax, and say so. Thresholds change, so check the current figure with your tax office.

faqs.question: How do I invoice a client in another country?
faqs.answer: Invoice in the currency the contract names, add your IBAN and SWIFT, and include the client's tax ID if they're a business. Within the EU, business-to-business services usually fall under the reverse charge, which needs its own wording. The free generator has 38 currencies and 11 invoice languages.

faqs.question: Is a self-employed invoice different from a freelance invoice?
faqs.answer: No. Self-employed, sole trader and freelancer describe the same set-up: you are the business. What changes by country is which tax details you must show.

faqs.question: When should I send a freelance invoice?
faqs.answer: When the contract says: on delivery, at a milestone or at month-end. For long projects, agree a deposit or milestone invoices up front rather than one large bill at the end.

title: Independent Contractor Invoice Template (Free) | Invoicor
meta_description: Free independent contractor invoice template for US contractors. Bill as a business, not an employee, and download a PDF your client can file.
h1: Free Independent Contractor Invoice Template
subtitle: For US independent contractors who bill clients directly: an invoice that reads like a bill from a business, matching the client's records and tax forms.
intro_paragraph: When a US company pays you as an independent contractor, it doesn't run payroll for you. No tax is withheld, no benefits are added, and at year-end the client may report what it paid you to the IRS. Your invoice is part of the record behind that arrangement. It should read like a bill from one business to another: your name or business name, your own invoice number, work described by result or by hour, and no employee-style lines. If you freelance outside the US, the general freelance invoice is the better fit.
what_to_include_intro: The client will match your invoice to the W-9 it keeps on file and, later, to its year-end filings. These fields keep them consistent.
req_1_title: The name that matches your W-9
req_1_text: Invoice under the legal name or business name on the W-9 you gave the client. If your W-9 shows an LLC, invoice as the LLC. When the invoice and the tax form name different payees, payment can stall.
req_2_title: Your own invoice number and dates
req_2_text: Employees get paystubs; businesses send numbered invoices. Use your own sequence (IC-2026-011), an issue date and a due date. It shows you set your own billing.
req_3_title: Work described as a service, not a job title
req_3_text: 'Project management support, November: 64 hours' describes a service. 'Salary, November' describes a job. Name deliverables or hours worked, not a position.
req_4_title: No tax withheld, and no payroll lines
req_4_text: The invoice asks for the full amount. Don't deduct income tax, Social Security or Medicare: as a contractor you handle your own taxes, often through estimated payments. Leave out overtime, PTO and benefit lines. Ask a tax professional how this applies to you.
req_5_title: Expenses billed only if the contract says so
req_5_text: Contractors usually cover their own tools and costs. If the contract lets you pass some on, such as a software seat used only for this client, list each on its own line and keep the receipt.
req_6_text: Put the agreement's name or date on the invoice: 'Per consulting agreement dated Jan 12, 2026'. It ties the invoice to the terms you signed and helps the client's records show a business relationship rather than employment.
what_to_include_outro: No single line decides your status: the IRS looks at the whole relationship. But an invoice that matches your contract and W-9 is one less thing to explain.
sample_breakdown_intro: A month of hourly contract work, a fixed monthly report and one expense the contract allows. No income tax is withheld. No sales tax is shown: many states don't tax this service, but rules vary by state, so check yours.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Project management support, Nov 2 to Nov 27 (hours per timesheet)
Monthly status report and review call
Reimbursable per contract: project software seat, November

sample_breakdown_notes: Services under the independent contractor agreement dated Jan 12, 2026. No taxes withheld. W-9 on file with the client. Software seat receipt available on request. Net 15, by bank transfer.
industry_notes_title: Independent contractor invoice rules worth knowing

industry_notes.title: The W-9 comes first
industry_notes.text: Many US clients ask a new contractor for Form W-9 before the first payment. It gives them your legal name, address and taxpayer ID, either your SSN or an EIN. Send it once and update it when something changes.

industry_notes.title: The 1099-NEC is the client's form
industry_notes.text: If a business pays you at or above the IRS reporting threshold in a year, it files Form 1099-NEC and sends you a copy. The threshold is set by law and has changed, so check the IRS page on Form 1099-NEC for your year. Your invoices let you check the total on the form.

industry_notes.title: The invoice doesn't make you a contractor
industry_notes.text: Your status depends on the working relationship: who controls how the work is done, who pays the costs, whether you work for others too. The IRS explains these rules on its website, and some states apply stricter tests. An invoice supports the arrangement but can't fix a role that works like a job.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes independent contractors make on invoices

mistakes.title: Putting your SSN on the invoice
mistakes.text: Invoices get emailed, forwarded and saved in shared folders. Your Social Security number doesn't belong there: the client already has it on your W-9. Use an EIN if you want a tax number on the page.

mistakes.title: Billing like a paycheck
mistakes.text: The same amount every two weeks labeled 'pay period' looks like wages. Bill for the work: hours at a rate, a named monthly retainer or a project fee.

mistakes.title: Losing track of what you billed
mistakes.text: At year-end you'll compare your records with any 1099-NEC you receive. Keep every invoice in one place and mark each one paid when the money arrives, so the year's total is easy to add up.

pro_tip: Send your W-9 with your first invoice, before anyone asks. Payments to new contractors often wait until a W-9 is on file, and sending it early saves a round of emails with the client's accounts team.
format_pdf_desc: Clients keep contractor invoices with their tax records. A PDF holds its layout, can't be changed by accident after you send it, and files cleanly next to your W-9.

faqs.question: What is a 1099 invoice?
faqs.answer: An informal name for an invoice from an independent contractor, after Form 1099-NEC, which the client may file to report what it paid you. There's no special format: use a normal business invoice with no tax withheld.

faqs.question: Do I need to send a W-9 with every invoice?
faqs.answer: No. The client usually asks for a W-9 once, before the first payment, and keeps it on file. Send a new one if your name, business type, address or tax ID changes.

faqs.question: Should an independent contractor invoice show taxes?
faqs.answer: Not income tax: nothing is withheld. Sales tax is separate. Many professional services aren't taxed, but some states tax certain services, so check your state's revenue department.

faqs.question: Can I use an EIN instead of my SSN?
faqs.answer: Yes. Sole proprietors can get an EIN from the IRS at no cost and put it on the W-9 instead of their Social Security number, which keeps the SSN off business paperwork.

faqs.question: How often should I invoice as an independent contractor?
faqs.answer: As your contract says: hourly work often weekly, every two weeks or monthly; project work at milestones or on delivery. In the Invoicor app you can duplicate last month's invoice and change the dates and hours.

faqs.question: What if a client treats me like an employee?
faqs.answer: That's about the working relationship, not the invoice. The IRS describes the factors on its page about independent contractors and employees, and you can ask the IRS for a determination. Talk to a tax professional if you're unsure.

title: Subcontractor Invoice Template (Free PDF) | Invoicor
meta_description: Free subcontractor invoice template. Bill the main contractor with the PO, percent complete, retainage and change orders, then download a PDF.
h1: Free Subcontractor Invoice Template
subtitle: For subs who bill the general contractor, not the owner: contract numbers, percent complete, retainage and change orders the GC can approve.
intro_paragraph: A subcontractor invoice travels up the chain. You bill the general contractor, the GC folds your numbers into its own pay application to the owner, and the owner's payment flows back down to you. Each step checks your invoice against the subcontract. So a sub invoice looks different from a bill to a homeowner: it names the project and the GC's contract or PO number, shows how much of your scope is done, holds back retainage and lists approved change orders by number. Miss one and it waits for the next billing cycle.
what_to_include_intro: GCs often collect sub invoices by a fixed monthly cutoff. These six items are what their project manager checks first.
req_1_title: Project name, address and the GC's numbers
req_1_text: Show the project name and site address, the GC's subcontract or PO number and their job number if they use one. A GC running several jobs sorts invoices by these references, and one it can't match waits.
req_2_text: For a fixed-price subcontract, bill by progress: the contract value, the percentage complete to date and the amount earned to date. The GC compares your percentage with what its superintendent saw on site, so keep it realistic.
req_3_title: Previously billed, as its own line
req_3_text: Subtract what earlier invoices claimed on a negative line that names them ('Less invoice SUB-0412'). This invoice then asks only for this period's work, and the GC can check the running total without rebuilding your math.
req_4_text: Many subcontracts let the GC hold back a share of each payment, often 5% or 10%, until the work is accepted. Show it as a deduction and keep a running total, because you'll invoice it separately at the end.
req_5_text: Approved extra work goes on its own line with the change order number and date: 'CO-03, six added circuits, approved Oct 9'. Never fold it into the base contract line, and get unapproved changes signed before you bill them.
req_6_text: Put your license number in the notes if your state requires it. Many GCs want a current certificate of insurance and, in many states, a conditional lien waiver with each payment request. Lien waiver rules vary by state: check yours.
what_to_include_outro: A sub invoice that answers the GC's questions before they're asked gets added to the owner's pay application without edits.
sample_breakdown_intro: The second invoice on an $18,000 electrical subcontract, now 40% complete after a first invoice for 20%, with one approved change order and 10% retainage held. The sample assumes labor-only work with no sales tax; construction tax rules vary by state, so check yours.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Electrical rough-in, subcontract SC-2214: 40% of $18,000 complete to date
Change order CO-03: six added circuits, approved Oct 9 (100% complete)

sample_breakdown_notes: Riverside Medical Office, 410 Harbor Rd. GC PO 7781. Retainage held to date: $855.00 ($360.00 on SUB-0412 plus $495.00 here). Net 30 per subcontract. Conditional lien waiver for this amount enclosed. License #EC-XXXXX.

industry_notes.title: Pay-when-paid and pay-if-paid clauses
industry_notes.text: Many subcontracts tie your payment to the GC being paid by the owner. Some US states limit these clauses or won't enforce them, especially pay-if-paid. Your invoice can't change the clause, but it can make sure the delay isn't your paperwork.

industry_notes.title: UK: CIS deductions
industry_notes.text: Under HMRC's Construction Industry Scheme, the contractor deducts tax from a subcontractor's payments, pays it to HMRC and gives the sub a statement of deductions. It applies to labor, not materials, so show them on separate lines. HMRC sets the rate by registration status: check its CIS guidance for current rates. Many UK construction services also fall under the VAT domestic reverse charge (HMRC guidance again).

industry_notes.title: Retainage comes back on its own invoice
industry_notes.text: Once your scope is accepted, invoice the retainage as a separate document listing each amount withheld. Some states cap retainage or set release deadlines on certain projects, so check your state's rule and your subcontract.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes subcontractors make on invoices

mistakes.title: Billing the owner instead of the GC
mistakes.text: Your contract is with the general contractor. Unless the subcontract says otherwise, the invoice goes to the GC's legal name and billing address, not to the property owner.

mistakes.title: Missing the monthly cutoff
mistakes.text: If the GC compiles its pay application on the 25th and your invoice arrives on the 27th, your work waits a month. Ask for the cutoff at the start of the job and send yours before it.

mistakes.title: Percent complete that runs ahead of the site
mistakes.text: Billing 60% when the superintendent sees 40% gets the line cut back or the invoice returned, and it weakens your position in any later dispute. Bill what's in place.

pro_tip: Keep a one-page ledger per subcontract: contract value, change orders, each invoice's percent and retainage held. Each new invoice is then the last one with three numbers updated. In the Invoicor app, line prices can't be negative, so duplicate the previous invoice, bill this period's amount as the line and show the percent, earlier invoices and retainage in the notes. The free generator takes negative lines, as in the sample.
format_pdf_desc: GCs attach sub invoices to their own pay applications. A PDF keeps your numbers fixed, prints cleanly for the project file and can't be altered once it's part of the owner's billing.

faqs.question: What's the difference between a subcontractor invoice and a contractor invoice?
faqs.answer: Who it goes to. A contractor bills the owner. A subcontractor bills the contractor who hired it, using that contractor's contract or PO number, and its amounts become part of the contractor's bill to the owner.

faqs.question: How do I show retainage on a subcontractor invoice?
faqs.answer: Bill the amount earned this period, then deduct your subcontract's retainage percentage as its own line, with the total held to date in the notes. Release it later with a separate retainage invoice.

faqs.question: Should change orders go on the same invoice?
faqs.answer: Approved ones can, each on its own line with its number and approval date, so the GC can match each to its signed change order.

faqs.question: Do I need to send a lien waiver with my invoice?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. Many GCs want a conditional lien waiver with each payment request and an unconditional one once payment clears. Some states require their own statutory forms, so check yours.

faqs.question: How does CIS affect a UK subcontractor invoice?
faqs.answer: The contractor deducts CIS tax from the labor part of your payment and sends it to HMRC. Show labor and materials on separate lines so the deduction is easy to work out. HMRC's CIS guidance has the current rates.

faqs.question: Can Invoicor fill in my GC's pay application form?
faqs.answer: No. Invoicor makes invoices, not pay application forms with a schedule of values. Many subs bill on a plain invoice like the sample. If your GC requires its own form, fill that in and keep the invoice for your records.

title: Past Due Invoice Template (Free PDF) | Invoicor
meta_description: Free past due invoice template. Re-send an unpaid invoice with its original number, PAST DUE, the days overdue and a late fee only where allowed.
h1: Free Past Due Invoice Template
subtitle: How to re-send an invoice that wasn't paid on time: the same number, marked PAST DUE, with the days overdue and any late fee your terms allow.
intro_paragraph: A past due invoice isn't a new bill. It's the invoice you already sent, sent again after its due date, marked so nobody mistakes it for a second charge. It keeps the original number, issue date and due date, then adds a clear PAST DUE label and how many days late it is. If your contract or the law allows a late fee, it shows that too. The aim is to make paying now the easiest thing to do. This page is about the document itself, not follow-up emails or collections.
what_to_include_intro: Most late invoices are lost, stuck in an approval or forgotten rather than disputed. A past due invoice should remove every reason to wait.
req_1_text: Re-use the original number. A new number makes the client's accounts team think it's a new charge, so it may be paid twice or not at all. A late fee billed separately gets its own number and names the original.
req_2_text: Put 'PAST DUE' where it can't be missed: in the notes, the first line or your email's subject. Many accounts teams handle overdue items faster, but only if they can see that this is one.
req_3_text: Show the issue and due dates exactly as they were, then the days overdue as of today: 'Due Oct 15, 2026. 30 days past due on Nov 14.' The client can check it without digging out the original email.
req_4_title: A late fee only if you agreed one
req_4_text: You can usually charge a late fee only if the contract, your accepted terms or the law provides for it, and some places cap the rate. If your original terms said '1.5% per month on overdue balances', apply it. If they didn't, don't add one now: a surprise fee invites a dispute.
req_5_text: Restate the balance. If the client paid part of it, show the payment received as a negative line (in the free generator) or in the notes (in the app, where prices can't be negative), so the remaining amount is clear.
req_6_text: Repeat your bank details or payment link in full. The original email may be buried, and whoever handles overdue items may never have seen it.
what_to_include_outro: Keep the tone neutral. The facts on the page, a number, a date and an amount, do the persuading.
sample_breakdown_intro: Invoice INV-1042 for $3,450, issued Sep 15 and due Oct 15, re-sent 30 days late with the 1.5% monthly late fee its original terms allowed. The sample assumes services with no sales tax; tax rules vary, so check yours.

sample_breakdown_rows.description: Consulting services, September (per agreement dated Aug 4)
Late fee: 1.5% of $3,450.00, 30 days overdue (per original terms)

sample_breakdown_notes: PAST DUE: 30 days. Invoice INV-1042, issued Sep 15, 2026, was due Oct 15, 2026. Late fee of 1.5% per month applied under the original terms. If you've already paid, please reply with the payment date. Payment by bank transfer to the account above.
industry_notes_title: Past due invoice rules worth knowing

industry_notes.title: Re-send or re-issue
industry_notes.text: Where your records allow edits, you can re-issue the same number with PAST DUE and a late fee line, as in the sample. In the Invoicor app a sent invoice is locked: share the same PDF again and bill any late fee on a new invoice that names the original.

industry_notes.title: Late fees and interest have limits
industry_notes.text: Many US states cap late fees or interest, and consumer contracts face stricter rules. In the UK, the Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998 gives businesses a right to statutory interest on late business-to-business payments, and EU countries have similar rules. Check yours before you add a number.

industry_notes.title: Mark it overdue in your records
industry_notes.text: In the Invoicor app an invoice can carry the overdue status. The app doesn't send reminders, so set a day each week to look at overdue invoices and re-share them yourself.

mistakes_title: Three mistakes on past due invoices

mistakes.title: Giving it a new number
mistakes.text: A new number on the same work looks like a second bill. The client may pay both and ask for a refund, or pay neither while they sort it out.

mistakes.title: Adding a fee nobody agreed to
mistakes.text: A late fee that wasn't in the contract or original terms is hard to enforce, and the argument over it can hold up the main amount. Put late fees in your terms before the next job starts.

mistakes.title: Waiting too long to re-send
mistakes.text: Two weeks late needs a nudge; four months late is a collections problem. Re-send soon after the due date and again at regular intervals, each time with the updated days overdue.

pro_tip: Before you re-send, ask your contact one short question: 'Is anything stopping this invoice from being paid?' A missing PO number or a wrong billing address is often the answer. Fixing that gets you paid faster than a firmer tone.
format_pdf_desc: A past due invoice may land in front of a manager, a bookkeeper or a collections agency. A PDF keeps the original dates and amounts exactly as sent.

faqs.question: What should I write on a past due invoice?
faqs.answer: The original number, issue date and due date, PAST DUE, the days overdue, the balance owed, any late fee your terms allow, and how to pay. A short note helps: 'This invoice was due on Oct 15 and is now 30 days past due. Please pay the balance of $3,501.75 by Nov 21, or let us know if something is wrong with it.'

faqs.question: Should a past due invoice get a new invoice number?
faqs.answer: No. Keep the original so the client matches it to the bill they already have. Only a separate late fee invoice gets a new number.

faqs.question: Can I charge a late fee on an overdue invoice?
faqs.answer: Usually only if your contract or original terms said so, or a law gives you the right, such as statutory interest on UK business debts. Many US states cap fees and interest, so check your rule first.

faqs.question: When does an invoice become past due?
faqs.answer: The day after its due date. Many businesses wait a few days, since a payment may be on its way, then re-send every week or two until it's paid.

faqs.question: Does Invoicor send overdue reminders?
faqs.answer: No. Invoicor gives each invoice a status, including overdue, but it doesn't send reminders or track whether the client opened your email. You re-share the PDF yourself.

faqs.question: What's the difference between a past due invoice and a payment reminder?
faqs.answer: A reminder is a letter or email about an invoice. A past due invoice is the invoice itself, re-sent with PAST DUE and the days overdue. Many people send both: a short email with the past due invoice attached.
